# MeetingPipe Q6 archive (running)

> Running archive of Q6 items that reached done-done. Since the 2026-07-10 process change, a completed item moves here (its ToC row plus its Task-spec text) in the same commit that ships it, instead of sitting `done` in the active ToC until the quarter roll; the active backlog is [`meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md`](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md). This file freezes at the quarter roll, like [`q5-final.md`](./q5-final.md). Items moved here before the process change landed as a batch on 2026-07-10.

| VALID1 | On-device acceptance measurements | Validation | done | P1 | Closed 2026-07-16 after three quarters, all five bars settled. **DIAR1 DER = 8.99%** (3 meetings reviewed end to end; bimodal 0.3/13.6/49.0, and the 49% outlier is the real defect, now DIAR2), **DIAR1 latency PASS** (132 runs / 47.7 h, worst 5.3x real time), **UX4 PASS** (owner forced a capture-TCC failure), **A15 baseline set** (cold 39.8 s / warm 31.4 s / 8.4 s load, 7B), attribution baselined (3.2% unattributed post-roster); A16 + SUM1-APPLE quality already closed in Q5. | MIC10 | Re-lock the Teams mini-window mute control + VAD-contradiction staleness | Detection | done | P1 | Shipped 2026-07-14. The stale mute button was never the hub/pre-join window every earlier writeup blamed: a live AX dump proved it is the **backgrounded full meeting window of the same call**, which freezes its mute description when the call pops out into the floating compact panel and then reads `muted` forever. Both windows carry a `Leave` button, which is why the Leave anchor could never discriminate. Now anchored on the panel's `AXSystemDialog` subrole (locale-independent), so the frozen button is never read; plus a unanimity fusion (a cross-window disagreement reads blind under capture-first instead of letting the stale one win) and part 2's VAD-contradiction discredit as backstops. |
| MIC6 | Attribute-based (futureproof) native mute read | Detection | wont-do | P1 | Closed 2026-07-14 as unachievable, not unbuilt. Four of five parts had shipped; the fifth (read the mute button's stable state attribute instead of the localized title) was gated on a live AX dump, and the dump refuted it: **Teams exposes no `AXValue` and no `AXIdentifier` on any element in its entire tree.** The localized `AXDescription` is the only mute signal Microsoft offers, so the shipped `MuteLabels` catalogue + cross-locale fallback is the answer, not a stopgap. Both of MIC6's goals are met anyway: locale by that fallback, UI-redesign durability by MIC10's `AXSystemDialog` anchor (a structural signal, which is the durable thing MIC6 was hunting). Teams is the only native client the daemon has ever built AX handles for (386/386 in the whole event log), so the unmeasured Zoom/Webex leg is hypothetical; re-open with the same dump if either ever becomes a real client. |
| END6 | Device-idle end corroborator | Detection | done | P1 | Closed 2026-07-14. The correlated-pair gate (the load-bearing half) shipped earlier and is now **validated in production**: same-pid restart within 3 min of an end fell from 12/82 native ends (15%, incl. the 4-fragment screen-share incident) pre-gate to zero real chops post-gate. The remaining `kAudioDevicePropertyDeviceIsRunningSomewhere` leg is **refuted by measurement, not deferred**: a new probe (`daemon/scripts/end6-device-idle-probe.swift`) shows our own capture pins the default input **and** the default output RUNNING for the whole recording (`AVAudioEngine.inputNode` builds a `CADefaultDeviceAggregate` spanning both directions), so no device can read idle while we record and the signal is structurally blind, in either direction. It would not have helped anyway (post-gate the AX re-walk confirms native ends at a **median 0.17 s**, with zero backstop auto-stops) and would have hurt (a device-global cross-class signal instant-promotes a provisional end, re-opening the fragmentation hole the gate closed). The unconfounded read is the per-process one: DET2 owns it. Writeup: `docs/spikes/end6-device-idle-corroborator.md`. |

| AI5 | Spike: meeting-type classification | Intelligence | done | P3 | Resolved 2026-07-23 **NO-GO**, measured. The 2026-07-11 prototype could not be judged (2 test meetings); the library has since filled to 193, so both legs ran for real (the `--llm` leg forced onto the local backend, since the owner's config is `anthropic` and the question is about on-device labels). Two independent labellers over the same 10-type taxonomy agree on **1 of 10 types** (`standup`, 94% Jaccard) and have **zero overlap on 4** (`client`, `brainstorm`, `retro`, `interview`); overall agreement 45.6%. Root cause is the input, not the classifier: `summary["title"]` is the *summarizer's invented* title, not the calendar's, the workflow tag has 3 distinct values library-wide, and `attendees` is diarization-derived (31 meetings report 1 attendee). The local LLM does not abstain, it relabels the garbage bucket (`other` 36% to 7% by moving 36 meetings into `one_on_one`, which it assigns 48 times but on only 5 of the 13 genuinely-2-person meetings). One real defect found and fixed: the `\bsync\b` to `one_on_one` rule produced 22 of 33 one_on_one labels with 20 of them at 4-12 attendees; removing it moves agreement only 45.6% to 47.7%, which is the proof that the taxonomy, not the regex, is the problem. No schema change landed (acceptance honored). Harness kept; verdict + revisit gate (a real calendar title, blocked by CAL1) in `docs/spikes/ai5-meeting-type-classification.md`. Unblocks AI9. |

| UX47 | Prep card wraps its lines, admits its scroll, and stays inside its panel | UX | done | P2 | **Shipped 2026-07-30, same day as filed: 1886 daemon tests green (4 new), truth fences green.** The document is constraint-hosted with width pinned to the clip, which is the whole bug fix; the promoted probe is now the regression fence, measuring alignment rects (constraints position those, and a label's frame sits ~2pt wider, which tripped the fence's first draft at 590 vs 588 before it measured the right rect). Points and actions wrap via `NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString:)` at a measured `layout(for:width:)` whose self-calibrating row gap keeps every short-card height byte-identical, so the UX34 clamp arithmetic and its tests stood untouched; the action ring pins to the first baseline so a wrapped action does not float its ring between lines. A second probe cleared the arithmetic first (205pt computed, lowest label at 191, slack exactly the 12pt pad plus rounding), then found `grad.frame = CGRect(origin: .zero, ...)`: a `CALayer` mask is positioned in its layer's coordinate space and an `NSClipView`'s bounds *origin* is what moves when its document scrolls, so the mask stayed over the first screenful and everything past it had no coverage and composited transparent. The numbers predict the screenshot exactly (scrolled 82 into 205 with a 123 viewport: visible only in bounds 82-123, eyebrow at 142 and action at 159 masked to nothing, fade band 97-123 explaining the dissolved second line). Fix is `clip.bounds` whole; gradient stops lifted into pure `fadeLocations(viewport:fadeHeight:)` so the band stays 26pt rather than a viewport proportion, clamped into [0,1]. The new source fence initially failed against correct code because the comment beside it quotes the banned literal, so it strips comments now; mutation-verified both ways, the second fence in this task to be wrong about its own subject. 1888 tests green. **Owner-owed:** the next real prompt: bullets read as complete sentences, the fade reads as "continues", scrolling reveals the eyebrow and actions, the date sits top right. **Provenance, from the filing:** owner's live prompt screenshot, 2026-07-30 (bullets sliced mid-glyph at the panel edge, no wrap, scroll invisible); a layout probe separated one bug from two design calls: as UX34's "frame-sized, not constrained" scroll document, the card's width is dictated by content under the layout engine, so it laid out **879pt wide in a 600pt panel** (long bullets at maxX 773/867/823 against a 588 inset; the right-aligned date at maxX 867, off-panel since UX34 landed; the configured tail-ellipsis never fired because nothing compressed). The design calls: CAL2's recorded single-line-truncation trade, overruled by the owner's eyeball ("I was thinking text will be line breaked"); and UX34's half-row-slice scroll cue, which the owner read as broken, not inviting. Design run 2026-07-30 offered wrap+fade / two-line clamp / honest ellipsis; **owner picked wrap+fade**. Scope: pin the document width to the clip (fix shared by any option), wrap points and actions at a measured width with the one-arithmetic-pass invariant kept (self-calibrating row gap keeps short-card heights byte-identical), keep the 123pt viewport, fade the bottom edge while content continues below (gradient mask so the vibrant material shows through), flash the scroller on expand. Two-line clamp is the pre-agreed one-constant retreat if wrapped scrolling annoys. CAL3 owns the card's content; this is its form. |
| UX36 | Summary reading measure: centered column, honest padding, wrapping metadata | UX | done | P2 | **Closed 2026-07-30: owner confirmed the eyeball ("UX36 - good to close") after the fourth pass put both reading tabs on the shared 720 measure.** Shipped 2026-07-29, 1829 daemon tests green (8 new), no pipeline change, dash guard and truth fences clean. All four cap sites in the three summary surfaces now read `.frame(maxWidth: readingMeasure).padding(contentPadding).frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .top)`: gutter outside the cap, block centered. That alone **widens the real text column from 600 to 640** without touching the constant, which matters because 600 was below the 640-720 reading column `design/README.md` asks for, so the app had drifted under its own design system. `SummaryLayout` gained `contentPadding` and `noticeMeasure = 460`, the latter absorbing the two stray literals (which are in the failed state, not the "BYO/preview area" the spec guessed); the acceptance grep comes back empty. **Band pick, recorded: `ViewThatFits` with a two-line fallback, not trailing truncation.** Truncation must sacrifice either the owner (the most load-bearing fact on an action, and a clipped name can mean two people) or the anchors (the row's only route back to the recording); in an already-scrolling pane a second line is free, so height is the cheaper currency than width, and the split at owner/due/confidence over anchors converges on the shape the bullet rows already use. `MeetingRow`'s deliberate removal of `ViewThatFits` does not apply: that was NSTableView caching row heights inside a `List`, and these rows sit in a `LazyVStack`. **Not in the spec:** the band's guard read `action.evidence` while `EvidenceChips` draws nothing without an `onCite`, so a static surface (digest reader, A16 compare pane) with anchors and no chips opened an empty indented band; a new `shownEvidence` closes it. The inline editor's `contentPadding: 16` became the shared 20 (its squeeze rationale was about the old inside-the-cap geometry, and 4pt a side of drift across the edit crossfade is what the shared constant exists to prevent). The A16 compare pane's headings moved onto the measure too, since centering the columns they label would otherwise strand them a whole margin away. **Deliberately not done:** the optional 640 to 680 nudge, which the spec marks owner-eyeball-gated and a headless session cannot judge; a test pins the measure inside 640-720 so it stays safe to apply. **Second pass 2026-07-29, after the owner's eyeball came back negative ("still pretty much ugly, this time less readable"), mocked at true scale and approved before any code.** The eyeball caught the relationship, not the measure: the body centred while the header sat at the pane edge and the tabs spread the full pane, so the first 200pt offered three left edges and none was the prose's. Underneath it was a real bug, `tabButton` drew the active underline as a bare `Rectangle` **sibling** in a `VStack`, and a `Rectangle` is a greedy shape, so it took every point offered, the stack inherited that, and three greedy buttons divided the pane while the trailing `Spacer` got nothing; the strip read left-aligned in source and shipped spread across 1230pt with an underline several times wider than its word. Now an `.overlay(alignment: .bottom)` on the label, and a `daemon/CLAUDE.md` "Don't", since only the render was wrong. **Owner decision, recorded: header + tab strip are chrome, not content**, banded on `bgRaised` across the pane with the existing Divider as its edge. Putting them on the reading column was traced and rejected because `TranscriptTab`/`AudioTab` are full-width and uncapped, so a measured header aligns on Summary and misaligns on the other two; the two alternatives offered (one ~1000pt column for the whole pane, which would have narrowed this spec's own no-max-on-the-detail-panel rejection, and left-parking everything, which returns the dead space this task was filed for) were declined. **The pre-registered nudge was taken, 640 to 680**, inside the 640-720 `design/README.md` band, which the first pass's range test allowed without an edit; 720 was rejected for prose (near 100 characters a line) even though the inspector card is 720, because a label/value grid is not prose. 1877 daemon tests green, 2 new fences. **Third pass 2026-07-29, after the owner rebuilt and marked both remaining gutters on a screenshot.** Two findings. The band was **invisible**: `bgRaised` over `bg` in dark is an 11-of-255 step, unfindable in a screenshot even knowing where to look, and a band nobody sees licenses nothing, so it now recesses to `bgSunk` with a `borderStrong` hairline (the direction mac toolbars take, and it frees `bgRaised` to mean content). And the **axis jumped between tabs**, which was my error in proposing the band: I traced whether a measured header would fight the transcript, but never whether the two tab bodies would fight each other, and they did (summary centred at 275, transcript full-width at 16, so changing tab slid the body 259pt under a fixed header). Owner's counter beat my proposed inner page card: a 940 page inside a 1372 pane only relocates the gutters, so **cap the column instead**. That reverses this spec's own first-pass rejection of a detail max, correctly: the rejection assumed the other tabs used the width, and the transcript was running past 1300pt unmeasured, which is not use. `LibraryLayout.detailMaxWidth = 1040` as the column's `max:`; split-view columns always fill, so slack goes to the meeting list where titles truncate today (~460 to ~740 on the owner's window) and the detail pane carries **zero** gutters there. With the pane bounded, all five cap sites drop their centring and every tab's content shares one left edge; UX33's 720 card is now nearly redundant inside it. Verified there is exactly **one** three-panel UI (one `NavigationSplitView`), so the cap has one home; Preferences is a separate fixed two-panel split; all five detail contents suit a cap, including `DigestReaderView`, which is prose despite its comment claiming it wants full width. 1882 tests green, 3 new (2 arithmetic invariants, 1 source fence). **A fence that could not fail, caught by mutation:** the left-align fence first used a 320-char window that the intervening comment overran, so it ran zero assertions and passed against a mutated file; it now anchors on the next placement frame and asserts `checked > 0`. **Fourth pass 2026-07-29: the transcript joins the measure, shared at 720 (option A of the reading-width run, owner-picked).** The third pass's left seam closed and the owner's next look found the right one: summary text ended at 700, transcript ran to ~1024, a ~300pt right-edge jump per tab change. Three options were mocked at the shipped cap (one measure; screenplay gutter, rejected for re-breaking the left axis; reference rail, rejected for dashboard drift) and A won: `TranscriptTab`'s reading zone (cast strip + captions + rows) rides the identical `SummaryLayout.readingMeasure` stack with the internal horizontal 16s stripped so the stack's gutter is the only inset, while the transport, empty state, and Audio stay full-bleed (instruments and states, not reading content). Measure 680 to 720 by owner pick, the top of the design band; it now equals the inspector card's 720, a deliberate convergence recorded in the inspector test whose strictly-greater assertion asked "if these converge, say why" (relaxed to greater-or-equal, keeping the half that matters: a grid never narrower than prose). 1882 tests green; the left-align fence now scans `TranscriptTab.swift` too. **Owner-owed:** rebuild and read one meeting across both tabs, right edge at 740 on each, cast chips starting on the rows' text edge, 720 prose comfortable; the single knob left is `detailMaxWidth` if the trailing margin bothers the eye, at the cost of Audio's waveform width. |

Leg (d): re-runs land on run-all's done notification, and SummaryTab's lone NSAlert is gone in favour of the one notifier every affordance shares. **CONVENTIONS note:** the event table is a *category* table (the fence asserts exactly two rows) and CONVENTIONS states actions are deliberately ungoverned, so `pipeline_dequeued` needed no row; `coordinator` is already listed and `truth_fences.py events` is green. **Owner-owed:** the spec's eyeball, cancelling a healthy Reprocess within 5 s and watching a detail-menu Re-summarize chip appear, complete, and toast. Out of scope as specced: no cancel for the in-process ANE transcription stage. **Closed 2026-07-31, acceptance met in full including the event leg.** The owner's first attempt looked fine but left no trace, because `cancelActiveJob` returns silently when no job is active (`SinkDispatcher.swift:453`) and a short Reprocess had already finished inside the five-second window, which makes a late click indistinguishable from a successful one. Re-run against a 68-minute meeting it landed properly, and the log carries the whole sequence: `pipeline_queued` at depth 2 (a duplicate Reprocess), `pipeline_dequeued` back to depth 1, then `pipeline_cancelled`. The dequeue is the first ever recorded, so the queued-duplicate half of the acceptance is verified rather than assumed. Cancel is visible while the job is healthy, not only when stalled, and the row returns retryable. The re-summarize half passed separately (busy chip in both the row and the detail header, shared toast on completion). One defect found by this pass and filed rather than fixed here: the cancellation also raises `Pipeline failed: pipeline exited 15` captioned with an unrelated INFO line, because the app cannot tell its own SIGTERM from a crash. That is UX50; it is a presentation fault on top of a cancel that works. |

| UX42 | Launch-at-login toggle truthfulness | UX | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-07-31, daemon green at 1997 (17 new), the 9-case `scripts/test-login-agent-guard.sh` green, truth fences and both dash guards clean; no Python touched. One mechanism owns login-start now, and it is the LaunchAgent that was always doing the work. `LaunchAtLoginService` no longer touches `SMAppService.mainApp` (a registration the agent never consulted, which is why the app started at login however the toggle read); it reads `launchctl print-disabled gui/<uid>` and writes `launchctl enable` / `disable` on `com.meetingpipe.daemon`, behind an injected `LaunchctlRunning` so the state machine is tested without ever mutating the real service. Off is `disable`, never `bootout`: booting out the agent that owns the running process would kill the app under the user's pointer. **The delegated decision, answered: the plist's `RunAtLoad` is NOT rewritten**, so launchd's disabled-overrides database is the single owner of on/off. The belt would be the weaker of the two (install.sh regenerates the plist from the template on every run, while the overrides DB survives that), it only takes effect after a bootout+bootstrap, which is the app-killing move just ruled out, and it would break `rebuild.sh`, whose bootstrap relies on `RunAtLoad` to bring the daemon back. The shell half is a new `scripts/lib/login-agent.sh` sourced by both scripts: `install.sh`'s `launchctl load -w` became a plain `bootstrap`, because `-w` *is* a write of an enabled override and was re-arming the toggle on every install, and `rebuild.sh` relaunches the app directly instead of bootstrapping when the agent is disabled (bootstrapping a disabled service fails, so it would otherwise die on a state the owner chose). Errors reach the General footer instead of the log. **Owner-owed:** the eyeball needs a real logout, so no session can do it; walkthrough in the spec, and it carries a third check the spec did not have (install over a disabled agent). **Closed 2026-07-31, all checks passing, owner-confirmed across two real logouts.** The toggle now means what it says: with launch at login off the app did not start at login, with it back on it did, `launchctl print-disabled` agreed with the switch at every step, and both `rebuild.sh` and `install.sh` left the disabled agent alone rather than re-arming it (the install leg could not be tested from a session at all, which is why it was owner-owed). The TECH-UX7 crash net survived: a `kill -9` brought the icon back within about ten seconds. Three defects surfaced by running it, all filed rather than folded in, and none of them a fault in this task's own fix: UX54 (two daemons ran at once, and there is no single-instance guard anywhere; this task's sequence is full of ways to reach it), UX55 (the status-bar menu still offers "Quit (do not relaunch)" when the agent is disabled and nothing can relaunch, because the row keys off the preference rather than the agent this task made the single owner), and UX56 (Preferences opens behind other windows, suspected UX39 regression). UX55 is the one worth reading as this task's own loose end: it is the same truthfulness defect, one layer up. |
| LOCAL16 | Local-LLM resource protection: RAM tiers, fail-closed spawn, free-RAM watchdog | Local models | done | P1 | Shipped 2026-07-30; all five scope items landed, and the status is the pre-registered eyeball clause only. `mp.resource_guard` is the shared module: the sizing helpers promoted out of `doctor`, a pure RAM-tier policy (8/16/24/32/48 GB rows, anchored on the numbers the product already asserts rather than on a ratio, which put the 14B over on 24 GB when tried), and an injectable-sampler `MemoryWatchdog` whose throttled `check(...)` is callable per batch, so AI11 can take the policy and the watchdog separately. `_spawn` and `mp serve-local` refuse an over-tier model before any load, `LocalModelPreloader.shouldPreload` gained the same term, the local request loop checks the watchdog on every call, and the server's output now lands in a rotated `mlx-server.log` whose tail the startup-failure message quotes instead of guessing. Preferences annotates each preset against `ProcessInfo.physicalMemory` and disables an over-tier one with the reason on the row itself. A refusal or abort carries the phrase `Not enough memory`, which the daemon matches to select the new `memory` failure stage, so the Library row says why. The guard refuses only what it can measure (a Custom repo id is never refused on size, the watchdog covers it); `MP_RAM_GUARD=0` is the owner-dev bypass. **Owner-owed:** the walkthrough at the end of the spec, whose one live leg is a local summarize under real memory pressure aborting with the named error instead of beachballing the Mac. **Closed 2026-07-31 on its verified legs, with the unverified one split out to LOCAL18 by owner decision** (the VALID1-to-EGRESS1 precedent: a leg that was not measured is split rather than dressed up as a pass). Verified by the owner: the RAM tiers annotate the Preferences presets against this machine rather than a generic "wants 24 GB+"; `mp doctor` reports the tier honestly ("32 GB RAM admits a model up to ~9 GB (~8000 tokens per request)", then a verdict on the configured model, then "free memory now: 38%"); and the fail-closed refusal reads well as writing, naming the Mac's RAM, the model's need and the fix in one sentence. That tier refusal is the protection that would have stopped the documented 14B-on-32GB incident, and it works. **Not verified, and the reason it is a task rather than a retry:** the runtime free-RAM watchdog has never fired in the entire event-log history, and a deliberate attempt to make it fire failed, with `memory_pressure` running out of allocable memory at 65% while the summarize completed normally. The doubt is that `free_pct` sums buckets macOS reclaims under pressure, so it may read high exactly when the machine is in trouble. LOCAL18 carries that. Two walkthrough defects corrected in this spec while running it: step 2 sent the owner to a disclosure that only renders once the backend is already local, so following it silently repointed their daily summaries from Anthropic to Qwen 7B, and step 5 suggested `memory_pressure -S`, which simulates the pressure level without applying real pressure and therefore could never trip a watchdog that reads `vm_stat`. An unselectable Custom preset noticed in the same pass is UX43's filed (c) leg, not a defect here. |
| SEC15 | Fence RAG excerpts in mp ask | Security | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-08-03. `mp ask` was the last model-facing surface that interpolated meeting content raw. `rag_user` now wraps the packed excerpts in `prompt_safety.wrap_untrusted()` once, whole block rather than per chunk, with the `[stem]` markers inside the fence (they are excerpt content, and `RAG_SYSTEM` already tells the model to cite tags found in the excerpts) and the question outside it, since the question is the only instruction-bearing text the user actually wrote. `RAG_SYSTEM` appends the shared `UNTRUSTED_GUIDANCE` verbatim rather than a RAG-worded copy: its "transcript content" phrasing reads a shade narrow next to "excerpts", but an excerpt IS transcript or summary text, and one copy of the marker names is what stops this surface from fencing against markers a later rename no longer writes. The citation contract is unaffected end to end, since `extract_citations` / `verify_citations` parse the answer and not the context, and the fence markers carry no `[stem]` of their own. The assess-and-record leg on `mp digest` came out **yes**, not the "likely no" the filing guessed: the narrate facts are second-order (fields a summarizer wrote), but an action task or decision line can carry a participant's words close to verbatim (FEAT10 evidence quotes are the explicit case), so an "ignore your instructions" spoken in a meeting reaches the narrator through its own summary. `narrate` fences the whole facts block (every instruction it follows lives in `_NARRATE_SYSTEM`, so the user turn is data and nothing else, and the AI10 header it opens with is a count that reads the same fenced) and `_NARRATE_SYSTEM` carries the guidance too. Six new tests pin both paths, including marker-smuggling on the rag path and through a summary, plus the wiring assertion that the fence and the guidance reach `engine.complete_text`. Pipeline green: ruff clean, pyright 0 errors, 1163 pytest passed (1157 before); truth fences green, no config key or event category touched. |

| UX48 | No main menu, so every command-key shortcut is dead in the Library | UX | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-08-04; every engineering line of the acceptance is green and the status is the eyeball clause plus two owner questions. `swift build` clean, daemon suite green with 13 new tests (`MainMenuTests` 9, `WindowActivationManagerTests` 4), truth fences clean; no Python touched. **The fix:** `MainMenu.swift`, an `NSApp.mainMenu` of App (Preferences) / Edit (Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All) / Window (Minimize, Close), every item on a nil target so AppKit walks the responder chain from the key window. `WindowActivationManager` installs it in the same step that raises the policy to `.regular` and removes it in the same step that drops back to `.accessory`, so the menu bar exists exactly while the app owns one. Preferences routes through a new `AppDelegate.openPreferencesFromMainMenu`, since a menu item's responder chain reaches `NSApp`'s delegate and not `Coordinator`. `292dfe49`'s zero-opacity `Button` and its comment are deleted from `LibraryWindow.swift`. **Two spec claims were measured rather than assumed, and both were wrong.** (1) The band premise: there is **no `NSTextView` in this app**, so there is no context menu to fall back on. An offscreen `NSHostingView` probe reports `.textSelection(.enabled)` is backed by `SwiftUI.SelectionTextField`, an `NSTextField` subclass with no `.menu`, nil from `menu(for:)`, and no response to `copy:`; no ancestor carries a menu either. Recommendation is therefore **P1, not P2** (DIAR2 precedent), hedged only by the probe being unable to create a live selection headlessly, which walkthrough step 1 closes in one right-click. The reason not to repeat the shape is unchanged and stronger: Copy has to reach the text under the pointer, which no button this app owns can be. Why the owner saw Cmd+, tick is unsettled and plausibly UX56 (Preferences opening behind the Library). **Remainder:** the owner walkthrough in the spec, and two questions. (a) The band, from step 1. (b) The spec's `:33` claim that a main menu makes Cmd+K work with no dropdown open is **false and was not shipped**: `NSApp.mainMenu.performKeyEquivalent` searches the main menu tree only and an `NSStatusItem`'s menu is not in it (HYG6 filed the same defect independently). Cmd+K from any MeetingPipe window needs a Quick Find row on the main menu, four lines, recommended; Cmd+K with another app frontmost needs a Carbon global hotkey that would take the chord from every app, recommended against. Neither shipped without a yes. A third, smaller: the enumerated menu has **no Quit**, so Cmd+Q still beeps in the Library while the app now looks like a normal app; UX55 is in that area, so it was left alone. UX39's archived walkthrough steps 3 and 4 were corrected in `q6-final.md` in the same commit (both were unrunnable or unfalsifiable because of this bug), and `docs/GUIDE.md`'s menu-bar sentence, which DOC11 wrote true only while no main menu existed, was corrected with it. **Walkthrough run 2026-08-04, steps 1 and 3 to 8 all pass.** The band question is answered and the band **stays P2**: right-click Copy on a real mouse selection works, so a mouse path out of the app did exist and this fix is the convenience it was filed as, not a broken core promise. That falsifies the strong reading both probes had been given (neither could create a live selection, so both measured the untouched control), and `daemon/CLAUDE.md` plus FEAT13's row were corrected in the same commit. Owner's method note, worth keeping: check this on the **selection**, never on the transcript line, because the row carries its own context menu (Edit text…, Clarify…) and answers first. Cmd+A / Cmd+C in the search field, Cmd+C over transcript text, Cmd+M, Cmd+W, Cmd+, from the Library, Cmd+K in the open dropdown, and the menu-bar handback on close all pass, so no keystroke beeps any more. **Cmd+K decision answered 2026-08-04: yes to the main-menu row, and it shipped in the same session.** A `Find` submenu carrying `Quick Find…` on Cmd+K, routed through `AppDelegate.openQuickFindFromMainMenu` on the same nil-target responder-chain seam Preferences uses, so `MainMenu` still holds no coordinator. The Carbon global hotkey stays rejected. Suite green with 1 new test, plus three existing MainMenu tests updated for the fourth submenu; README and `docs/GUIDE.md` (both hotkey tables and the Quick Find recipe) corrected in the same commit, since DOC11's contract makes a stale key table a filing-quality failure. **Remaining: the owner's own Cmd+K-from-a-window check after the next rebuild, then archive.** **Closed 2026-08-04 on the owner walkthrough**, all steps pass: right-click Copy on a real selection works (band stayed P2), no keystroke beeps any more, and the menu bar hands back on the last close. | UX58 | Speaker colour is keyed on the raw label and reshuffles on every launch | UX | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-08-04; the status is the walkthrough clause only. `swift build` clean, daemon suite green with 9 new tests; no Python touched. Speaker colour is now two calls, `MeetingCast.colorIndex(for:in:)` then `TranscriptDisplay.color(atCastIndex:)`, and the slot is the speaker's **position in the meeting's cast**, keyed on UX57's `rowSpeaker(...)` identity rather than on `segment.speakerID`. One rule answers all three defects: colour follows a reassignment because the identity it indexes does, it is a pure function of the meeting's own files so a relaunch reproduces it exactly, and first-appearance position is collision-free while the cast is at or under the palette's eight. Past eight it wraps, said in the comment rather than fixed with a wider palette; the eight are UX14's contrast-tuned set and DSN18's `ContrastFloorTests` is untouched. The `speaker_N`-parses-its-own-integer branch went with the hash: kept beside cast positions it would have collided with them, which is precisely the no-two-share-a-colour clause. **Decisions not in the spec.** The two sheets take the *resolved* identity rather than only a colour, so the line editor's header and Clarify's no longer name the cluster a reassigned line was moved off while wearing its hue; both read `segment.speakerID` for name and colour alike. FEAT13's `ClarifySheet` is a fourth call site that did not exist when this was filed, so `ClarifyTarget` carries `speakerName` + `speakerColorIndex` in place of `speakerID`; leaving it behind would have kept the launch-reshuffle alive in one surface. Nine cases in `MeetingCastTests`: the mapping computed twice from freshly declared inputs and compared (never by hashing, which agrees with itself inside one process and proves nothing about a launch-to-launch defect), uniqueness at six and at eight voices, a reassignment moving one line's slot and leaving its old speaker's alone, naming leaving every slot where it was, the ninth voice wrapping onto the first, and a no-speaker line drawing muted. **UX59 consumes exactly this:** `MeetingCast.colorIndex(displayName:in:cast)` then `TranscriptDisplay.color(atCastIndex:)`, the same two calls a row makes, and the index is stable for a meeting whichever view asks. Colour is per **meeting** by construction, so one person can read differently in two meetings, which UX59's scope already accepts. **Owner-owed:** the seven-step walkthrough at the end of `UX58`'s entry in this file, whose live legs are steps 3, 4 and 5 (the reassignment, the relaunch, and no two voices sharing a colour), plus step 1's `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, which was not run from the session that built this. Original report: filed 2026-08-03, owner-reported ("once I assign Sudip, then want to re-assign wrong replica from Sudip to someone else, color remains on sudip"), plus two defects found in the same function that no eye could isolate. `TranscriptDisplay.color(for:)` took the raw label, so colour did not follow a reassignment (UX57's root confusion, different consequence), and it indexed the palette by `abs(hashValue) % 8`. Swift reseeds string hashing per process and nothing here sets `SWIFT_DETERMINISTIC_HASHING`, so **colours changed on every launch**: measured 2026-08-03 across three processes, `THEM-A` landed on slot 3, then 4, then 7. Collisions were routine too, about 92% likely with 6 voices, and run 1 put three speakers on one slot. Teams meetings all took that hash branch (`THEM-*`), so it hit every real meeting. **Closed 2026-08-04 on the owner walkthrough**, steps 2 to 6 pass: a reassigned line takes the target speaker's colour on both the dot and the name, colours are identical after a full quit and relaunch (the check the old hash-indexed build failed every time), no two speakers share a slot, and both appearances stay readable. |

| FEAT13 | Clarify a misheard word where you find it, not in Preferences | Feature | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-08-04; `swift build` clean, `swift test` green, 22 new tests, `truth_fences.py both` green. **Clarify a word…** now sits on a transcript line's right-click menu, under **Edit text…**. Found while running it, filed as UX66 rather than folded in: a per-meeting overlay and a vocabulary rule that touch the same word fight, and the stale overlay wins silently. |

| UX55 | "Quit (do not relaunch)" is still offered when nothing can relaunch | UX | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-08-04; every engineering line of the acceptance is green and the remainder is the owner walkthrough in the spec. `swift build` clean, daemon suite green with 3 new tests, truth fences clean; no Python touched. **The fix:** `StatusBarModel.offersQuitWithoutRelaunch(_:)` is the rule (`!disableAutoRestart && launchAgentEnabled`) over a new `Inputs.launchAgentEnabled`, and `StatusBarController` asks it instead of carrying its own `if !UISettings.shared.disableAutoRestart`. `Row` needed no change, since `quitWithoutRelaunch` was already modelled, so the tests pin the shipped row directly rather than falling back to a fence the way DOC11's unconditional row had to. **The one decision not in the spec:** the agent state is `LaunchAtLoginService.status().isOn`, read in `refreshMenuBeforeDisplay` and cached on the controller rather than read where it is used. `status()` spawns `launchctl`, and `populateMenu` also runs on every model-download progress tick and every processing-count change, so an inline read would have been a subprocess per tick on the main queue; the pre-display hook is where the permissions re-probe already lives and AppKit calls it before every display. That is also what settles the spec's "confirm rather than assume" about the toggle: the re-read is per menu open, so no rebuild or relaunch carries it. A `.notInstalled` agent reads as not enabled and hides the row for the same reason nothing can relaunch it; an unreadable `print-disabled` reports enabled and keeps the row, which is what Preferences already renders. One source fence over `StatusBarController` was added beside the model tests, because the menu is built by hand rather than from `rows` and a correct model beside a stale hand-built condition is precisely this defect. Docs: `README.md` (startup paragraph + the Idle-in-a-meeting troubleshooting line), `docs/GUIDE.md`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `daemon/CLAUDE.md`. **Remainder:** the spec's owner walkthrough, steps 2 to 4 (step 1's `rebuild.sh` was deliberately not run, with 18 parallel worktrees in flight). A recommendation on UX48's open Cmd+Q question was returned to the owner unshipped: the app menu's quit section, if it is added, has to read the same predicate or it reproduces this defect on a second surface. **As filed** (2026-07-31, line numbers below are the pre-fix ones): owner-reasoned from the menu alone at the end of UX42's walkthrough: "I just need to see one 'quit' instead of 'quit dont relaunch', cause when this flag is off, relaunch is not working for classic quit." Correct. The row's condition is `if !UISettings.shared.disableAutoRestart` (`StatusBarController.swift:601`), which consults only the preference, while UX42 made the login agent the single owner of relaunch-after-quit and its own close note says "with launch at login OFF, Quit MeetingPipe really quits". So with the agent disabled, plain Quit already means quit, which is exactly the case the code's own comment says should hide the extra row, and it is shown anyway. Behaviour is correct either way; this is a truthfulness defect of the same family UX42 was about, a control describing a distinction the machine no longer makes. Scope: condition on `disableAutoRestart` **and** the agent being enabled (`LaunchAtLoginService` already reads the latter), with the predicate in `StatusBarModel` where its comment at `:262` already describes the rule. **Closed 2026-08-04 on the owner walkthrough.** The owner confirmed the Startup toggles and the dropdown agree: **Quit (do not relaunch)** is shown or hidden to match, so the row now describes a distinction the machine actually makes, which was the whole defect. Found while running it and not folded in: the Startup toggles were briefly unresponsive until a full quit, filed separately rather than absorbed here, since UX55 changed only the menu predicate and never the toggles' own binding. |

The regulated mis-keying is corrected by dropping the claim rather than re-deriving it: nothing-published now reads "Meeting processed / Nothing was published.", since "Local Markdown ready (regulated mode)" asserted a *mode* off a nil page URL and was a guess for a BYO, too-long, or zero-sinks run alike. `PublishSink` is a fourth type carrying the `output.sinks` vocabulary and is pinned against `WorkflowSink` and `PublishTarget` rather than merged with them, since `WorkflowSink.notion` carries a database id and cannot be built from a bare name. Deliberately untouched: the Open action's behaviour, and the `General`-classification question behind "no Notion since 28th", which is routing working as configured. **Owner-owed:** the five-step walkthrough at the end of `UX49`'s entry in this file, whose live leg is a finished `Personal` meeting whose banner no longer says Notion and whose Open still opens the summary. **Closed 2026-08-04 on the owner walkthrough.** The done notification no longer names Notion for a filesystem publish and names the local note instead, and its Open action still opens the summary, so the rename did not break the action it renamed. Corroborated on disk: the publish sidecar for a Personal meeting carries the `sinks` model UX49 added (`sinks: {filesystem: {ok: true, page_url: file://...}}`), which is the source of truth the wording now reads instead of guessing from `page_url`. | LANG2 | One stray Cyrillic character disables the whole summary-language target | Pipeline | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-08-04; suite green, 4 new tests (ruff, pyright, truth fences clean). The `cyr == 0` purity gate is now one symmetric share, `_LANG_MAX_MINORITY_SHARE = 0.33`: a transcript is a firm target only when at least two thirds of its letters are one script, whichever script leads. **The threshold was measured, not guessed, and measured on the right text.** The first pass scored the 232-transcript library by raw segment text and landed on 20%; re-scored on the rendered **markdown**, which is what `summarize` actually hands the function, the Cyrillic side's ceiling moves from 10.8% to 23.1% and 20% would have de-verified a real Ukrainian meeting, which is the damage the walkthrough's step 3 exists to catch, arrived at from the other side. On markdown the population is three groups: 205 meetings single-script exactly; the 19 Cyrillic-dominant ones at 0.9% to 23.1% Latin (a Ukrainian standup borrows English terms word by word, longest Latin run 14 words); the Latin-dominant ones at 0.1% to 1.4% with one at 8.0% (Cyrillic only enters an English transcript as contiguous 35 to 94-word asides); and exactly one genuinely bilingual meeting at 45.2%. So the window is (23.1%, 45.2%) and 0.33 sits 1.43x above the ceiling and 1.37x below the bilingual one. Verified against the whole library: **7 meetings change answer, all `None -> en`, and none loses a target**, so it is a pure widening. On the subject meeting `20260730-163434` the target is now `en` and all five stored sections flag as divergent, so LANG1's repair fires. `language_signature` was reviewed in the same pass and deliberately **left on the majority split**: real Ukrainian summary sections carry 20% to 37% Latin (one title at 49%), so sharing the threshold would make `divergent_sections` blind to most of them, which is LANG1's mechanism switched off. **Finding worth its own task:** the 23.1% ceiling is not linguistic. That meeting's speech is 5.7% Latin; the rest is the markdown wrapper, whose header and one `**Name**:` label per turn are Latin whatever the meeting was spoken in, a fixed cost per turn that lands hardest on the shortest meetings. A still shorter Cyrillic meeting could clear 33% on labels alone, and the fix for that is to stop counting the wrapper rather than to keep raising the constant. **Owner-owed:** the five-step walkthrough at the end of `LANG2`'s entry in this file, whose live legs are the re-summarize of `20260730-163434`, a read of two or three genuinely Ukrainian meetings to confirm they are unchanged, and the judgement call on the two code-switched meetings the corpus scan named (`20260521-163051`, now `en`; `20260611-113210`, still unverified). **Closed 2026-08-04 by owner decision, walkthrough NOT run.** Recorded plainly so the archive is not read later as a verified pass. What *is* verified, by the shipping session: `_LANG_MAX_MINORITY_SHARE = 0.33` was chosen against a re-measurement of all 232 transcripts after the session caught its own first pass scoring the wrong text (raw segments rather than the rendered markdown `summarize` actually passes, whose per-turn labels are Latin whatever the meeting was spoken in); the resulting window is (23.1%, 45.2%), and a library-wide check showed 7 meetings change answer, all `None -> en`, **none losing a target**, so the widening is pure. On the subject meeting `20260730-163434` the target is now `en` and all five sections flag divergent, so LANG1's repair fires on the exact meeting that produced the report. Suite green with 4 new tests, ruff, pyright and truth fences clean. What is **not** verified is the owner's eyeball on the two genuinely code-switched meetings the corpus scan found, `20260521-163051` (now English-targeted) and `20260611-113210` (still unverified either way); whether that split is right was the one input that would have moved the constant. Also carried forward unfiled: the 23.1% ceiling is a markdown-wrapper artefact rather than a linguistic fact (that meeting's speech is 5.7% Latin), so a shorter Cyrillic meeting could clear 33% on labels alone, and the real fix is to stop counting the wrapper rather than to keep raising the constant. |

| UX53 | Sweep every operation for whether the open view learns it happened | UX | done | P2 | Sweep done 2026-08-04, table in the spec: 29 operations scored on observed behaviour, 23 refresh, 3 partial, 3 do not, **none unchecked**. `swift build` clean, `swift test` green with 5 new tests. The finding worth the sweep: the failure is two independent halves, and only the second one actually broke. Every operation *does* reach a `revision` bump, because both trees write sidecars atomically and an atomic write is a rename the directory watcher sees; what fails is a pane keying its reload on `meeting.stem` and ignoring the bump. So the UX52 signature is a `.task(id: meeting.stem)` over a disk read, and there was exactly one more of them in the detail view: the header's Notion / Obsidian Open buttons, stale after a republish while the publish-state line beside them refreshed off `Meeting`. Fixed with UX52's idiom (`@ObservedObject` store + `PublishURLsReloadKey(stem:revision:)` + a two-sidecar fingerprint guard), pinned at the decision rather than the rendering. UX52's own "complete" claim was checked adversarially and holds for its operation. Named rather than fixed, each with a stated design question: `CorrectionWindow` writes the summary it loaded back over a newer one (a lost update, not a reload key); the Audio tab keeps a waveform for audio the retention sweep removed (its stem-only key is deliberate, playback); the Digests rail misses a digest the scheduler or automation started (no watcher on that dir); a roster rename that matched no meeting publishes nothing at all. FEAT13's row was checked on the rebase rather than left unchecked, and it paid: both its paths refresh correctly (its line path is row 12 exactly, and it removed its own `reload()` on finding `retranscribeMeeting` already publishes, which is this task's rule applied by a sibling), but checking it **re-scored row 13**. An open Preferences ▸ Vocabulary pane can overwrite a term added from the transcript, and FEAT13 moved that from "reachable only behind a just-edited line" to a direct item on every transcript row, so it graduated from a named gap to a drafted filing. | UX54 | Two MeetingPipes can run at once, and nothing stops the second | UX | done | P2 | Closed 2026-08-04 on the second pass, after the first one shipped a guard that never fired once. **The cause was the guard's own identity, not its peer query and not its ordering rule.** The shipped version read this process off `NSRunningApplication.current`, and at the point in `App.main()` where the guard has to run that object is a *placeholder*: measured across three live instances, it answers `processIdentifier` **-1**, nil `bundleIdentifier`, nil `launchDate`, `isTerminated` **true**. `decide` over a current with pid -1 collapses to `peer.pid < -1`, false for every real pid, so the incumbent list came back empty however many daemons were running and every copy concluded it was the only one. That is why `second_instance_stood_down` was never emitted, in either events file, ever, while the owner watched two and then three daemons run. The walkthrough's leading hypothesis, that the peer query returns empty that early, is **refuted**: at `main()` entry, 3 to 12 ms in and before `NSApplication` exists, `runningApplications(withBundleIdentifier:)` correctly listed 0, then 1, then 2 peers with the right pids as instances came up. So the query never needed moving or warming and the guard stays exactly where it was, which is the constraint the task set. Identity now comes from the kernel instead: `ProcessInfo.processInfo.processIdentifier` for the pid and a `sysctl` `KERN_PROC_PID` read of `p_starttime` for the launch date, neither of which needs a Launch Services connection. The peer side takes the same fallback, and that is not belt-and-braces but load-bearing: a Launch Services `launchDate` is nil for **79 of the 104** running apps on this Mac **including the launchd-started MeetingPipe itself**, so without it the real daemon's ordering would have been a bare pid comparison, and the observed duplicate pair was 87918 and 89520 against a ~99998 wrap ceiling. The two clocks were checked rather than assumed to agree: median disagreement 14 ms across the 25 apps Launch Services did date. **Verified by running it, not by argument.** The real `SingleInstanceGuard.swift` was compiled unmodified into a throwaway probe bundle carrying its own identifier (only `Log` shimmed, to keep the event out of the owner's real `events.jsonl`) and launched three times from `Contents/MacOS/...`, the route the owner reproduced the third daemon on. Control, built the same way from the shipped guard at `HEAD`: **3 alive**, no event, `NSRunningApplication.current` pid -1 in all three. Fixed: **1 alive**, the first one; instances 2 and 3 each logged one `second_instance_stood_down` naming pid 6444 with their own real `self_pid`, and each exited **0**. Nothing else was written by either. `swift build` clean, full daemon suite green (2324 tests, 4 new here for 14 total), `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` OK. What the probe cannot show is a *status item*, since it has none: one-status-item follows from one-process plus a stand-down exiting inside `main()` before `NSApplication` exists, which is structure rather than observation. `rebuild.sh` was checked for the failure mode a working guard newly makes reachable, a newcomer standing down against a peer that is still dying and leaving zero daemons, and it is self-cancelling: the Launch Services registration that would let the guard see the dying copy is the same one that makes `open` coalesce onto it instead of starting a newcomer, and the script's `pgrep` verification fails loudly rather than silently if nothing comes up. The launchd branch cannot race at all, since `bootstrap` retries until the old job is reaped. Also added: one unified-log line per launch naming the peer count on the **start** path, since a guard whose failure mode is "decided not to act" is silent by construction, and that silence is precisely what cost this task a walkthrough. |

| MIC8 | Teams `LogMuteAdapter` (native mute signal) | Detection | done | P2 | Shipped 2026-08-04, closing the last band the 2026-07-23 spike left open. The remainder was a build, not a measurement, and the gate on it was one owner word: **fuse, not supersede**. Three new files in the Core island: `SlimCoreMuteLog` (pure line parse + family resolution + byte-range tail), `LogMuteAdapter` (the host: 1 Hz tick, blocking read off main, edge-triggered sink), and `MuteSourceFusion` (the precedence). Teams' SlimCore media log now feeds the same `MicGate` field the AX scrape writes, and the log wins while it is fresh; the AX read carries whenever the log has been quiet for 5 s. **The build's one decision the spec did not settle:** "present" has to mean *the log spoke recently*, not *the log file exists*. The log is a transition stream that says nothing until the first toggle, so a file-existence rule would blind the gate at join time (only the AX read knows whether you joined muted) and would not cover the single measured log gap fusion exists for. 5 s is >5x the measured p90 lead, so it costs the log nothing normally while bounding an uncorrectable log miss to five seconds, which is the side the MIC9/MIC10 incidents say to protect. Fusing needed one seam change: `MicGate` starts **one adapter per source** rather than the first match overall (the two browser no-op adapters share a bundle set and still start only the first, so their distinct events still tell the no-AX surfaces apart), and `injectAxMuteEvent` / `clearAxMute` carry a `MuteReadingSource` that defaults to `.ax`, so the 1 Hz window watcher is unchanged. The clear is gated like a reading, deliberately: a blind AX read is not evidence about the log. **Verified against the real logs on this Mac, not only against fixtures.** The shipped resolver picks the live generation out of 132 files where it ranks 8th by mtime (the gotcha, live); the shipped parser finds exactly the 31 transitions `grep` and the Python census find in that generation; and the real adapter, replaying that file's real bytes line by line, emits exactly its edge-collapsed transition sequence with UTC-correct stamps. The standing regression test was re-run at pickup and the format held across 12 further days and 3 further generations (381 transitions / 6 generations, 93 pairs, 90 agree, log leads 90/93, p50 46 ms). 2346 daemon tests green (26 new), truth fences clean, no Python touched. **Not verified, and cheap to confirm incidentally:** the in-app path on a live Teams call. The wiring is one array entry in `Coordinator` plus per-source start, both unit-tested, and the next real call will write `log_mute_event` into `events.jsonl` if it works, so no walkthrough is owed; grep that action after the next meeting if you want the confirmation. Zoom deliberately stays on the AX read alone (empty/stale logs, opt-in verbose logging, zero Zoom calls in the corpus). |

The cancel intent now rides from the click to the termination handler on a **per-run** handle (`PipelineRunSlots`, lifted out of the launcher so the binding is testable without racing a signal against a real subprocess), so a killed run completes as `LaunchError.cancelled` rather than `nonZeroExit(15, <whatever was last on stderr>)`. Reprocess to run it again." Nothing reports it: no `pipeline_failed`, no error banner, no notification. The Library's one Cancel reaches four legs, not one, since UX28 put the re-summarize and publish re-runs in run-all's retain slot, so `SinkDispatcher`, `PipelineJobDispatcher`, and `MeetingLibraryService`'s regenerate / republish / ask branches all ask `PipelineLauncher.isCancellation` first; the ask leg stops double-logging `ask_failed` over the `ask_cancelled` its own click already wrote. Secondary half taken: `nonZeroExit`'s second value is now a caption from `failureCaption(stderr:)` (last `ERROR`/`CRITICAL` line, else last `WARNING`, else today's tail), so a genuine failure quotes the pipeline's own error rather than the last INFO line; LOCAL16's `.memory` staging survives it because `orchestrate` reports through `log.exception`. Does not close.** Verified from the log and the sidecar rather than the screen, on a real Cancel of a full re-run of `20260716-163031` at 13:04:55Z: `pipeline_cancelled` fired, **`pipeline_failed` did not**, no `mp` process was left running, no banner or notification appeared, and the terminal marker is exactly the shape decision 1 argued for (`stage: interrupted`, `reason: You cancelled this run. Reprocess to run it again.`). So `Pipeline failed: pipeline exited 15`, the whole reason this task exists, is gone, and the retryable modelling survived. **What fails is the other half of step 2, that the row returns to normal.** The row froze at **Cleaning up 0:20** in the In progress section and did **not** clear, including across a close and reopen of the Library, so it is not the projection being stale. The owner's screenshots contain the discriminator: the toolbar read **Idle** while that row still read **Cleaning up**, so the job lane cleared correctly and a **per-row progress entry did not**, and it outlives the window because the view does not own it. `Cleaning up` is the `diarize_cleanup` phase label (`MeetingRow.swift:396`), so the row is rendering the last phase the pipeline reported before the kill, with nothing on the cancel path clearing it. Distinct from UX52 and UX53's class, which is a view failing to re-read correct disk state; here the disk state is correct and a live in-memory entry is wrong. **Second finding, unmeasured:** Cancel is not offered immediately after Reprocess and appears only some time later, so there is a window in which a running job cannot be stopped; the owner reported it but its length was not measured. Steps 3 and 4 (re-Reprocess after a cancel, and cancelling an Ask) were not reached. **Second pass 2026-08-04: the walkthrough's remaining defect is fixed and the task closes.** The stuck row was neither the projection nor a missing reload key. The row's live progress entry was cleared by the *reporting* of a completion (the Coordinator's `onDone` / `onError`), while `PipelineJobDispatcher.route` returns early for exactly the two completions this app deliberately reports nothing about, a cancel and a library re-run, so UX50's own quieting took the clear away with the alarm and a cancelled run-all was left rendering its last heartbeat. `SinkDispatcher.onActiveProgressEnded` is the one clear now, fired from `completeActiveJob` on every path, beside UX28's busy-chip clear and for the reason that comment already gave; the done and error closures no longer touch `activeProcessing`. 5 new tests (4 in `SinkDispatcherTests`, 1 in `PipelineJobDispatcherTests`), and the four `SinkDispatcher` ones were each run red against the fix removed before it went in. `swift build` clean, `swift test` green at 2325, `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green. **The second finding is measured, and it is a different defect.** From the owner's own run: Reprocess clicked 13:03:39.998Z, FluidAudio ASR 13:03:40.034 to 13:04:32.574 (52.5 s), `mp run-all` up at 13:04:33.553, first `stage_progress` beat at 13:04:38.629, so **Cancel first appears 58.6 s after the click**. About 52.5 s of that is the daemon's own transcription, where there is no subprocess to signal and Cancel would be a dead control (`cancelActiveRun` has nothing retained yet), so covering it needs a cancellation seam in `TranscriptionRunner` rather than a presentation change; the remaining ~6 s is fixed cost, process start plus one 5 s heartbeat interval. Proposed as its own task at the end of the archived spec rather than widened into this one. The same log confirms the frozen label exactly: `Cleaning up 0:20` is beat 4 (`elapsed_s: 20`, 13:04:53.867Z), the last heartbeat before the 13:04:55.321Z kill. **Steps 3 and 4 close without a second walkthrough.** Step 3's blocker *was* this bug, since a row stuck in the In progress block disables Republish, Regenerate, Export and Move to Trash on that meeting, and what it checked, that a cancel leaves the row usable, is now pinned by the entry-clears tests beside the existing interrupted-marker and lane-drains ones. Step 4 does not share the seam at all: `AskModel.cancel` closes its own run out synchronously and the run-id guard drops the late completion, which five `AskModelTests` already pin. |

Step 4, the delta refresh, is the leg that was still owed and it passes on measurement rather than impression: the first ask after 27 new meetings logged stems_embedded=15 against stems_total=236 in 9.58 s, so the incremental path engaged (equal values would have been the bug this step exists to catch). | REC9 | The stop-time merge truncates the recording to the shorter capture channel, then deletes the only recoverable copy | Recording | done | P1 | **Shipped 2026-08-05, all four scope items; owner-owed is the walkthrough at the end of the spec (a real recording with Screen Recording toggled on mid-call), which needs a live meeting and cannot be run here.** Daemon suite green, 2377 tests with 21 new (`RecordingPostProcessorTests`, `RecordingDurationParityTests`); `swift build` clean; truth fences clean. The merge now runs under an explicit length policy (`RecordingPostProcessor.mergeLengths`: `apad` both legs, `adelay` a late system channel, `-t max(mic, offset + system)`), verified against real ffmpeg 8.1 before any Swift was written, where the shipped filter gave 3.000000 s and the new one 10.000000 s with the system channel silent outside its captured window. The head offset is measured rather than inferred, from `systemUptime` at start against the first frame written into the system WAV **as it currently stands** (the mark clears in `startSystemCapture`, because `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` truncates), with sub-1 s offsets dropped as the CAP1 skew so no normal recording moves; it also lands in `intermediate_durations` as `head_offset_sec`, since `delta_sec` cannot tell a channel that stopped early from one that started late. `outputIsPlausible` keeps REC1's 4 KiB floor and adds a duration check against that target with a 0.5 s tolerance, failing closed onto the kept intermediates plus a `.recordfail.json` whose `reason` names the shortfall, pinned end to end by a stand-in ffmpeg that exits 0 having written a short file. The parity warning is now `recorder`/`duration_parity_low` plus a "Recording is shorter than the meeting" notice over the pure `RecordingDurationParity`. All three doc/comment sites land here and each turned out to be a claim that this commit makes **true** rather than one to delete, so each names what re-breaks it. REC10 is untouched and still open; its scenario improves without being fixed, since a retry's audio is now placed where the retry happened rather than at sample 0, while the audio it overwrote is still lost. Filing note kept for provenance: filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band; the only critical finding, confirmed by an independent skeptic and reproduced by hand. `mergeToTempViaFFmpeg` uses a bare `amerge` with no length policy (`RecordingPostProcessor.swift:197`), so the final `<stem>.wav` ends where the **shorter** of mic/system ends; `producedPlausibleOutput` (`:66`) only checks 4096 bytes, `promoteMerged` (`:173`) reuses that same predicate, and `:131-132` then deletes both intermediates. Reproduced 2026-08-03 with the exact filter and args: 10.0 s mic + 3.0 s system produced a 3.0 s output at 192 KB, and `ffmpeg -h filter=amerge` shows the filter has no `duration` option at all. Measured cost across 153 recordings: 140 have system shorter than mic, 77.3 s of mic audio discarded in total, median 0.21 s (the harmless CAP1 skew). The tail is not harmless: on 2026-07-15 an SCStream TCC failure gave mic 41.2 s against system 5.28 s, and the merge kept 5.28 s, **87% of the meeting destroyed**, logged as `recording_stopped {produced_final: true}` and transcribed as one line. `MeetingRecorder.swift:1260` asserts the opposite of the measured behaviour ("the ffmpeg merge pads to the longer input"), and the DEP1 spike found this divergence on 2026-07-11 and dismissed it on a premise the log refutes. CAP1's trigger is skew magnitude rather than audio loss, so it never fired. Scope: explicit length policy with head-offset handling, duration-based plausibility check, keep intermediates on failure, promote the parity warning to an event, fix three doc/comment sites. **Closed 2026-08-05 by owner decision ("just archive it with remark in it").** Walkthrough step 3 is unperformable: changing the Screen Recording grant restarts the app, so the permission cannot be re-enabled mid-recording, and the step was written without accounting for that. It closes instead on three tests that drive real ffmpeg and decode the output per channel, including the audit's exact repro. REC10's retry-path overwrite is unaffected and stays open. |

C accounts for all three confirmed observations: both toggles dead together, window otherwise fine, cleared by a full quit and not by a window close. **Owner chose to fix C here rather than file it (2026-08-17), so all three landed.** C: every `launchctl` call is watchdogged, the child killed at `ProcessLaunchctl.ceilingSeconds` (5 s), and `LaunchAtLoginModel` is `@MainActor` running reads and writes on a detached task with an `isBusy` the toggle disables on. B: the reading is re-taken on the pane's `.onAppear`, deliberately not per render, since `status()` spawns a subprocess and UX55 recorded what an inline read on a hot path costs. A: a write that does not move `isOn` emits `daemon.launch_at_login_write_refused` carrying launchctl's exit status and stderr tail, pinned on the pure `LaunchAtLoginRefusal.decide` rather than on a log read, so the next occurrence is greppable instead of needing somebody to notice the group footer. One correction worth recording, and it is in `daemon/docs/gotchas.md`: the first version of the test read `preferredContentSize`, which is the property `NSHostingSizingOptions` is named for and which reads `(0, 0)` for every input in this harness, so it passed on the bug and on the fix alike; `intrinsicContentSize` is the same number by a route that is actually observable headlessly. The source fence was likewise verified red against a deliberate revert rather than assumed. `swift build` clean, `swift test` 2515 passed with 3 new.
