## Task specs

**[DONE] DET11 (P2): every surface says Accessibility only affects end-detection, but denying it kills start-detection too, silently.** Shipped 2026-08-15. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close, with the `MicInUseTier` question its Acceptance asks for answered in writing at the end.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. The finder's original framing was refuted; this is the narrower claim the skeptic established in its place, and it is the more useful one.

## What is wrong

Four surfaces tell the user that Accessibility buys end-detection only:

- `docs/SETUP.md:94`'s permission table gives the cost of skipping it as "Recordings do not auto-stop, so you get up to 15 extra minutes of audio".
- `README.md:158`: "Without this, native apps will record fine but the call won't auto-stop".
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/StatusBarController.swift:475` renders "Accessibility off - meeting end-detection degraded".
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Coordinator.swift:582` logs "Accessibility: NOT trusted - native meeting end-detection disabled".

The code disagrees. `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingSourceScanner.swift:253` is `if axTrusted {`, gating **every** native signal collection, so with Accessibility denied `titleMatch`, `callingControlsToolbar`, `leaveButton` and `muteButton` all stay false. `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingSourceScorer.swift:85` is `let contenders = candidates.filter { distinctSignalCount($0.signals) > 0 }`, which drops the zero-signal native entirely. So "records fine" is false: a native meeting is not detected at all, and the recording never starts to need stopping.

The drop is also invisible. `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingSourceScanner.swift:58-60` computes `droppedCandidates` from candidates that already have at least one signal, so a zero-signal native is filtered out **before** the dropped list is built and emits no `candidate_dropped` event. Nothing in `events.jsonl` records that a known meeting app was running and was discarded.

## What the skeptic refuted, recorded

The finder also claimed `MicInUseTier` should name a native holder and does not, citing `ARCHITECTURE.md:255` ("names the plausible holder (a browser / native meeting app / `mic_plausible` app)"). That half does not survive: the native exclusion is a deliberately shipped fix for a measured problem, documented 28 lines below the line the finder quoted. `MicInUseTier.swift:36-40` reads "plausibleBundles: browser + mic-plausible bundles (native whitelist apps are excluded - discovery owns them; see the watcher)", and `MeetingDiscoveryWatcher.swift:31-36` gives the causal story (a native pre-join holds the mic).

So `ARCHITECTURE.md:255` is wrong and should be corrected, but the exclusion itself is correct and must not be "fixed".

## Scope

Correct the four permission surfaces to say what Accessibility actually buys: with it denied, native meetings are not detected at all, not merely not auto-stopped. `docs/SETUP.md:94` matters most, since it is the clean-Mac walkthrough and a user who skips the grant on its stated cost gets a product that never notices a Teams call.

Correct `ARCHITECTURE.md:255` so it stops claiming the tier names a native.

Emit an observable event when a whitelisted native bundle is running but produced zero signals because Accessibility was untrusted, so the drop stops being silent and `mp analyze-detection` can see it.

Consider, and decide explicitly rather than by default, whether the native exclusion in `MicInUseTier` should become conditional on discovery actually being able to see natives, which would give the Accessibility-denied case a working catch-all tier. Note this is gated on DET10: the tier's input is dead today regardless, so this leg buys nothing until DET10 resolves.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A test drives the scanner with `axTrusted == false` over a running native candidate and asserts an observable event is emitted rather than silence. The four permission surfaces and `ARCHITECTURE.md:255` are corrected in the same commit. The `MicInUseTier` question is answered in writing in this spec, whichever way it goes.

## The `MicInUseTier` question, answered (2026-08-15)

**No. The native exclusion stays unconditional, and this leg is closed rather than deferred.** Three reasons, in the order that decides it.

**It would condition a tier that cannot fire.** `MicInUseTier.decide` needs a sustained mic-busy dwell, and the span tracker's only input is `AVCaptureDevice.isInUseByAnotherApplication`, which has never once read true across the whole event log. DET10 is the open task on exactly that, and its GO/NO-GO is owner-owed and unresolved. So on the machine this was filed for, both answers to the question produce identical behaviour today: silence. A change whose entire effect is conditional on another task's unresolved verdict is a change to make after that verdict, not before it.

**It is not a free option, because the exclusion is load-bearing.** A native pre-join holds the mic before its meeting window exists, which is why the exclusion was shipped in the first place. Conditioned on AX trust, the AX-denied machine would get a generic prompt naming whichever app was frontmost when the mic was grabbed (right often, wrong sometimes), and that prompt engages no lifecycle, so the recording it starts runs to the idle backstop instead of ending with the call. That is a real cost, paid for a detection tier that is off anyway, and unmeasurable while the input is dead.

**And the condition that reads obvious is the wrong one.** "Discovery cannot see natives" must be written as AX trust being absent, not as "the scan found no winner". A live call routinely produces no confident winner for tens of seconds while the client hides its call controls (DET9 measured 48 s once, 21-33 s in END9), so a winner-shaped condition would let DET1 prompt over a meeting the whitelist is already handling, which is the precise pre-emption the exclusion exists to prevent. The AX-shaped condition also needs a way to tell a blackout from an idle app, and that is what this task shipped: `detector.candidate_unreadable` fires only when a whitelisted native was actually running under a denied grant.

So: revisit if and only if DET10 returns GO, on the AX-trust condition, and reuse `candidate_unreadable` rather than inventing a second signal. `MicInUseTier.swift` carries a pointer to this answer beside the exclusion so the question is not re-opened by inspection.

**[DONE] LOCAL19 (P2): the auto backend's local fallback ignores `local_memory_floor_pct`, which poisons LOCAL18's own experiment.** Shipped 2026-08-15. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close; its line references had drifted by roughly 60 lines (the omission it names at `summarize.py:806-816` was at `:865-875` when the fix landed), and the decision it left open is recorded in the ToC row.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Found independently by the pipeline-contracts angle and the SOLID angle. Proposed high, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic.

## What is wrong

There are four production constructions of `LocalSummaryClient`. Three thread the configured memory floor and one does not.

- `pipeline/src/mp/summarize.py:806-816` is `_AutoFallbackClient._local`, whose argument list ends without `memory_floor_pct`.
- `pipeline/src/mp/summarize_local.py:313` is `memory_floor_pct: float = resource_guard.DEFAULT_FLOOR_PCT,`, so the omission silently substitutes 10.0 (`resource_guard.py:62`) rather than failing.
- `pipeline/src/mp/summarize.py:745`, `pipeline/src/mp/engine.py:103` and `pipeline/src/mp/diarize_cleanup.py:413` all pass it.
- `pipeline/src/mp/summarize.py:750-751` shows this is the whole `auto` backend, not a corner of it.

The documentation side is worse than the code side. `pipeline/src/mp/diarize_cleanup.py:411-412` states the intent as a universal: "the configured floor, not the default, so turning the watchdog down (or off) means the same thing on **every local path**". `README.md:613` and `config.example.toml:195` both say `0` turns the watchdog off. None of that holds on `auto`.

CI5's dead-knob fence cannot see this, because the key is genuinely read at four other sites. This is the class of drift a set-comparison fence structurally cannot catch.

## Why this matters more than its severity suggests

**It poisons LOCAL18's own investigation.** LOCAL18's cheap first leg is "whether the abort path works at all, answerable safely today by raising the `summarization.local_memory_floor_pct` knob so any run trips it". Run that way on an `auto` backend, the watchdog still runs at 10 percent, nothing aborts, and the result reads as "the abort path does not work". That is a false negative on the one experiment LOCAL18 exists to run, and it would be written up as evidence about the watchdog when it is actually evidence about this constructor.

Anyone picking up LOCAL18 should land this first or pin their backend to `local` for the duration.

## Scope

Pass `memory_floor_pct=self._cfg.summarization.local_memory_floor_pct` at `summarize.py:806`, matching the other three sites.

Add a test that walks every production `LocalSummaryClient` construction and asserts each threads the configured floor, in the shape of `test_entry_contract.py`'s dispatch walk, so a fifth construction cannot forget. Note that `test_entry_contract.py`'s own walk is a substring test and CI6 covers strengthening it; this new test should assert on the constructor call rather than on source text.

Correct the ARCH5 spec's inventory, which records three constructions where there are four. Decide separately whether `dogfood.py`'s three constructions (`:106`, `:147`, `:154`) should honour the floor or stay on the default, since `MP_RAM_GUARD=0` is the documented bench escape.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A config with a non-default floor and `backend = "auto"` produces a fallback client carrying that floor. The new test fails against today's code. LOCAL18's spec gains a line naming this as a prerequisite for its first leg.

**[DONE] PIPE17 (P2): the channel-aware finalize branch still hand-rolls `write_text`, which PIPE8 recorded as converted.** Shipped 2026-08-15. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close; it was implemented as written, and the ToC row records the test shape and one environment finding that came out of it.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Medium, spot-checked.

## What is wrong

`storage.atomic_write_text` backs only the already-labelled branch of the finalize stage. The channel-aware / mono fallback branch writes the transcript non-atomically, so a kill mid-write leaves a truncated `<stem>.json` or `<stem>.md` rather than the prior file intact.

- `pipeline/src/mp/orchestrate.py:738-739` are `json_path.write_text(...)` and `md_path.write_text(...)`, followed by `os.chmod(..., 0o600)` at `:741-742`. That is exactly the `write_text` + `chmod` pair the helper exists to replace.
- `pipeline/src/mp/orchestrate.py:704` is the other branch of the same function, 34 lines above, using `storage.atomic_write_text`.
- `pipeline/CLAUDE.md:40` states the rule: "**Rewriting the only copy of a transcript/summary is atomic.** ... Used by `orchestrate` finalize + glossary, `summarize`, and `merge_meetings` (PIPE8). Don't hand-roll `write_text` + `chmod` for content files."
- `docs/backlog/q6-final.md:404` is the shipped-work record claiming the conversion covered `orchestrate._finalize_streamed_transcript`. Only half of it happened.

The branch is live rather than theoretical: the owner's `pipeline.log` carries 23 occurrences of "Finalized transcript:" (the log line at `orchestrate.py:743`, unique to this branch) and 20 of "Stereo recording; channel-aware speaker labelling at finalization" against 172 "FluidAudio sidecar already labelled segments", so it runs on roughly one recording in eight.

Failure shape: FluidAudio labels fewer than half the segments (mono input, or a diarization miss), so finalize takes this branch. `PipelineLauncher`'s watchdog SIGKILLs a wedged run-all, or the Mac loses power, while `md_path.write_text` is partway through. A retry's `mp run-all` then reads the truncated file and summarizes half a meeting, and neither the no-speech guard nor the suspect-transcript guard fires on a partial file.

## Scope

Replace the `write_text` + `os.chmod` pair at `orchestrate.py:738-742` with two `storage.atomic_write_text` calls, matching the sibling branch.

Re-check `q6-final.md:404`'s PIPE8 entry, since its acceptance text asserts a conversion that only half happened. Correct it to record what actually shipped, per the archive's role as the trail.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A test pins **both** finalize branches through the helper, since the existing PIPE8 storage tests only cover the labelled path, which is how this survived. The archive entry is corrected in the same commit.

**[DONE] PIPE16 (P2): `require_env`'s `sys.exit(2)` escapes run-all's handlers, so a publish-stage secret failure leaves the row reading "Ready".** Shipped 2026-08-15. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close; its acceptance asks for exit 3 and surviving sibling sinks in one scenario, which are mutually exclusive, and the ToC row records how each was pinned instead.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Proposed high, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic on the recovery available to the user.

## What is wrong

`require_env` calls `sys.exit(2)` from inside `publish_router._build_one`. `SystemExit` derives from `BaseException`, not `Exception`, so it passes straight through both of orchestrate's handlers, skipping the `run_failed` event, the exit-3 mapping and the `<stem>.publish.json` write. The daemon then sees exit 2 over a meeting whose summary is already on disk.

- `pipeline/src/mp/config.py:458` is `sys.exit(2)` inside `require_env`, called as library code rather than from a CLI main.
- `pipeline/src/mp/publish_router.py:82` is `token = require_env("NOTION_TOKEN")`, reached from `build_publishers`, which `fanout` calls at `publish_router.py:135` before any publisher runs and before `_write_publish_sidecar`.
- `pipeline/src/mp/orchestrate.py:275` and `:766` are both `except Exception`, so the `run_failed` emit at `:276` and the `return EXIT_PUBLISH_FAILED` at `:774` are both unreachable on this path. Verified by running the same try/except/finally shape under uv: `SystemExit escaped main with code: 2`.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Coordination/SinkDispatcher.swift:469` maps only exit 3 to `.publish`; exit 2 falls to `.pipeline`, whose retry re-runs the summarizer instead of republishing the summary already on disk.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingStore.swift:578` makes a row `.done` when a summary is present, and `:553` suppresses the failure sidecar entirely in that case, so the durable row settles on **"Ready"** for a meeting that published nowhere.

This also contradicts the module's own stated contract at `publish_router.py:5`, that one sink's failure must not abort the rest: a missing `NOTION_TOKEN` kills the Obsidian and filesystem sinks configured alongside it.

## The skeptic's narrowing, recorded

The user is not left entirely in the dark at the time: the notification body carries the full "$NOTION_TOKEN is not set" stderr tail, and both the row context menu and the detail toolbar offer a summary-only Republish, so recovery is cheap. The surviving harm is a wrong **durable** row plus a lost publish sidecar, not a silent failure with only an expensive retry. Note the repo already pins this behaviour as intended for the summarize path at `pipeline/tests/test_summarize_backend.py:51-59` ("require_env raises SystemExit(2) by design, fail-fast for missing secrets"), so the fix must not break that intent at the CLI boundary.

## Scope

Make `require_env` raise a named exception (`MissingSecretError`) instead of calling `sys.exit`, and let each `main` translate it to the exit code that command owes: 2 at the CLI boundary, preserving the fail-fast intent the existing test pins, and `EXIT_PUBLISH_FAILED` from the publish stage in `orchestrate`, `publish_cmd`, `publish_from_paste` and `merge_meetings` after recording the outcome, so the row gets the publish-only retry it deserves.

The alternative, and it is worth considering as the smaller change: have `build_publishers` treat an unreadable required token the way it already treats an empty `obsidian.vault_path`, warn and skip that sink, so the others still run. That honours `publish_router.py:5`'s stated contract directly.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A test drives a publish stage with a required secret missing and asserts the process exits 3, emits `run_failed`, writes `<stem>.publish.json`, and that the other configured sinks still ran. The existing `test_summarize_backend.py` fail-fast expectation still passes.

**[DONE] PIPE15 (P2): the Anthropic summarize path has no shared coercion and its one retry is blind.** Shipped 2026-08-15. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Proposed high, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic on measured impact.

## What is wrong

`AnthropicSummaryClient.summarize` validates the tool payload directly with no coercion for a section that arrived as a JSON-encoded string instead of a list, and its single retry re-issues a byte-identical request with no error feedback, so the same malformed reply can recur and the run dies.

- `pipeline/src/mp/summarize.py:399` is `return MeetingSummary.model_validate(tool_blocks[0].input)`, sending raw tool input straight to pydantic. The shared recovery helper `json_extract.parse_summary` is never used on this path.
- `pipeline/src/mp/summarize.py:366-406` builds an identical `messages` payload on both attempts, with no ValidationError replayed to the model, and `:406` is `raise last_err`.
- `pipeline/src/mp/schemas.py:150-160` shows `normalize_model_summary` returning the payload untouched unless a section is a list containing dicts, so a `str` section passes through unrepaired to the strict `list[str]` field at `schemas.py:187`.

Reproduced against today's tree on 2026-08-03: `MeetingSummary.model_validate({"summary": json.dumps(["a","b"]), ...})` still raises `list_type`, including when `decisions` arrives in the post-FEAT10 object shape so `normalize_model_summary` actually executes.

The local backend has three recovery layers plus `summarize_local.repair_messages`, which replays the pydantic error to the model. The cloud path, which is the shipped default (`config.py:122`), has neither.

## Measured impact, stated honestly

It has fired three times on the owner's real corpus: `pipeline.log:472` (2026-05-22, `summary`), `:1195` (2026-06-10, `questions`), and `:2925` (2026-07-20, `summary`). Two of the three recovered only because the blind attempt-2 re-roll happened to come back well-formed, at the cost of a second paid model call.

One killed a run: `20260720-130337.error.json` exists with no sibling `.summary.json`. The skeptic checked what that meeting was and it is a 78-second non-meeting whose entire transcript is the word "Who". So **no meeting content has been lost to this**, and the failed row keeps a working Retry. That is why it is medium rather than high. The mechanism is real, the wasted paid call is real, and the next occurrence could land on a real meeting.

## Scope

Add a coercion to `normalize_model_summary`, which is the file's own designated home for a transform every backend must share: when a section or `attendees` arrives as a string that `json.loads` to a list, use the decoded list. Leave everything else untouched so the normalizer stays idempotent on the stored shape.

Separately, make the Anthropic attempt-2 replay carry the ValidationError back to the model the way `summarize_local.repair_messages` does, instead of re-issuing an identical request. That is the cheaper half and it fixes the whole class rather than one shape.

Fix `summarize.py`'s module docstring, which still describes a recovery ladder this path does not have.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A schemas test pins a stringified section round-tripping to a list. A summarize test pins that attempt 2 differs from attempt 1 and carries the validation error. No owner walkthrough: the trigger is a model behaviour the owner cannot summon on demand.

**[DONE] PIPE14 (P2): publish state is read from `run.json` while every document names `publish.json`.** Shipped 2026-08-15. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close; two corrections to it are recorded in the ToC row (the `MeetingStore.swift:708-711` reference is the property doc at `:108-111`, and there is a seventh reader, `AudioRetentionSweep.swift:128`, that the filing missed).

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Found independently by the pipeline-contracts angle and the doc-truth angle. Proposed high by both, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic on reachability.

## What is wrong

`Meeting.publishState` has exactly one assignment and it reads the run sidecar, not the publish sidecar. Only `mp run-all` ever writes a fresh value, so `mp publish`, `mp merge-meetings` and `mp publish-from-paste` all rewrite `<stem>.publish.json` and leave the value the whole Library branches on frozen at its previous state.

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingStore.swift:661` is `publishState: (run?["publish_state"] as? String),`.
- `pipeline/src/mp/orchestrate.py:533` is `set_publish_state(sidecar, publish_state(pub))`, the only site that writes a fresh value. `summarize.py:913` merely carries the prior value forward.
- `pipeline/src/mp/publish_cmd.py` contains no `set_publish_state` call anywhere in the file. `merge_meetings.py:236-241` ends at `publish_fanout` with none either.
- The six branch sites all read the run-sourced value: `MeetingRow.swift:277` and `:278` (the retry-vs-publish action), `MeetingRow.swift:198` (the badge), `AudioRetention.swift:59` (`isSettled`, so a stale value keeps the audio forever), `LibraryScope.swift:134` (Needs-you membership), `MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:209` and `:212`.

Four documents assert the other file:

- `ARCHITECTURE.md:496` calls `<stem>.publish.json` "this run's publish outcome ... Rewritten every run, so it is never stale (PIPE1)".
- `CONVENTIONS.md:360` attributes the six literal-comparing branch sites to `publish.json`'s `state`.
- `daemon/CLAUDE.md:30` instructs "Read `<stem>.publish.json` via `PublishResult.load` (PIPE1)".
- `MeetingStore.swift:708-711`'s own doc comment repeats it.

## Reachability, stated honestly

The skeptic checked the owner's disk and the loop has never been reachable in this configuration: `"partial"` needs two or more sinks and every workflow the owner has recorded under has exactly one, and `"none"` has never once been written (95 of 95 run sidecars and 37 of 37 publish sidecars read `"full"`). Publish has also never failed here: 0 non-residue `publisher.sink_failed` rows across 173 `sink_started` / `sink_completed` pairs.

So this is a latent trap plus a live documentation lie, not an active bug. It is filed at medium because the trap arms the moment a second sink is configured or a publish fails, and because four documents currently instruct the next reader to believe the opposite of the code.

## Scope

Pick one source of truth and delete the other read. Either have `publish_cmd`, `merge_meetings` and `publish_from_paste` call `corrections.set_publish_state` after `fanout` the way `orchestrate.py:533` does, or change `MeetingStore` to source `publishState` from `PublishResult.load` and fall back to the run sidecar only when `publish.json` is absent. The second is closer to what every document already claims and to what `daemon/CLAUDE.md:30` instructs.

Then correct `ARCHITECTURE.md:496`, `CONVENTIONS.md:356-360`, `daemon/CLAUDE.md:30`, `MeetingStore.swift:708-711` and `summarize.py:890-893` so they name the file the branches genuinely read.

Note the interaction with UX62, which fixes the sibling blindness in `needsRepublish`. Both are about the Library inferring publish outcome from the wrong file, and both should reuse whatever helper lands first.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A test drives a run that publishes to zero sinks, then a successful `mp publish`, and asserts the Library's derived publish state reflects the second outcome. The cross-tree golden fixture that CI4 pins covers whichever file becomes the source of truth. The five doc sites are corrected in the same commit.

**[DONE] REC9 (P1): the stop-time merge truncates the recording to the shorter capture channel, then deletes the only recoverable copy.** Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band as its only critical finding, confirmed by an independent skeptic and reproduced by hand. Shipped and closed 2026-08-05. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close.

**Closed 2026-08-05 by owner decision, with the walkthrough's step 3 recorded as unperformable rather than left owed.** Step 3 asks the owner to deny Screen Recording, start a recording, and re-enable the permission *while still recording*. That cannot be done: changing the Screen Recording grant restarts the app, so re-enabling it kills the recording the step exists to test. The step was written without accounting for that, and it is the HYG6 class of walkthrough that cannot pass. It is recorded here so nobody re-files the missing check as a gap.

What carries the close instead: the head-offset path is pinned by three tests that drive **real ffmpeg** and decode the produced WAV per channel, including the audit's exact repro (10 s mic plus 3 s system gave 3.000000 s before and gives 10.000000 s now, with the system channel silent outside the window it was captured in) and a late-starting system channel landing at its correct offset rather than at sample 0. The filter was verified against real ffmpeg 8.1 before any Swift was written. What step 3 would have added is end-to-end confidence through the daemon's own capture path, not confidence in the filter or the offset arithmetic. Step 2 (a normal recording plays back at full length) remains performable and is the regression check if anyone wants one.

One thing the fix does not cover, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: REC10's retry path still overwrites the pre-loss system partial, because `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` truncates. REC9 improves that case without fixing it, since a retry's audio now merges where the retry actually happened rather than at sample 0, but the audio the retry overwrote is still lost. REC10 stays open.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Severity critical, confirmed by an independent skeptic and reproduced by hand.

## Progress (2026-08-05, shipped; owner-owed walkthrough)

All four scope items ship. Daemon suite green, **2377 tests, 21 new** (15 `RecordingPostProcessorTests`, 6 `RecordingDurationParityTests`); `swift build` clean; `truth_fences.py both` clean. The two new event actions (`recorder`/`merge_too_short`, `recorder`/`duration_parity_low`) sit in the existing `recorder` category, so the fence needed no table edit.

**The length policy is `RecordingPostProcessor.mergeLengths`, and it is pure.** `apad` on each leg so neither can end the merge, `adelay` on the system leg for a late start, and `-t` at `max(mic, offset + system)`. Verified against real ffmpeg 8.1 before writing any Swift: the shipped filter turned a 10 s mic plus a 3 s system into 3.000000 s, the new one into 10.000000 s with the right channel silent outside the window it was captured in. Both shapes are exercised end to end by tests that decode the produced WAV per channel rather than trusting its duration alone.

**The head offset is measured, not inferred.** `MeetingRecorder` marks `systemUptime` at start and at the first frame written into the system WAV *as it currently stands*: the mark is cleared in `startSystemCapture`, not at `start()`, because `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` truncates, so what the merge needs is where the audio the file actually holds begins. Offsets below 1.0 s are dropped as the routine CAP1 skew (median 0.21 s over 153 recordings), so no normal recording moves. The offset also lands in the `intermediate_durations` event as `head_offset_sec`, since the existing `delta_sec` cannot tell a channel that stopped early from one that started late.

**The promote gate fails closed.** `outputIsPlausible` keeps REC1's 4 KiB floor and adds the duration check against the policy's target, with a 0.5 s tolerance for resampler rounding. An output that cannot be measured is refused rather than promoted. The refusal path is the one that already existed, so it keeps both intermediates and writes `.recordfail.json`, now with a `reason` that names the shortfall in seconds. Pinned end to end with a stand-in ffmpeg that exits 0 having written a short file, which is exactly the shape the byte floor waved through: a clean exit status is not evidence that the audio survived.

**The parity warning is visible.** `RecordingDurationParity` is the pure verdict (same family as `RemoteAudioWarning` and `MicCoverageWarning`), snapshotted at stop into `lastDurationParity`; `MeetingSessionController` raises a "Recording is shorter than the meeting" notice and `checkDurationParity` emits `duration_parity_low`, so `mp logs` and the Diagnostics viewer both see it.

**Three corrections, and what they turned out to be.** `MeetingRecorder.swift`'s "the ffmpeg merge pads to the longer input" and `RemoteAudioWarning.interrupted`'s "absent from the death point on" were both false when written and are **true as of this commit**, because the policy makes them true; each now says so and names what re-breaks it, which is more useful than deleting a claim the code finally honours. `Notifier`'s interrupted-capture body ("the recording is mic-only from that point") is the same case and keeps its wording for the same reason, with the dependency recorded above it.

**Scope held to REC9.** REC10 (the retry path overwriting the system partial) is untouched and still open. Its scenario does improve here without being fixed: because the offset is keyed to the file's own first frame, a retry's audio is now merged where the retry happened instead of at sample 0. The audio the retry overwrote is still lost, which is REC10's defect.

## What is wrong

`RecordingPostProcessor.mergeToTempViaFFmpeg` builds a bare `amerge` with no length policy, so the merged `<stem>.wav` ends where the **shorter** of `mic.wav` / `system.wav` ends. `produceFinal` then verifies only that the output exceeds 4096 bytes, promotes it onto the canonical path, and deletes both intermediates, so whatever the merge dropped is unrecoverable.

Reproduced on this Mac on 2026-08-03 with the exact filter and arg vector from `RecordingPostProcessor.swift:194-208`: a 10.000000 s mono mic plus a 3.000000 s stereo system produced a **3.000000 s** output at 192,078 bytes. `ffmpeg -h filter=amerge` on ffmpeg 8.1 lists only `inputs` and `layout_mode`, so no length policy is even expressible in that filter.

Evidence:

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/RecordingPostProcessor.swift:197` is `[micL][sysR]amerge=inputs=2[stereo]`, carrying no `apad`, no `duration=longest`, no `-shortest` and no `-t`.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/RecordingPostProcessor.swift:66` is `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) && fileSize(url) > 4096`, the only verification before promotion. A truncated merge passes it trivially at 192 KB.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/RecordingPostProcessor.swift:173` shows `promoteMerged` gating on that same byte predicate, so the promote step adds no independent check.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/RecordingPostProcessor.swift:131-132` deletes `mic.wav` and `system.wav` the moment `promoteMerged` returns true.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1260` reads `// system.wav is fine - the ffmpeg merge pads to the longer input.` That comment asserts the exact opposite of the measured behaviour, and it is what licenses every short-`system.wav` path.

## What it has actually cost

Measured across the owner's whole event-log history on 2026-08-03, 153 `intermediate_durations` rows:

- 140 of 153 recordings have `system.wav` shorter than `mic.wav`, so the tail of the owner's own mic channel is discarded on nearly every recording.
- Total mic audio discarded: 77.3 s. Median per affected recording: 0.21 s. That routine case is the CAP1 skew and is harmless.
- The tail is not harmless. On 2026-07-15 the SCStream start failed on TCC and system capture only came up at 14:28:42. At stop, `mic_audio_sec` was 41.2 and `system_audio_sec` was 5.28, `delta_sec` -35.92. The merge kept 5.28 s, which is **87 percent of the meeting destroyed**.
- That run was recorded as a clean success: `recording_stopped {produced_final: true}`, then `engine_succeeded {audio_seconds: 5.28, segments: 1}`. The published transcript is one line. The intermediates are gone from disk.
- The only detector fired into a text log and nowhere else: `MeetingRecorder.swift:1607` writes `WARN: WAV is <n>% of recording wallclock` via `Log.writeLine`, with no `Log.event`, so it is invisible to `mp logs`, to the Diagnostics viewer and to the user.

The `docs/spikes/dep1-avfoundation-vs-ffmpeg.md:42` spike found this divergence on 2026-07-11 and dismissed it, reasoning that in production both channels span the same wall-clock window so the delta is the small CAP1 skew. The event log refutes that premise: 140 of 153 recordings disagree, and one by 35.9 s. CAP1's own promotion trigger is skew magnitude rather than audio loss, so it never fired on this.

## Scope

Give the merge an explicit length policy so the final is never shorter than the longer capture channel. Padding the tail alone is not sufficient: a channel that starts late (the 2026-07-15 shape) needs its head offset handled explicitly, or the recovered audio lands against the wrong mic timestamps.

Strengthen `producedPlausibleOutput` from a byte count to a duration check against `max(audioDurationSec(mic), audioDurationSec(system))` with a tolerance, so an under-length merge fails, keeps both intermediates, and writes a `.recordfail.json` breadcrumb instead of promoting.

Promote `checkDurationParity`'s ratio warning from a bare `Log.writeLine` to a `Log.event` plus a user-visible notice, so a future occurrence is diagnosable and the user knows.

Fix `MeetingRecorder.swift:1260`'s comment in the same commit, and correct `Notifier.swift:272`'s interrupted-capture copy, which tells the user the recording continues mic-only past the loss when in fact it ends at the loss. `MeetingSessionController.swift:557`'s `RemoteAudioWarning.interrupted` rationale rests on the same false premise.

Related: REC10 covers the sibling defect on the retry path, and its fix shares this one's offset handling. Pick them up together.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A merge fed a 10 s mic and a 3 s system produces a 10 s final with the system channel silent where it had no audio, and a merge fed a system channel that starts late places its audio at the correct offset rather than at sample 0. An under-length merge result is refused by the plausibility check, keeps both intermediates, and leaves a `.recordfail.json`. A ratio-parity failure emits an event. The three doc and comment corrections above land in the same commit.

## Owner walkthrough

Steps tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Record a short meeting normally and stop it. Pass: the recording plays back at its full length, both sides audible, nothing different from today.
3. [owner] The case that matters, and it needs Screen Recording denied at the start. Open System Settings, Privacy and Security, Screen and System Audio Recording, and turn MeetingPipe **off**. Start a recording, talk for about 20 seconds, then turn the permission back **on** while still recording, talk for another 20 seconds, and stop.
4. [owner] Open the meeting in the Library. Pass: the recording is about 40 seconds long and your voice is present for the whole of it, including the first 20 seconds when system capture was unavailable. Before this fix that recording would have been about 20 seconds and the first half of your own audio would be gone.
5. [owner] Say "REC9 good to close" or what is wrong.

**[DONE] REC10 (P2): the REC8 auto-retry overwrites the system-audio partial that REC4 and REC8 both claim it preserves.** Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Shipped and closed 2026-08-14. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close, followed by what actually landed.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Proposed high, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic on reachability, and the mechanism confirmed.

## What is wrong

`retrySystemAudio()` re-enters `startSystemCapture(systemURL:)` with the same URL, and `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` truncates an existing file, so a recovery after a mid-meeting SCStream death destroys every system-audio sample captured before the death. The recovered channel then begins at retry time but merges at sample 0, so the remote side plays back early by the outage offset.

Evidence:

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:613-620` re-enters `startSystemCapture(systemURL: systemURL, isRetry: true)` with `self.systemURL`, the same path `start()` used.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:528-531` opens it with `systemFile = try AVAudioFile(forWriting: systemURL, settings: ...)`. The overwrite is Apple's documented contract, not an inference: `AVAudioFile.h:68` in the macOS SDK reads "Will overwrite a file at the given URL".
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:703` documents `handleSystemAudioLost`'s contract as keeping the partial "on disk so a no-retry stop still merges what was captured", and `:715` clears only `systemCapture`, deliberately leaving `systemFile` and `systemWriter` pointing at the partial. That is exactly what the retry then overwrites.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:720` calls `scheduleSystemAudioAutoRetry()`, which REC8 made hands-off, so no human decision stands between a death and the overwrite.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:697-698` takes the same path from `handleDidWake`, which is REC8 walkthrough step 3's exact scenario.
- `docs/backlog/tasks/REC8.md:5` asserts the retry "preserves REC4's partial-recording rationale". It does not.

## Reachability, stated honestly

This path has never executed on the owner's machine. `system_capture_lost`, `system_capture_stall_detected` and `system_capture_auto_retry` are each **0** across `events.jsonl` and `events.1.jsonl`. That is why the skeptic downgraded it from high to medium, and the downgrade is correct: the defect is real in code and unobserved in practice. It is filed because the trigger is a designed-for state (REC4 exists for it) and because the cost when it does fire is silent loss of the remote half of a meeting.

## Scope

On a retry, do not reopen the same path. Two shapes work:

- Write the recovered stream to a numbered sibling (`<stem>.system.2.wav`) and teach `produceFinal` to concatenate the system legs with a silence gap before the merge.
- Or pre-pad the new file with silence covering the outage window so sample 0 still means recording start.

The offset handling is shared with REC9's length policy. REC9 shipped 2026-08-05 (see [q6-final.md](./q6-final.md)) and stands alone, so this is no longer a joint pickup: `RecordingPostProcessor.mergeLengths` already applies `adelay` for a late-starting system channel, and the head offset is measured from `systemUptime` at start against the first frame written into the system WAV as it currently stands, with the mark cleared in `startSystemCapture` precisely because `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` truncates. Build on that rather than reinventing it. Note what REC9 did and did not change here: a retry's audio now merges at the offset where the retry actually happened rather than at sample 0, but the pre-loss audio the retry overwrote is still lost, which is this task's whole subject.

Fix `handleSystemAudioLost`'s doc comment and `REC8.md:5`'s preservation claim in the same commit.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A test drives `handleSystemAudioLost` then `retrySystemAudio` over a fake file sink and asserts the pre-loss bytes survive and the post-retry frames land at the right offset. Not owner-verifiable without killing an SCStream mid-call, so this closes on tests alone, and the spec says so rather than pre-registering an observation the owner cannot make. It previously said it would close on tests plus REC9's walkthrough; that leg is gone, because REC9 closed 2026-08-05 with its walkthrough step 3 recorded as **unperformable**: changing the Screen Recording grant restarts the app, so the permission cannot be re-enabled mid-recording. Do not re-introduce an owner step of that shape here.

## Shipped (2026-08-14)

`SystemCaptureRetryPlanner` is the pure decision a retry runs: resume the WAV the dead SCStream left open, or open the path fresh. Only the fresh branch may truncate, and it is reached exactly where truncating costs nothing (the first start, and a retry after an initial SCStream failure, which deletes the path and drops the writer). On a resume the outage is padded with silence before the stream restarts, through `CaptureRecoveryPlanner.silenceFrames`, which grew a measured-span entry point so the mic's device-switch pad and this one share one piece of gap arithmetic rather than two.

Neither of the two shapes the spec offered was taken, and the reason is worth recording. Numbered legs plus a concatenating merge would have touched `produceFinal`, `mergeLengths` and `recoverOrphan`, and orphan recovery has no head offsets to place a leg with, so a crash would have left legs it could only guess at. Keeping the file open instead is confined to `MeetingRecorder`: `produceFinal`, `mergeLengths` and `recoverOrphan` are untouched, the single `<stem>.system.wav` carries pre-loss audio then silence then recovered audio in order, and REC9's head offset keeps meaning what it meant, because the file's first frame never moved.

Three second-order holes closed with it. The SCStream-start-failure branch deleted the file and dropped the writer unconditionally, so a failed *retry* would have destroyed the same partial from the other side; it now tears down only a file that holds nothing. `systemFirstFrameUptime` is cleared in `openSystemFile` rather than on every entry, so a resume keeps the offset that places its audio. And `handleSystemAudioLost` dates the loss, with the watchdog path dating it to when the audio actually stopped (`now - stallAfter`) rather than to the ~1 Hz tick that noticed, so the pad matches the hole.

A gap past 300 s is padded to that ceiling and reported as clamped, in `system_capture_resumed`. The pad is real audio (48 kHz stereo Float32, ~384 KB/s), so an unbounded pad is a disk-usage defect; a silently clamped one would be the same silent misplacement this task was filed against, wearing a fix.

**The acceptance test is substituted, and this is the substitution.** The spec asked for a test driving `handleSystemAudioLost` then `retrySystemAudio` over a fake sink; both need a live recorder, which needs an AVAudioEngine and an SCStream to kill. Split instead the way this codebase splits such things: the decision is pure and pinned (8 tests, including the clamp and both degenerate clock cases), and the two claims that carry the fix are pinned against real files on disk. `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` destroying an existing recording is measured rather than quoted from `AVAudioFile.h`, and a resumed handle is driven through a real `SerialBufferWriter` and read back to assert the pre-loss samples survived whole, the outage reads as silence, and the recovered audio starts after both rather than at sample 0. Writing those tests found one thing worth keeping: an `AVAudioFile` write handle buffers, so its `length` reports a flushed count (4096 for 4800 written) and the header is invalid until every strong reference is released, which is the same reason `stop()` drops the file handles before ffmpeg reads.

Verification: `swift build` clean, daemon suite 2411 tests 0 failures (15 new across this task and REC11), truth fences clean. Still 0 `system_capture_lost` / `system_capture_stall_detected` / `system_capture_auto_retry` in the whole log, so this closes on tests alone, as the spec pre-registered. Docs: `ARCHITECTURE.md` (new module bullet in Recording), `daemon/CLAUDE.md` (Recording index row + a Don't entry covering the truncate trap and the buffered-`length` read), `REC8.md:5`'s preservation claim and `handleSystemAudioLost`'s doc comment, all in the same commit. Checked and unchanged: `README.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `design/` - no user-visible control, flow, schema, event category or UI surface moved.

**[DONE] REC11 (P2): recorder teardown concurrency, an unbounded drain on the quit path and an off-main `stop()`.** Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Shipped and closed 2026-08-14. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close, followed by what actually landed.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Two defects in one teardown path, medium, spot-checked.

## (a) The quit path uses the unbounded `finish()` REC7 replaced everywhere else

`flushIntermediatesForTermination` is `@MainActor` and calls `SerialBufferWriter.finish()` with no timeout, while `stop()` calls the REC7 bounded `finish(timeout:)` for the same drain on the same writers. The wedge REC7 exists to bound is therefore still unbounded on the one path that runs during `applicationWillTerminate` and the SIGTERM handler.

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1485-1486` calls `micWriter?.finish()` and `systemWriter?.finish()` inside the `@MainActor` flush declared at `:1445`.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/SerialBufferWriter.swift:27-28` is `func finish() {` over `queue.sync {}`, an unbounded block on the writer's serial queue.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1311` is the graceful path's bounded variant.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:45-47` is the project's own risk model naming this exact drain as a thing that can wedge.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1440-1441` claims the flush is "Deadlock-free: the only blocking calls are the writers' own serial queues, never the main queue." That is true about deadlock and quietly does not cover an indefinite block.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Coordinator.swift:603-605` calls it synchronously from `applicationWillTerminate` and the SIGTERM source.

Failure shape: the disk fills, or an external volume holding `~/Documents/Meetings/raw` stalls, while a recording is live. The owner quits, or `rebuild.sh` sends SIGTERM, and the app blocks forever on the main thread. The launch agent cannot relaunch it and the owner has to force-quit, which is exactly the situation where the intermediates the flush was protecting are least likely to be intact.

## (b) `stop()` is nonisolated async, so the teardown races the main-thread owners of its own fields

Per SE-0338 a nonisolated async function does not inherit the caller's actor, so `await recorder.stop()` from the `Task { @MainActor }` in `stopRecording` runs the whole teardown off the main thread.

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1214` is `func stop() async -> Bool {` with no `@MainActor`, unlike `start` (`:320`), `unwindFailedEngineStart` (`:496`), `recoverCapture` (`:961`) and `flushIntermediatesForTermination` (`:1445`).
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1279-1280` states in a comment that `stop()` is off-main, so this is the intended reading rather than a misread.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1236-1246` writes the four timer handles, the wake observer and the idle-sleep assertion off-main.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:1440` claims the flush is "Main-thread only (it mutates the recorder state the render path also touches)", i.e. exclusive main-thread ownership of the very fields `stop()` writes off-main.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:664-668` guards `IOPMAssertionRelease(idleSleepAssertionID)` with a non-atomic `guard holdsIdleSleepAssertion`, reachable from both the off-main `stop()` and the `@MainActor` flush, so a double release is possible.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRecorder.swift:729-731` schedules a 1 Hz `checkSystemLiveness` on the main queue whose only interlock with the off-main teardown is timing.

## Scope

For (a): use `finish(timeout:)` in `flushIntermediatesForTermination`, with a termination-specific budget since `applicationWillTerminate` has its own OS deadline, log a `writer_drain_timed_out` event on the abandoned path exactly as `stop()` does, and correct the "Deadlock-free" comment to say what it actually guarantees.

For (b): mark `stop()` `@MainActor` and keep only the genuinely long waits off-main, since the SCStream stop, the writer drains and `RecordingPostProcessor.produceFinal` are already `async` and bounded and can be awaited from the main actor without blocking it. If that cascades further than is comfortable, the smaller fix is to hop the teardown block through `MainActor.run` the way the recovery-task box at `:1275-1281` already does. Delete the contradictory `:1440` claim either way.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. Both suites still pass with strict concurrency. A test pins that the termination flush abandons a wedged writer within its budget and emits the event. No owner walkthrough: neither defect is observable without a wedged disk or a race, and pre-registering an observation the owner cannot make is the failure mode this band was filed against.

## Shipped (2026-08-14)

(a) `flushIntermediatesForTermination` drains with `terminationDrainTimeoutSeconds` (3.0 s) instead of the unbounded `finish()`. Tighter than the graceful path's 10 s on purpose: that path can suspend, this one cannot (it runs under `applicationWillTerminate` and the SIGTERM source), so its budget *is* main-thread freeze time and has to be spent before the OS or `rebuild.sh` stops waiting. An abandoned drain emits `writer_drain_timed_out`, and both emitters now carry a `path` attribute (`stop` / `termination`) so a reader can tell which one gave up; `intermediates_flushed_for_termination` carries `writers_drained` for the same reason. The "Deadlock-free: the only blocking calls are the writers' own serial queues" comment is replaced with what the code now actually guarantees, which is that it cannot deadlock *and* cannot block longer than its budget.

(b) `stop()` is `@MainActor`. The teardown no longer writes the four timer handles, the wake observer and the idle-sleep assertion off the actor the termination flush claims exclusive ownership of, which is precisely what makes `releaseIdleSleepAssertion`'s non-atomic `holdsIdleSleepAssertion` guard sound rather than lucky. The contradictory comments are gone, including `MeetingSessionController`'s "recorder.stop is async (off the UI)".

Marking it `@MainActor` would have been a regression on its own, and that is the part worth knowing: `SerialBufferWriter.finish(timeout:)` blocks its caller, so a wedged disk would have frozen the app for the whole 10 s budget on the one path the user is watching. So the graceful path moved to a new `drain(timeout:)`, same bounded abandon-on-timeout contract, but it parks the semaphore on a global utility thread and suspends the caller. The synchronous `finish(timeout:)` stays for the termination path, which cannot await. With the hop gone, the `@unchecked Sendable` `RecoveryTaskBox` had no reason left to exist (its doc comment said as much: it existed so an off-main `stop()` could reach a main-confined handle) and is a plain stored property again, which is one fewer `@unchecked Sendable` in a target that already carries two it would rather not.

**One acceptance leg is unpinned, named rather than faked.** The spec asked for a test that the termination flush abandons a wedged writer within its budget *and emits the event*. The bound is pinned, on both the synchronous and the async path, over a genuinely wedged handler. The emission from the flush is not: `flushIntermediatesForTermination` returns early unless `currentFile` is set, and only a live `start()` sets it, so reaching it needs an AVAudioEngine. Adding a test-only setter to reach a two-line log call would have asserted less than its presence implied. A third test pins the property `drain` exists for, that awaiting a wedged drain from the main actor leaves the main actor free to run other work.

**Deliberately not done here.** `stop()` now makes its engine teardown (`removeTap` / `engine.stop()`) on main. That is not new isolation for those calls in this app: `recoverCapture` and the termination flush are both `@MainActor` and both already do it. Bounding all of them, plus `MicLevelMonitor.swift:39`, plus surfacing a stuck stop, is REC13's named scope, and it was filed the same day from a live incident where the engine's own serial queue wedged. Doing a third of it here would have left the fix half-applied across three paths and collided with that task.

Verification: `swift build` clean with no new Sendable warnings under `-strict-concurrency=targeted`, daemon suite 2411 tests 0 failures (15 new across this task and REC10), truth fences clean. Docs: `ARCHITECTURE.md` (a teardown-isolation note in Recording), `daemon/CLAUDE.md` (Recording index row naming both writer entry points, plus the Don't entry's second half on two paths draining the same thing differently). Checked and unchanged: `README.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/GUIDE.md`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `design/`.

**[DONE] DET8 (P2): revive per-process mic attribution by enumerating HAL process objects (DET2's close measured the wrong process).** Band origin: filed 2026-07-30 (session finding while re-examining DET2 at the owner's request; owner approved filing the same day). Shipped and closed 2026-08-05. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close, including the build annotations added when it landed.

**Closed by owner decision with the dogfood leg unobserved.** All three legs shipped and every engineering bar is green, but the acceptance's live-log confirmation (that `process_audio_is_running_input` transitions appear on real Teams calls where eight weeks showed zero) had not yet been observed when the owner closed it. That is a real gap in the record rather than a formality: the signal is proven live by the probe, and proven wired by the unit tests, but not yet proven to fire through the daemon's own path in production. Anyone revisiting should grep `process_audio_object_resolved` first, since its `object_count` says whether matching worked at all.

## Where this stands (read this first)

**All three legs shipped 2026-08-05, in one commit. The only thing still owed is an owner observation over the next few dogfood days.**

- **Leg 1, the owner-run live-call probe: RUN TWICE, GO.** B1 pass, B3 pass, B2 pass (informational, not part of the gate). Both runs' output, the per-run verdicts, the mute confirmation and the churn finding are in `docs/spikes/det2-process-tap-attribution.md`'s DET8 amendment. Churn was a pre-registered open question and is now answered: ModuleHost held the same object ID and PID across both calls, but `replayd` re-registered under a new ID, which is why the resolver caches and refreshes on a list change rather than assuming IDs are permanent.
- **Leg 2, the build: DONE.** `ProcessAudioSignal` resolves by enumerate-and-match instead of translating `context.pid`, ORs `isRunningInput` across matches, subscribes a listener per matched object plus one on the process-object list, and re-resolves lazily (once per unresolved streak, or on a list change) rather than per poll. `usesProcessAudio` is true for Teams and Zoom, and `processAudioIsRunningInput` carries `requiresCorroboration == true`.
- **Leg 3, the record corrections: DONE.** `ProcessAudioSignal.swift`'s header, `NativeLifecycleAdapter.swift`'s `usesProcessAudio` comment, `InputDeviceIdentity.swift`'s end-signal note, `LifecycleAdapterTests` (renamed to `test_process_audio_is_enabled_with_the_corroboration_rail`), `tasks/DET6.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s signals bullet, and the three `MeetingPipe`-target scanner comments.

**Still owed, and the reason the ToC row is `owner-owed` rather than `done`:** the acceptance asks that within a few days of dogfood, `events.jsonl` shows `process_audio_is_running_input` transitions on real Teams calls where eight weeks showed zero, and that `process_audio_unresolved` stops being the steady state. That is an observation over time, not a build step. `process_audio_object_resolved` (new in this task) is the fastest thing to grep for: it carries `object_count`, so it says whether matching worked at all before you go looking for transitions.

### Three decisions taken during the build that the spec did not pre-decide

1. **Webex and Slack stay `usesProcessAudio: false`.** The spec says "flip on the native `NativeLifecycleConfig`s" without naming which. Cisco holds the mic open post-call for ultrasound device discovery, a carve-out that predates DET2 and that an input read cannot see around; neither app was covered by the probe (Teams only); and `Coordinator` builds both adapters without a `halBus`, which a true flag requires. Flipping either needs its own measurement.
2. **The start-side scanner corroborator was NOT revived**, though this spec's Leg 2 says "the scanner corroborator revives with no change". That sentence is stale: it rests on the Context section's claim that `MeetingSourceScanner.collectSignals` "already calls `ProcessAudioSignal.defaultProbe` and feeds the scorer", and the DET2 cleanup had already deleted both the probe call and the scorer's disjunct, so there is nothing to revive without writing new code. Re-admitting bare brand-token titles on an audio read is a start-side false-positive question that [DET6](./tasks/DET6.md) owns and gates on its own measurement, and the cost argument got worse rather than better (resolution is now a whole-list enumeration, which per candidate per scan is heavier than the old translate). DET6's spec and the three scanner comments now record this.
3. **A process-object-list listener was added**, which the spec offered as an alternative to the unresolved-streak refresh ("re-resolve on the existing unresolved streak or a list-change notification"). Both shipped, because the probe's `replayd` observation makes the list path load-bearing: a client that tears down and re-registers gets a new object ID, which a streak-only refresh notices late or not at all if the stale ID still reads.

## Context: the DET2 close is refuted, not reopened on a hunch

DET2 closed NO-GO on 2026-07-20: translating the meeting app's PID to a HAL process object returned `object 0, OSStatus 0` under all three mechanisms (Screen Recording grant alone, a live bare process tap, a private aggregate around it), corroborated by 13,419 `process_audio_unresolved` events over eight weeks, and `ProcessAudioSignal` was declared dead by design ("refuted, not untried").

On 2026-07-30 a headless enumeration probe in this repo's own harness, holding **no** TCC grant at all, showed the close measured the wrong process. `kAudioHardwarePropertyProcessObjectList` returned 33 live process objects, including `Microsoft Teams ModuleHost` (bundle `com.microsoft.teams2.modulehost`, the SlimCore media stack MIC8 proved owns the mic and the mute logs, a direct child of the `MSTeams` shell) and the WebView `audio.mojom.AudioService` helpers (`com.microsoft.teams2.helper`). Translating ModuleHost's PID resolved to its object with `OSStatus 0`; translating the shell PID returned `object 0, OSStatus 0`, the exact production failure signature. So the HAL was answering truthfully all along: the **shell** process the daemon detects (`com.microsoft.teams2` via NSWorkspace, the PID in `MeetingLifecycleContext.pid`) never registers as a CoreAudio client, and every one of the 13,419 unresolved reads asked about it. Mechanisms A/B/C never mattered because none of them changed the target. Neither the DET2 probe nor `ProcessAudioSignal` ever enumerated the list; that was the one query that would have exposed this.

Three facts from the 2026-07-30 run, each better than DET2's best case assumed: (1) enumeration and the per-object boolean reads (`kAudioProcessPropertyPID` / `BundleID` / `IsRunning` / `IsRunningInput` / `IsRunningOutput`) resolve with **no TCC grant**, from a disclaimed harness shell, so the daemon-side read is zero-setup (the det2 TCC caveat voids negative probe results, never positive ones); (2) every Teams audio helper carries the `com.microsoft.teams2` bundle prefix and ModuleHost is a direct child of the detected shell PID, so matching is a bundle-prefix check with PID ancestry as fallback; (3) the booleans are live (the MeetingPipe daemon itself read `isRunning=true output=true` while resident, and idle processes read `input=false`).

What this buys once revived: a UI-independent, locale-independent, redesign-proof answer to "is this app on the mic right now". Start-side, `MeetingSourceScanner.collectSignals` already calls `ProcessAudioSignal.defaultProbe` and feeds the scorer (weight 3, a `shouldWalkControlAX` precondition, and the required corroborator for bare-brand-token browser titles whose death filed DET6). End-side, `PromotionEngine` already classes `processAudioIsRunningInput` as its own `EndEvidenceClass.processAudio`. The prompt already names the attributed app. Nothing in the fusion vocabulary changes; only the read comes alive.

## Scope

**Leg 1, the owner-run live-call probe (gate).** Instrument: [`daemon/scripts/det8-process-object-probe.swift`](../../daemon/scripts/det8-process-object-probe.swift) (read-only, no taps, no audio). Bars pre-registered 2026-07-30, before any live-call data, in the probe header: **B1** at least one `com.microsoft.teams2*` object reads `isRunningInput=true` within 5 s of joining; **B2** the value stays true across a >= 15 s in-call mute (expected, since client mute is a transmit gate; a flip is recorded, informs the end-leg debounce, and does not kill the task); **B3** every `com.microsoft.teams2*` object reads false within 60 s of leaving. **GO = B1 and B3.** Also record object churn: whether ModuleHost's object ID persists across two calls in one probe run (decides how aggressive re-resolution must be).

**Leg 2, the build (on GO).** Repoint the already-injectable resolution seam in [`ProcessAudioSignal.swift`](../../daemon/Sources/MeetingPipeCore/Lifecycle/Signals/ProcessAudioSignal.swift) (`ProcessObjectResolver` / `defaultProbe`): instead of `translate(context.pid)`, enumerate `kAudioHardwarePropertyProcessObjectList` and match objects whose bundle ID shares the detected app's bundle prefix (fallback: PID ancestry to `context.pid`), OR-ing `isRunningInput` across matches (Teams splits audio across ModuleHost and the WebView audio service; "any of them on the mic" is the question). Subscribe the HAL listener per matched object and re-resolve on the existing unresolved streak or a list-change notification; the 1 Hz poll fallback already exists. Flip `usesProcessAudio` to true on the native `NativeLifecycleConfig`s **together with `requiresCorroboration = true` for `processAudioIsRunningInput`**, the safety rail the DET2 spike pre-registered so a mute- or churn-induced input drop can never solo-confirm an end. The scanner corroborator revives with no change. Browser bundles (e.g. `com.google.Chrome.helper`) match by the same prefix rule against the browser's own bundle, which is exactly the corroborator END5's admission gate wanted and DET6 still wants.

**Leg 3, the record corrections (same commit as leg 2, as filed).** The repo asserted the refuted claim in prose in these places: `ProcessAudioSignal.swift`'s header ("do not re-propose; that hypothesis is refuted, not untried"), `NativeLifecycleAdapter.swift` and `InputDeviceIdentity.swift` comments, `LifecycleAdapterTests.test_process_audio_signal_is_disabled_for_every_provider` (comment and the pin itself, which the flip inverts), and `tasks/DET6.md`'s "DET2 then closed the signal permanently" paragraph. The spike doc `docs/spikes/det2-process-tap-attribution.md` and the det2 probe header carry a dated refutation pointer as of this filing; the rest move with the build.

## Explicitly not in scope

- **A mute oracle.** Client mute is a transmit gate and the OS mic stays live (MIC8's measurement), so `isRunningInput` is expected to stay true while muted. Mute stays MIC8's `LogMuteAdapter` plus the AX read; this task is call-lifecycle and attribution.
- **Taps and aggregate devices.** The 2026-07-30 enumeration resolved bare; DET2's mechanisms B and C stay dead and nothing here creates a tap.
- **Browser detection itself.** DET6 owns the admission gate for non-Meet browser tabs; DET8 only makes the corroborator it lost available again.
- **Re-litigating DET2's archive entry.** The q6-final entry records what was measured then and stands; the refutation lives here and in the spike doc's dated amendment.

Leg 1: the probe's watch-mode output from one real Teams call is pasted into the spike doc's amendment section with a named B1/B2/B3 verdict against the pre-registered bars. On NO-GO (B1 or B3 fails live), this task closes with the measurement recorded and the doc corrections of leg 3 still applied minus the flip (the enumeration fact stands regardless). **Met, and exceeded: two calls rather than one, all three bars passing, GO.**

Leg 2 (on GO): unit tests pin the new resolver (bundle-prefix match hits a modulehost-shaped fixture, ancestry fallback, OR across multiple matched objects, no match resolves to unresolved-with-status); `LifecycleAdapterTests` flips from pinning disabled-everywhere to pinning enabled-with-corroboration-rail (the rail assert is the load-bearing one); both suites and truth fences green (`process_audio_*` events already exist under the `signal` category, no schema change). Within a few days of dogfood, `events.jsonl` shows `process_audio_is_running_input` transitions on real Teams calls where eight weeks showed zero, and `process_audio_unresolved` stops being the steady state.
