**[DONE] LOCAL9 (P2): corrections Phase 3, local LoRA fine-tune.** **Closed 2026-07-30 as the spec's pre-registered honest negative: adapter-not-worth-it, measured three independent ways in the first real run of the loop; `summarization.local_adapter_path` stays unset (owner decision 2026-07-30, formal scorecard grading waived by the owner).** The run: `mp train-adapter --source runs` on the M1 Pro under caffeinate + the <10% free-RAM watchdog. Memory forced `--max-seq-length 8192 --batch-size 1`: a 12288 backward drove 32 GB to 4-5% free at any batch size across the instrumented attempts (two early attempts were additionally contaminated by a v1 watchdog wrapper that killed only `caffeinate` and orphaned the live trainer, so runs briefly overlapped; the v2 wrapper kills the process group), and the `--batch-size` passthrough this surfaced shipped as commit c0d5209. The ceiling cut the corpus from 176 candidate pairs to 42 (train=33, all short meetings; the long information-rich ones are exactly what dropped). 300 iters, ~3 h, checkpoints at 100/200/300. Measurements: train loss memorized to 0.001 while valid-split loss rose monotonically from the untrained 1.173 baseline (1.294 at iter 200, 1.532 at 300); the held-out test triple (base evaluated via a zero-weight adapter, since `mlx_lm.lora --test` unconditionally loads one) read base 1.659 < ckpt-100 1.792 < final-300 2.052; and the `mp dogfood --adapter` A/B on the untrained LOCAL13 anchor `20260723-103118` showed the distillation mechanism itself working (register shifted to cloud-style specificity, 13 actions against 3, the spoken "second three one zero" correctly normalized to ticket 2310) while disqualifying the artifact: zero evidence anchors anywhere (all 42 training pairs are April-June meetings summarized before FEAT10 existed, so the adapter faithfully learned evidence-free output), the one real decision demoted to a question, blanket high confidence, at least one unverifiable ticket number, and ASR garbles promoted to entities (the "Venusaur" ticket; "Irish" as an action owner). Disposition per the spec's own terminal clause: the corpus stays a prompt-context asset, README's Improving-local-quality section records the measured outcome, and the revisit is filed as LOCAL17 (bottom of the backlog, P3) keyed on a post-FEAT10 evidence-bearing corpus large enough to clear the ceiling that gutted this one. Artifacts kept for the trail: `~/Documents/Meetings/adapters/2026-07-30-runs-7b/` (all three checkpoints, `train.log`, `eval.log`, `dogfood-ab.log`, `split.json`) and the side-by-side in `pipeline/runs/20260723-103118.dogfood.md` (gitignored). One more specimen worth remembering: a first A/B attempt crashed on the BASE side with an 11-bullet summary against the 10-item schema cap, live confirmation of the unconstrained-decoding flakiness LOCAL13 documented. Original spec and progress trail follow.

**LOCAL9 (P2): corrections Phase 3, local LoRA fine-tune.** `mp corrections-stats` advertises a Phase 3 readiness check (~20 corrections over ~200 minutes) that no backlog task owns; make it real or stop advertising it. Scope: an owner-invoked `mp train-adapter` that fine-tunes a LoRA on the standard 7B via the MLX LoRA path, building prompt/completion pairs from the corrections corpus (original vs corrected summaries); evaluation is `mp dogfood` A/B (base vs adapter) on held-out meetings, hand-graded like the engine comparison; the adapter ships only through an explicit config opt-in (`summarization.local_adapter_path`), never silently applied. Fully on-device, no egress; training is a command the owner runs, no background training. An honest terminal outcome is allowed: if the A/B shows no capture win, close as adapter-not-worth-it, keep the corpus as a prompt-context asset (few-shot exemplars are the cheaper fallback lever), and fix the README wording. Gated on the corpus bar, which is owner-owed grading volume. Classification note (2026-07-10): `mp train-adapter` is owner-dev tooling under the de-CLI standing rule, CLI-only by design, like dogfood. Acceptance: with the bar met, a training run produces a loadable adapter; the dogfood scorecard decides adoption; README's corrections section describes the real flow either way.

**Progress (2026-07-23): the blocker was the corpus source, not the tooling.** Measured first: the corrections dir has held **0 records** since it was created on 2026-05-18, while the recordings dir holds **169 run sidecars, all with transcript and summary on disk, 2,422,719 transcript chars** (12x the 200k bar), 167 of them summarized by `claude-sonnet-4-6`. So the spec's only training source was empty for two months next to a ready-made distillation corpus. This pass added `--source {corrections,runs,both}` (default unchanged): `runs` builds pairs from the run sidecars (transcript -> the summary that run published), skipping local-backend runs since a model learns nothing from its own output; `both` puts corrections first and withholds their stems from the runs fill. Measured end to end on the real corpus: 167 pairs, train=135 / valid=16 / test=16.

Three defects surfaced while validating against real data, each of which would have made a training run worthless without failing loudly. (1) **Train/inference prompt mismatch.** `_base_instruction()` hand-substituted two of the master prompt's four placeholders, so every training prompt carried a literal `{extra_sections_directive}`, said "(no team context configured)" where the server sends the real team context, wrapped the transcript in `<transcript>` tags the server never uses, and omitted the schema block entirely. Fixed by building the pair from the shipping helpers: `summarize._load_system_prompt` plus `summarize_local.augment_with_schema` / `.compose_user_message`, the last two promoted from `LocalSummaryClient` methods to module functions so there is one copy. (2) **Wrong dataset format.** `{prompt, completion}` has no system role, so the system turn was being folded into the user turn; now emits `{"messages": [...]}` (mlx-lm's `ChatDataset`), the same three turns the server exchanges. (3) **Silent truncation.** `mlx_lm.lora` defaults to `--max-seq-length 2048` and truncates the tail, which is where the summary lives; 106 of 135 real pairs exceeded it, so most examples would have taught the model nothing at all. Now an explicit `--max-seq-length` (default 4096) with over-long meetings dropped and counted in the log, never truncated, plus `--mask-prompt` (loss on the summary, not the transcript) and `--grad-checkpoint`.

The A/B is now actually held-out: training writes `split.json` beside the adapter recording which stems went to train/valid/test, and `mp dogfood --adapter` refuses a transcript the adapter trained on, naming a held-out one instead (`--allow-trained` overrides; an adapter with no manifest warns rather than blocks, since it cannot be verified either way). Verified: 913 pipeline tests green, ruff and pyright clean, CI5 fences pass, and `mp train-adapter --source runs --dry-run` exercised against the owner's real 169 meetings. **Owner-owed remainder** (unchanged in kind, now actually runnable): run `mp train-adapter --source runs --adapter-path <dir>` on the M1 Pro, then `mp dogfood --adapter <dir> <held-out transcript>`, hand-grade the scorecard, and set `summarization.local_adapter_path` only if it wins. An honest negative result stays a valid terminal outcome. Note that LOCAL11 (warm-server identity) is a real precondition for trusting the A/B: a warm base-model server would otherwise serve base weights on both sides.

**Both preconditions are now resolved; the A/B is cleared to run (2026-07-23).** LOCAL11 shipped (commit 65ba629) and LOCAL15 shipped in the same session that raised it, so a configured adapter genuinely serves and a warm base-model server no longer silently answers both sides of the comparison. Verified end to end against a real `mlx_lm.server`: a summarize run carrying the adapter returns a summary, and a `local_adapter_path` that does not exist stops the run naming the path instead of quietly producing a base-model summary. The remaining work is the owner's training run, hand-grading, and the adoption call. The original blocker, kept for the trail:

~~**Do not run the A/B until LOCAL15 lands (filed 2026-07-23).**~~ A second, more fundamental precondition surfaced while shipping LOCAL11: mlx-lm 0.31.3 silently drops the `--adapter-path` flag this task's serving seam passes (`ModelProvider.load` keys its `_adapter_map` lookup by the already-resolved model path while the map is keyed `"default_model"`), so `summarization.local_adapter_path` is a no-op and the base model serves regardless. Verified by code read, empirically against a stubbed `ModelProvider`, and upstream (ml-explore/mlx-lm#1248 open since 2026-05-06, fix PR #1249 unmerged). Running the A/B before that is fixed compares the base model against itself, and the false negative would read as an honest "the adapter did not help" and wrongly close this task after real training and grading time was spent. Full evidence and scope in `LOCAL15`'s entry in this file.

**Progress (2026-07-11): tooling shipped, adoption owner-owed.** The full tooling is in: `train_adapter.py` (`mp train-adapter`) reads the summary-grading corpus, builds `{prompt, completion}` pairs (the base summarization prompt + transcript, from `mp.prompts/meeting_summary.md`, mapped to the owner's corrected summary JSON), splits train/valid/test, and shells out to `mlx_lm.lora --train` (subprocess, matching `build_server_command`'s precedent, so the module stays importable on Linux CI); it refuses below the `corrections-stats` readiness bar unless `--force`, and runs local-only via `entry.prepare(secrets=False)`. `summarization.local_adapter_path` (config, empty default) is the opt-in, threaded through `summarize_local.build_server_command` (+`--adapter-path`) and both `LocalSummaryClient` construction sites plus the `mp serve-local` warm path, so a configured adapter is actually served and never applied when unset. `mp dogfood --adapter <dir>` adds the base-vs-adapter A/B (local-only, no cloud baseline, no zero-egress refusal). README's "Improving local quality" section, `config.example.toml`, and the ARCHITECTURE subcommand table describe the real flow. Verified: pipeline 673 green (ruff + pyright clean), incl. pair-building / split / command-construction / `--adapter-path`-when-set / dogfood-adapter-mode-skips-cloud tests; `mp train-adapter --help` and the readiness gate (0/20 on this Mac) confirmed by hand. The two owner-owed remainders keep this partial: the **corpus is empty on this Mac** (grading volume is owner-owed), and the **A/B adoption decision** (run `mp train-adapter` then `mp dogfood --adapter`, hand-grade, set `local_adapter_path` only if it wins) needs a real corpus + Apple-Silicon Mac, not exercisable here. An honest negative result stays a valid terminal outcome.

**[DONE] DET7 (P2): record the suppressed meeting, attach off the live discovery candidate.** Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 7: "if the meeting got suppressed cause I didnt click record, after this I am not able to start the meeting recorder connected to a teams, only 'generic' one"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md). P2; the owner hits this in live dogfood, so re-band to P1 on the next recurrence that costs a meeting's attribution.

**Context.**

After a prompt dismissal (Skip, the close button, force-stop while prompting, or timeout with the skip default), `abandonPrompt` arms the cooldown and the skip latch and returns the state machine to `.idle` (`DetectionStateMachine.swift:104-109`). The latch is refreshed by every discovery sighting (~3 s cadence) for the meeting's whole lifetime (`MeetingSessionController.swift:1058-1061`), lapsing ~15 s after the app stops being seen. That suppression design is correct and stays.

The gap is the way back in. `toggleManual` has a correct attach branch: for `.prompting` and `.suppressed` it dismisses the prompt, clears suppression, and begins recording with the source (`MeetingSessionController.swift:171-187`, comment included). But `.suppressed` is legacy: nothing in production ever sets it (`DetectionStateMachine.setSuppressed` is documented as legacy, :79-85), and after `abandonPrompt` the machine is `.idle`, so every manual start takes the `.idle` branch: `beginRecording(source: nil)`. The status-bar menu deliberately keeps offering "Start Recording" during suppression, with a comment saying a skipped meeting must keep a menu route to record (`StatusBarController.swift:509-515`), but the route it offers is the generic one. The strong hint is that this feature existed and was lost to a refactor, not never designed: the dead `.suppressed` branch is exactly the wanted behavior.

What a generic (`source: nil`) recording costs: workflow resolution falls to the default (`MeetingSessionController.swift:345-349`), the meta sidecar carries no source bundle, display name, kind, or meeting title (`MeetingMetaSidecar.swift:33-37`) so the Library row has no app chip, and there is no lifecycle end-detection anchor (`armLifecycleLeaveButton` early-returns on nil, `MeetingSessionController.swift:1111`), leaving the stop to the silence backstop, which in this dogfood has historically fired approximately never (real ends are AX-detected), so a forgotten generic recording can trail many minutes of silence.

The one attached re-entry that exists is narrow: the timeout-skip path posts a notification whose "Start recording" action rebuilds the source, clears suppression, and records attached (`Notifier.notifySkippedMeeting` fired only from the timeout branch, `MeetingSessionController.swift:728`; handler `didRequestStartLate` at `Coordinator+Delegates.swift:121-133`). An explicit Skip or close posts nothing, and the notification route dies with Notification Center.

Where the live candidate is available: `handleDiscovery` receives a fresh `AppSource` every ~3 s while latched and discards it (`MeetingSessionController.swift:1058-1061`). Caveat for the affordance's label: discovery-path sources carry no `meetingTitle` (`MeetingSourceScanner` constructs without it, :93-96, :126-129, :175); only the lifecycle `.starting` path resolves titles. So the affordance names the app ("Record this Teams meeting"), not the meeting, unless it calls `MeetingTitleResolver.resolve` itself.

Adjacent fact, folded here rather than filed separately: `meetingpipe://record` / `toggle` are unconditionally `source: nil` too (`Coordinator+Automation.swift:44-45`), so a Raycast/Stream Deck start mid-meeting is also unattributed. The same cached-candidate preference can serve both.

**Scope.**

- Cache the last latched sighting where it is currently discarded (`MeetingSessionController.swift:1058-1061`) as `lastSuppressedCandidate: (source: AppSource, seenAt: Date)`, exposed through `SessionHost` (per daemon/CLAUDE.md: session logic reaches the host, not the Coordinator), cleared when the latch lapses.
- Add an explicit `recordAttached(to:)` entry that runs the `didRequestStartLate` sequence: clear suppression for the bundle, dismiss any prompt remnant, `beginRecording(source:)`.
- Surface it in the status-bar menu's suppressed state: the existing "Start Recording" row, when a live latched candidate exists, becomes (or is joined by) "Record this <App> meeting", built through `StatusBarModel` so the row logic is table-tested; plain "Start Recording" stays for the truly-idle case.
- Prefer the cached candidate in `toggleManual`'s `.idle` branch and in the `meetingpipe://record`/`toggle` router when the latch is live, so the hotkey and automation paths attach too. Record the decision if the hotkey is deliberately left generic.
- Decide-and-record: whether `notifySkippedMeeting` should also fire on explicit Skip/close (the plumbing is end-to-end already); recommendation is yes with a quiet banner, since the explicit-skip regret case is exactly the one the owner reported.

**Explicitly not in scope.**

Reviving the `.suppressed` machine state (the latch + `.idle` design is deliberate; add the candidate cache beside it rather than re-litigating the state machine). Changing latch/cooldown semantics or durations. Prompt re-display (this is record-without-reprompting). Title resolution improvements (CAL3's territory; the affordance may call the existing resolver, nothing more).

**Acceptance.**

Tests against `FakeSessionHost` (`MeetingSessionControllerBranchTests` idiom): a latched discovery sighting populates the cached candidate and refreshes it; the cache clears when the latch lapses; `recordAttached(to:)` clears suppression and begins recording with the source (meta sidecar inputs carry bundle id and display name); `toggleManual` from `.idle` with a live cached candidate records attached, and without one records generic; the automation `record` verb with a live candidate attaches.

`StatusBarModel` tests pin the menu row: suppressed-with-candidate shows the named attach row, idle shows plain Start Recording.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green (baseline at filing: 1770). Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball: let a Teams prompt time out (or skip it), open the menu bar: "Record this Microsoft Teams meeting" appears; click it; the HUD shows the workflow chip, the Library row carries the Teams chip, and the recording stops on its own when the call ends (AX end detection armed).

**Shipped 2026-07-30.** 1906 daemon tests green (18 new: 4 on the state machine's candidate facade, 9 on the controller's attach paths, 5 on the menu row), `swift build` green, `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green, no em-dash in any added line. What landed, against the scope above:

- **The cache** lives on `DetectionStateMachine` beside the skip latch (`noteSuppressedCandidate` / `liveSuppressedCandidate`), not on the controller. That is the spec's "exposed through `SessionHost`" satisfied by the shortest route: the state machine is already a `SessionHost` member, so the session logic still reaches it through the host, and the two *other* readers (the status-bar menu and the `meetingpipe://` router, both Coordinator-side) need no second seam. Its lifetime is the latch's by construction, so `liveSuppressedCandidate` is gated on `isSkipLatched` and drops a lapsed candidate on read; nothing has to run a timer to expire it, and `clearSuppression` drops it for that bundle so a consumed candidate cannot be re-attached minutes later.
- **`recordAttached(to:summaryMode:trigger:)`** on `MeetingSessionController` is the sequence `didRequestStartLate` already ran, lifted so all four entry points share it. `didRequestStartLate` now delegates to it rather than keeping a fourth copy, and the `start_late` event became `record_attached` with a `trigger` attribute naming who asked (`manual`, `automation`, `notification`), so the log still distinguishes them.
- **The menu row** is `StatusBarModel.Row.recordSuppressedMeeting`, chosen over joining a second row beside Start Recording: after this task the plain row *also* attaches, so two rows would be two labels for one action and one of them would be lying. `StatusBarController.populateMenu` builds `NSMenuItem`s by hand rather than from `rows`, so the copy lives in one `StatusBarModel.startRecordingTitle` helper both read, and the controller reads the candidate at `menuNeedsUpdate` time rather than caching it (the menu is repopulated in place on open, so the row is right at the instant it is looked at, and nothing has to rebuild on the 3 s discovery cadence).
- **Hotkey and automation**, the first decide-and-record item: **not** left generic. Both take one `startManual(summaryMode:trigger:)` rule on the controller. The reasoning is asymmetric cost, not preference: attaching when the user meant a fresh generic recording loses nothing (the workflow is re-routable from the Library, and the meeting really is the one running), while recording generic when they meant this meeting loses the workflow, the sidecar identity, the Library chip, and the AX end anchor, which in this Teams-only dogfood is what actually stops a recording. Automation keeps its own `.idle` guard, so a URL-scheme start still cannot stack onto a live recording. `startManual` exists as a named rule mostly so the automation branch is reachable from a test: `Coordinator` is unconstructible (ARCH4), so its three-line guard is the only part left uncovered.
- **`notifySkippedMeeting` on explicit Skip / close**, the second decide-and-record item: **yes**, as the spec recommended, and quiet in a literal sense. A new `SkipOrigin` splits the two causes: `.timedOut` keeps the sounded "Meeting prompt timed out. Start recording?" (the user may never have seen the prompt), `.dismissed` posts silently and says the meeting is still running (the user chose this, so it is an undo affordance, not an alert). The explicit skip also now gets the `Suppressed (<app>)` menu-bar label the timeout has had since UX10; without it the two surfaces disagreed, and the label is what makes the named row legible in context. Both reuse the existing per-bundle notification id, so repeat skips of one app still coalesce.

Not done, deliberately: the `.suppressed` machine state stays legacy and unrevived, latch and cooldown semantics are untouched, no prompt is re-displayed, and no title is resolved (the row names the app, since discovery-path sources carry no `meetingTitle`, exactly as the spec's caveat says).

Docs synced in the same commit: `README.md`'s `detection.default_prompt_action` entry (both skip paths, the renamed row, what attaching buys, and that it lapses with the call), a new **Suppressed candidate** glossary entry in `ARCHITECTURE.md` beside **Skip latch**, and `design/ui_kits/macos_app/MenuBarDropdown.jsx` gained the `suppressed` state so the mockup shows the row it now ships. Checked and unchanged: `CONVENTIONS.md` (no new event category, no schema change), `daemon/CLAUDE.md` (nothing renamed or moved, no new trap), `docs/SETUP.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, `design/README.md`.

One copy call the owner may want to overrule: the row reads **"Record this Microsoft Teams meeting"**, sentence case after the verb. That is the string this spec's own eyeball step names, and it reads against `design/README.md`'s "menu items use Title Case" rule; "Record This Microsoft Teams Meeting" shouts and the app name is a proper noun inside a sentence rather than a command word. The deviation is recorded at `StatusBarModel.startRecordingTitle`, so flipping it is one line plus two test strings.

**[DONE] UX37 (P2): Ask is safe to leave (root-owned model, cancellable run, preserved state).** **Shipped 2026-07-30: `AskModel` owns the run, the launcher retains `mp ask` in its own cancel slot, and the deeplink is consumed on completion. History cap 20 and refuse-the-second-ask are the two delegated decisions, recorded. One deliberate deviation from the acceptance text: `retainForCancel` did not become a `PipelineDriver` parameter a fake could record, because every ask should be cancellable and a knob with one possible value is noise. Retention is a `RetainSlot` inside `PipelineLauncher` with a second slot for ask, and the observable half is `cancelAsk()` on the driver protocol, which `MeetingLibraryServiceTests` pins reaching the fake. Owner eyeball still to do; everything else is pinned by 14 `AskModelTests` plus that forwarding test.** Original spec follows.

Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 6: "Ask should be safe to leave. Currently if I ask anything, and then leave tab and get back, process got interrupted"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

What the owner experiences as "interrupted" is state loss, not process interruption, and the truth is worse than a cancel: the run keeps going, invisibly, and its answer is thrown away.

The run's entire state is `@State` on the view struct: `question`, `asking`, `answer`, `errorText` (`AskView.swift:15-18`). `LibraryRootView` mounts `AskView` inside an `if/else` scope chain (`LibraryWindow.swift:747-751`), so switching to Facts or People tears the view down and destroys that state. The `Task {}` started by `ask()` (:224-248) is unstructured, so it is NOT cancelled on teardown; it completes into destroyed state.

The subprocess chain is `LibraryWindowModel.askMeetings` (`LibraryWindow.swift:358-360`) to `MeetingLibraryService.askMeetings` (`Library/MeetingLibraryService.swift:458-482`) to `PipelineLauncher.ask` (`PipelineLauncher.swift:437-461`): `runMP(["ask", question, "--out", tmp], timeout: 10 * 60)`. `retainForCancel` is not passed, so `cancelActiveRun()` cannot reach it (the UX28 machinery exists and is unused here); an abandoned ask holds a pipeline process for up to 10 minutes with no surface and no stop. The `--out` JSON is deleted in a `defer` (:441-442), so the returning answer is lost with the view.

Two adjacent losses. The `meetingpipe://ask?q=` deeplink prefill is consumed and cleared before the run (`AskView.swift:46` clears `model.pendingAskQuestion`), so navigating away loses even the question. And nothing anywhere persists an answer or history; every visit starts blank.

The in-repo fix precedent is two scopes over: `DigestListModel` is an `ObservableObject` held as `@StateObject` by the Library root (`DigestsView.swift:14-26`, `LibraryWindow.swift:450`, `:760`), so a scope switch destroys only the view and an in-flight generate lands on surviving state (`DigestsView.swift:164-178`).

## Scope

- Introduce `AskModel: ObservableObject` (question, asking, answer, errorText, and a session-scoped list of past question/answer pairs) held as `@StateObject` on the Library root beside `digestList`; `AskView` becomes a renderer over it. An in-flight ask completes into the model whether or not the view exists.
- Thread `retainForCancel: true` through `PipelineLauncher.ask` and give the running state a visible Cancel (the UX28 idiom: the run is cancellable, the cancel surfaces as a named outcome, not a silent blank).
- Preserve the deeplink question until the run it started completes (consume-on-completion, not consume-on-render).
- Session history stays in memory (the model), newest first, so returning to Ask shows the previous answers this session. Durable on-disk history is UX38's call, not this task's.

## Explicitly not in scope

Engine performance, indexing, and memory behavior (AI11 owns that; this task makes the UI honest around whatever the engine costs). The Ask pane redesign (UX38, which depends on this model extraction). Durable cross-restart history. Parallel asks (one at a time stays; a second ask while one runs queues or replaces per the model's single `asking` slot, record which).

## Acceptance

Model-level tests: start an ask, simulate view teardown (drop the view, keep the model), deliver the completion; the answer is present when the view remounts. Cancel invokes the launcher's cancel path (fake launcher records `retainForCancel: true` and the cancel call). The deeplink question survives a mount-unmount-mount cycle until its run completes. History accumulates newest-first and caps sanely (pick a cap, record it).

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green (baseline at filing: 1770). Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball: ask a question, immediately switch to Facts, come back; the spinner is still there and the answer arrives in place. Cancel a slow ask; the pane says it was cancelled instead of going blank.

**[DONE] FEAT10 (P2): Evidence-grounded summaries (citations with transcript jump).**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-22 (owner feature ask, designed and approved in the 2026-07-22 review session; owner calls from that session: published notes carry timestamps only, and the decisions section is included). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**FEAT10 (P2, new): every summary point carries verified evidence (verbatim phrase + timestamp) and a one-click jump to the transcript row.** The ask: a summary bullet, decision, action item, or open question is currently uncheckable against the meeting; the reader either trusts it or replays audio. Give each point up to two evidence anchors, each a short verbatim phrase plus a timestamp, rendered as quiet [mm:ss] chips in the Summary tab (hover shows the phrase) that switch to the Transcript tab, scroll to the source row, and briefly highlight it. Published Markdown gets plain ` [12:34]` suffixes, timestamps only.

Why the codebase is ready (evidence, line numbers as of 2026-07-22): the transcript sidecar carries absolute per-segment times (`TranscriptSegment` start/end, `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/TranscriptTab.swift:10`); time-to-row mapping plus scroll already exist for FEAT8 markers (`TranscriptSegment.index(at:in:)` TranscriptTab.swift:28, `ScrollViewReader` + `.id(seg.index)` + `proxy.scrollTo` at TranscriptTab.swift:535/601/615); tab switching is one write to `MeetingDetailView.selectedTab` (MeetingDetailView.swift:15); and `mp ask` is the verification precedent (model cites, `rag.verify_citations` checks against ground truth, graceful fallback when a weak model cites badly, ask.py:103-110). The one real gap: the model input has no timestamps. `summarize.summarize` reads the overlaid speaker-merged Markdown (summarize.py:396) built by `transcript_corrections.overlaid_markdown` (applies the speaker + text overlays to the `<stem>.json` segments, then `render_markdown`, transcript_corrections.py:82-106), and `render_markdown` emits no times (markdown.py:26). Second hazard, named so it is not rediscovered the hard way: Swift rewrites `summary.json` by re-serializing only the fields it models (`MeetingSummary.jsonObject()`, `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Library/MeetingSummary.swift:143`), from both `FactsView.markDone` (FactsView.swift:145) and `SummaryTab.persistEdit` (SummaryTab.swift:632), so an unmodeled evidence field would be silently dropped on the first mark-done or edit. Swift must model the field.

Scope, pipeline: (1) additive schema, ADR 0014 stays intact: `Evidence {quote: verbatim <=15 words, t: float seconds into the recording}`; `ActionItem.evidence: list[Evidence]` inline, and `MeetingSummary.evidence: {"summary"|"decisions"|"questions": list[list[Evidence]]}` index-aligned for the string sections; at most 2 anchors per item; legacy files (field absent) round-trip unchanged and every existing consumer ignores the field. (2) model-facing shape: `SUMMARY_TOOL`'s string sections become `{text, evidence[]}` objects so anchors attach at generation and can never misalign (schemas.py:77); one shared normalizer flattens the model shape to the stored shape and is used by every backend (the anthropic tool path in summarize.py; the JSON recovery paths in summarize_local.py, provider_claude_cli.py, provider_openai.py via `largest_balanced_json_object`). (3) timestamped model input: a timestamps variant of the overlaid render prefixing each merged turn with [mm:ss]; the stored `<stem>.md` is unchanged, and a meeting with only plain md (BYO paste) simply gets no evidence, no error. (4) verification pass in `summarize` after the language check: t must land inside or within 45 s of a real segment (snap t to that segment's start); the quote must be a normalized substring (case/whitespace/punctuation tolerant) of transcript text in that window; drop what fails and emit a pipeline event with kept/dropped counts. A wrong anchor never reaches disk. (5) LANG1 interplay: quotes are verbatim transcript language, so `summary_language.divergent_sections` must exclude evidence or a translated summary (summary_language=en over a uk transcript) gets falsely repaired. (6) published render: `render_summary_md` appends ` [12:34]` (multiple: ` [12:34, 18:22]`) per item (markdown.py:96); the Swift mirror `AppleIntelligenceSummarizer.renderMarkdown` matches, and the CI3 golden `summary-md-golden.json` is regenerated with an evidence-carrying case (`cd pipeline && uv run python ../scripts/gen_contract_fixtures.py`).

Scope, daemon: (7) `MeetingSummary` models Evidence with tolerant decode and `jsonObject()` serialization; the corrections editor remaps on save: an item whose text is unchanged keeps its anchors (text-match, the FactsView.markDone guard pattern at FactsView.swift:150-157), an edited or new item drops them, and index alignment for the string sections is rebuilt (the editor edits and deletes rows in all four sections, CorrectionEditor.swift:17-137). (8) `SummaryRenderedView` renders the chips after each bullet/decision/question and inside the ActionItemRow chip row (the existing chip idiom, SummaryRenderedView.swift:211): monospaced digits, muted tint, no sparkle per PRODUCT.md; hover shows the quote; VoiceOver reads "Source at 12:34: <quote>"; chips are keyboard-focusable; the target-row flash honors reduced motion. (9) a chip click sets `selectedTab` to transcript and hands TranscriptTab a pending seek time, consumed via the existing time-to-index mapping + scrollTo. This pending-seek seam is also what AUTO2 rides.

Backends and degradation: full treatment on anthropic, openai, claude_cli, and the local single-pass path. The local map-reduce path (`summarize_local._batched` / `_render_for_reduce`, summarize_local.py:110-124) and the Apple Intelligence backend (`Summarization/AppleIntelligenceSummarizer.swift`) emit no evidence in v1: absence over wrong anchors, and the verifier enforces the same rule everywhere. Old meetings gain evidence per-meeting via the existing Regenerate flows; no bulk migration. Expect a modest output-token bump (capped quote length and 2 anchors per item keep it small on cloud; on local it is the price of the feature).

Explicitly not: no quotes in published notes (owner call 2026-07-22; the phrase is hover detail in-app). No meetingpipe:// links in notes (AUTO2, filed separately at P3). No audio-seek on chip click in v1 (cheap follow-on once the pending-seek seam exists; `PlaybackBar` already lives in the Transcript tab, note for the pickup session). No evidence on `mp digest` / DigestsView (cross-meeting synthetic summaries; the renderer tolerates absence) or on WF7 extra_sections. No new config knob; the caps are constants. Rejected during design: inline [mm:ss] markers inside the bullet strings (pollutes Facts rows, `mp actions`, digest, the embedding index, and the corrections corpus) and a `summary: list[str] -> list[object]` migration (breaks the ADR 0014 lock and every publisher for no gain over the additive field).

Acceptance: Python tests pin the normalizer (all four sections), the verifier (valid anchor kept with t snapped; fabricated quote dropped; out-of-range t dropped; tolerant quote matching), the `render_summary_md` suffix, the LANG1 exclusion, per-backend evidence survival through JSON recovery, and that a legacy no-evidence summary round-trips unchanged. Swift tests pin decode/jsonObject round-trip preserving evidence through a mark-done and a correction save, the remap-on-edit rule, the chip presentation model, and the pending-seek time-to-row mapping. CI3 fixture regenerated and both suites green on it. End to end: a regenerated meeting's `summary.json` carries verified anchors and every rendered chip resolves to a real transcript row; ruff, pyright, pytest, swift test, and truth fences all green. Owner-owed eyeball: a chip click lands the Transcript tab on the cited row on a live meeting.

## Progress

**2026-07-24, shipped to `owner-owed`.** Every scope item (1) to (9) is built and the whole acceptance list except the two items that need a real model and a real meeting. Both suites green: 1665 Swift, 1018 Python, plus ruff, pyright, and truth fences.

Decisions taken that the spec left open:

- **The normalizer is a pydantic `mode="before"` model validator**, not a function each backend calls. The spec asked for "one shared normalizer used by every backend"; wiring it into `MeetingSummary` validation makes that true by construction, so the Anthropic tool path and the three JSON-recovery paths inherit it and a fifth backend cannot forget it. `normalize_model_summary` stays public and pure for direct testing.
- **`Evidence.t` decodes from `"mm:ss"` as well as seconds.** The model reads `[12:34]` markers in the transcript, and asking it to emit `754.0` adds an arithmetic step whose only failure mode is a silently dropped anchor. It can now copy what it saw. The stored shape is still float seconds, so this is tolerance on the read edge, not a schema change.
- **An anchor snaps to the segment that actually carries the quote**, when one does, rather than to whichever segment the timestamp landed nearest. Both satisfy the spec's "snap t to that segment's start"; this one makes the chip land *on* the cited row instead of near it, which is what the acceptance criterion asks for. A quote spanning a turn boundary falls back to the nearest segment in the window.
- **A quote over 25 words is dropped** even if it matches. The schema asks for <=15; this is the ceiling at which a "verbatim phrase" is really a pasted paragraph, and it keeps the hover card readable.
- **`SummaryRenderedView` bullets now carry their pre-filter index.** The view drops empty strings before rendering, which would have shifted every anchor after a gap onto the wrong bullet. Display numbering still counts rendered position.
- **The LANG1 exclusion needed no code change**, only a test and a comment: quotes live in their own field, so `_summary_sections` never saw them. That is worth keeping structural rather than defending with a filter.

Owner-owed remainder:

1. The eyeball the spec reserves: click a chip on a live meeting and confirm the Transcript tab lands on the cited row.
2. Confirm real yield. Every path here is exercised by fakes, so what is unmeasured is how often a real cloud model produces anchors that survive verification. The prompt's rule 10 is the tuning surface if the answer is "rarely"; the verifier's thresholds are deliberately not the first thing to loosen, since letting a wrong anchor through is the one outcome the feature cannot afford.

**[DONE] UX29 (P2): NDA-aware re-summarize affordance.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-23 (owner finding, 2026-07-23 assessment session). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**UX29 (P3, new): the UI offers a cloud action that can never do what it says on an NDA meeting, then stays silent about the substitution.** On 2026-07-23 the owner clicked "Re-summarize with Anthropic" twice on an NDA-workflow meeting (stem `20260723-103118`, toolbar events 07:46:26Z and 07:48:43Z), got local Qwen output both times, and read it as a bug. It is not: the daemon passes `--backend anthropic` and the pipeline's `effective_backend` clamps to local (the PIPE6 one-shot override deliberately "still flows through the regulated/NDA clamp"; the daemon additionally strips the API key from the child env, `PipelineLauncher.cloudSecretPolicy`, PipelineLauncher.swift:827-857). The clamp is the product's core privacy promise and stays untouched. The defect is purely communicative: the menu item is emitted unconditionally (`MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:205-208`, the comment at :203-204 even names the reliance on downstream clamping), and no surface says "this ran locally because NDA".

Scope. In the detail `...` menu (and any twin affordances), when the meeting's meta carries `workflow_nda_mode = true` or global regulated mode is on: render the cloud option disabled with an inline caption in the quiet register ("NDA workflow: summaries stay on this Mac"), and add a "Change workflow..." row beneath it that opens the existing reassign flow (`beginReassign`, MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:416-449), whose explicit NDA-transition confirmation is already the designed escape hatch the owner ended up using by hand. Derive the flag from the same meta the row already loads (MeetingStore carries the workflow block); no new state. VoiceOver reads the disabled reason.

Explicitly not: no per-meeting cloud override under NDA (it would weaken the promise the clamp exists to keep; the reassign flow with its confirm IS the override); no pipeline changes; the post-run provenance label ("Summarized locally") is PIPE11's run.json fix rendered by the existing badge, not new UI here; regulated-mode handling beyond reusing the same disabled state.

Acceptance. A presentation-model test pins: cloud item disabled with the caption when meta says NDA (and when regulated is on), enabled otherwise; the Change-workflow row routes to the reassign entry point; VoiceOver label carries the reason. Full daemon suite green. Owner eyeball: on an NDA meeting the menu explains itself and the path to Anthropic is one click away, with the existing confirmation intact.

**[DONE] UX33 (P2): Workflow inspector rework.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 1: the workflow details panel "looks quite strange to me, I think it requires rework", decision delegated and taken: rework is warranted). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

`WorkflowInspector.swift` (187 lines) renders the right-column pane for a selected workflow scope. Traced 2026-07-29, the "strange" read decomposes into six concrete defects:

1. **The Edit button floats mid-pane.** The layout is `ScrollView > VStack` (:11-12) with a `Spacer(minLength: 0)` at :18 meant to pin the "Edit workflow" button (:19-23) to the bottom. A `Spacer` inside a `ScrollView` is inert (the scroll view sizes to content), so a workflow with little content shows a short card and a large empty region below it. This is the biggest single contributor to the broken feel.
2. **A 320pt ribbon in an unbounded pane.** The inspector caps itself at `minWidth: 240, idealWidth: 260, maxWidth: 320` (:27) while the detail column it sits in has a min of 450 and no max (`LibraryWindow.swift:782`, `LibraryLayout.swift:25-26`). On a wide window the pane is mostly background.
3. **"Modes" usually says "-".** `modesLine` (:131-133) returns "-" whenever NDA is off, which is most workflows. A permanent row whose value is a dash is noise.
4. **Recent chips look interactive and are not.** The RECENT section (:87-111) renders up to 5 meeting titles as chip-backgrounded `Text` (:95-108) with no button, tap gesture, or navigation. Clicking a recent meeting does nothing.
5. **Trigger leaks implementation detail.** `triggerLine` (:115-129) prints raw bundle ids and `/regex/` strings joined by commas; "Output" truncates a Notion DB id to an 8-char slug (:140-143). Neither is written for the product's register (PRODUCT.md: quiet, deliberate, non-technical owner).
6. **The pane is unreachable whenever a meeting is selected.** The detail-pane branch order at `LibraryWindow.swift:950-954` is multi-select, then single meeting, then workflow scope, so selecting a workflow in the rail while a meeting selection exists shows the meeting, not the inspector. The pane is effectively an empty state, not an inspector.

Also missing entirely: retention policy (a real `Workflow` field, visible only in the editor sheet), meeting count, last-meeting date. The pane has exactly one affordance (Edit).

## Scope

Redesign `WorkflowInspector` into a pane that fills its column and earns each row:

- Identity header: emoji/colour, name, DEFAULT badge, the FEAT11 context state line (keep; it is good), and the context prompt behind a disclosure rather than a 3-line dump ahead of the facts.
- Facts that earn their row: drop "Modes" when it would read "-" (show it only when NDA or redaction is on); humanize Trigger ("Matches Microsoft Teams" plus a quiet secondary line for title rules); show Output as the sink names with the Notion target's display name where the picker already knows it.
- Add the two cheap truths the pane is missing: meeting count for the scope and the last meeting's date (both derivable from the already-loaded scope counts and meeting list; no new disk reads).
- Recents become buttons: clicking one selects that meeting in the list (the selection state lives on `LibraryRootView`; hand the tap up rather than resolving stems in the inspector).
- Actions: keep Edit primary; visually pin it (give the pane a non-scrolling footer or accept content-flow placement, but kill the dead region); the row-level Delete stays UX32's.
- Layout: widen to fill the detail column with a centered max around 400-480pt so it reads as a card, not a ribbon.
- Reachability: decide-and-record between (a) selecting a workflow rail scope clears the meeting selection so the inspector always shows, or (b) the inspector is also reachable from a compact header chip when a meeting is open. Recommendation: (a); it matches how scope switches already feel and is one line where the scope changes.
- Extract the row derivation into a pure `InspectorPresentation`-style type per the repo's decide-pattern (daemon/CLAUDE.md "Pure logic on its own type"), so trigger humanization and row visibility are table-tested.

## Reachability decision, taken at pickup 2026-07-29

**(a): selecting a workflow rail scope clears the meeting selection.** Taken as recommended, and implemented as `LibraryScope.clearsMeetingSelection` (true only for `.workflow`), read by one `onChange(of: scope)` in `LibraryRootView`.

Why not (b), the compact header chip: it adds a second entry point to a pane whose problem is that it is unreachable, which leaves the original branch-order bug in place and pays for it with new chrome in a header PRODUCT.md's register wants quiet. (a) removes the condition instead of routing around it.

Why the rule is scoped to `.workflow` and not "any scope change": `.allMeetings` is what Facts, People, Ask, Quick Find, and the `meetingpipe://open?stem=` deeplink all switch to *before* setting a selection, in the same closure. A blanket clear would fire on that scope write and undo the navigation those five surfaces had just performed. Pinned by `test_no_other_scope_clears_the_meeting_selection`.

Residual, accepted: with a meeting open under a workflow scope, getting back to the inspector still means deselecting. That is one click, the toolbar keeps its own `Edit workflow` button in that state, and it is the same shape every other scope already has.

## Explicitly not in scope

Inline editing in the inspector (the sheet remains the single editor). UX32's row actions. Any new analytics beyond count and last-date. Changing `LibraryScope` resolution semantics (TECH-B4 name-based resolution stays; UX30 owns the alert-copy honesty about it).

## Acceptance

Unit tests on the extracted presentation type: trigger humanization cases (bundle-only rule, bundle+title rule, no rules), Modes row hidden when NDA and redaction are both off and shown otherwise, Output naming with and without a known Notion display name, recents capped at 5.

A UI-level test (or the presentation seam) pins that tapping a recent invokes the selection callback with the right stem.

The reachability decision is recorded in this file at pickup and the chosen behavior is pinned by a test on the scope-change path.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green (baseline at filing: 1770). Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball: select the Client work workflow on a wide window; the pane fills sensibly, no dead half-screen, "Modes: -" is gone, clicking a recent meeting opens it, and the count/last-date line reads true.

## Second pass, 2026-07-29 (the owner's eyeball, and the ribbon that survived it)

The eyeball happened the same day: "workflow view looks better, yet still ugly, also 'edit workflow' button looks like something from another world". A layout review was mocked at true scale and approved before any further code was written.

**The card was still a ribbon.** `cardMeasure = 416` was derived as `LibraryLayout.detailMinWidth (450) - 2 * padding`, which is a correct derivation of the wrong quantity: it sizes the card for the narrowest window the app allows and then freezes it at every width. On the owner's 1230pt pane that left 812pt of background. This task was filed to kill "a 320pt ribbon in an unbounded pane" and shipped a 416pt ribbon in an unbounded pane. The spec is what failed, and it failed by self-contradiction: "widen to fill the detail column with a centered max around 400-480pt" asks for two things that cannot both be true at 1230pt, and the first pass followed the number rather than the intent. `.frame(maxWidth:)` already shrinks a wider cap back at the floor, so the floor never needed deriving at all.

`cardMeasure` is now `cardMaxWidth = 720`, owner-picked, a ceiling rather than a width. It is the top of the 640-720 reading column `design/README.md` asks for. The summary's own measure moved to 680 in the same session and deliberately stops short of 720: prose has a measure ceiling near 90 characters a line, a label/value grid does not, so the two numbers differ because the content does. A test pins the card inside the band and pins that it exceeds the floor-derived figure, which is the relation that actually matters now.

**Widening alone would have bought whitespace, not information.** The rows were a stacked eyebrow-over-value column, so extra width just moved the right edge. `InspectorRow` now renders a label/value grid above a `gridFloor` and falls back to the stacked form below it via `ViewThatFits`, so a narrow pane is unchanged and a wide one reads as a spec sheet.

**The footer was the "another world" control.** It was a full-pane `bgRaised` plinth: a filled band running the whole 1230pt to hold one ~140pt button, three times wider than the card above it, which is why it read as a separate surface rather than as this card's footer. It is now the card's width, carries a hairline instead of a fill (`design/README.md` is explicit that resting surfaces get a hairline and no fill), and puts Edit at the card's trailing edge so content-left and action-right bound the card. The capsule and `.mpGhost` were never the problem and are unchanged; the first pass was right about the style and wrong about the surface.

Verified: `swift build` clean, **1879 daemon tests, 0 failures**. The old floor-derivation test was replaced rather than edited, since it pinned exactly the relation being rejected; three tests stand in its place (grows past the floor-derived width, stays inside the design band and above the prose measure, and a source fence that the footer carries no `bgRaised` and aligns trailing).

**Owner-owed, still.** Rebuild (`./scripts/rebuild.sh`) and select Client work on a wide window: the card should fill sensibly with the facts reading as a grid rather than a list, and the Edit button should look like it belongs to the card under it. Then narrow to the detail floor and confirm the rows fall back to the stacked form without squeezing.

## Third pass, 2026-07-30: Edit moves to the top right

Owner, on seeing the shipped footer: "can we move edit button to the top right? it looks lonely bottom left". One correction for the record, since it does not change the answer: the second pass had already moved Edit to the card's *trailing* edge (`dd22cc9`), and the owner had rebuilt past that commit, so the running build showed it bottom-right rather than bottom-left; the "bottom left" recollection is of the screenshot from before that pass. The lonely part was accurate either way, and it was the band, not the side.

Edit now rides the identity row's trailing edge, pushed there by a `Spacer` rather than a frame of its own, and the footer band is deleted outright: the pane is a single `ScrollView` again. This is the second route this task's own spec offered ("give the pane a non-scrolling footer **or** accept content-flow placement"), so it needs no re-argument. Top right beside the name it edits is the mac inspector convention, and the action rides the first row in the pane, so "does not scroll away" survives in practice without a band to enforce it. The workflow name gained `lineLimit(1)` with tail truncation so a long name truncates rather than shoving the button off the card's edge.

The footer fence was replaced rather than edited, since it pinned a footer that no longer exists. The new one asserts no `private var footer` and no `bgRaised` survive, that `editButton` is its own named piece, and that inside the identity row the `Spacer` *precedes* `editButton` (without that ordering the button would sit beside the name instead of at the edge). It strips `///` and `//` comments before scanning, because the code's own history note names the plinth the fence bans, and it was mutation-verified two ways: removing the `Spacer`, and moving `editButton` out of the row. Both turn it red.

Verified: `swift build` clean, **1888 daemon tests, 0 failures** (no count change; one fence replaced another), truth fences green.

**Owner-owed, unchanged:** the eyeball on a wide window, now with Edit at the top right.

**[DONE] UX38 (P2): Ask surface redesign: invitation empty state, docked input, history.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 6: "build a nice animated search bar at center of the page, inviting user to ask anything, and show the results of the search in a list form below... and move the search to the top left/top right once search completed. what do you think?"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

The owner's instinct is right about the core thing: Ask has a different job from every other rail scope. Facts, People, Stats, and Digests are projections you read; Ask is a conversation you start. Rendering it as another sidebar-plus-content page makes an empty pane with a lonely text field, which invites nothing.

The design opinion the owner asked for, recorded: yes to the centered invitation, with one amendment. After the first answer, the input should dock to the TOP of the pane (full-width or centered), not shrink into a top-left/right corner. A corner placement hides the primary affordance of the surface behind a small target, and the center-then-top pattern is the one the muscle memory already exists for (Spotlight, Raycast, every command palette). Top-docked keeps ask-again one click and zero hunting.

Register constraints from PRODUCT.md: quiet, deliberate, local-first; anti-flashy. "Animated" therefore means a restrained focus/transition treatment honoring `MPMotion.reduceMotion` (the prompt panel at `MeetingPromptWindow.swift:566-573` is the in-repo precedent for motion gating), not a pulsing hero. QuickFind (Cmd+K) already owns find-a-meeting; Ask's copy must frame answering ("Ask about your meetings: what did we decide about X?"), not searching, or the two surfaces blur (the QuickFind Ask handoff row, UX25, already routes questions here).

Dependencies and material: UX37 extracts the root-owned `AskModel` with a session history list this redesign renders; AI11 gives the running state something honest to show (index-rebuild progress instead of a bare spinner). Citations in answers already resolve to real meetings (`rag.verify_citations`) and the answer view already deep-links stems; keep that affordance prominent.

## Scope

- Empty state: centered input with a one-line invitation, 2-3 suggested question chips derived cheaply (recent workflow names, a recent meeting title), and the session history beneath when it exists.
- Ask flow: on submit, the input docks to the top with the quiet transition; the running state shows the AI11 progress line when the index is rebuilding, else the thinking state; Cancel per UX37.
- Results: newest-first history list of question/answer cards (question, answer, citation chips that open the meeting), rendered from `AskModel.history`.
- Decide-and-record with the owner at pickup: whether history persists across app restarts (a small JSON in the config dir, the `SavedSearchStore` single-file idiom) or stays session-only. Default to session-only until asked; durable history is one store away if wanted.
- Reduce-motion path renders the same states without the transition.

## Explicitly not in scope

Engine behavior (AI11). Model ownership and cancellation (UX37; this task builds on it and must not land first). Multi-turn conversation threading (an answer is a card, not a chat; revisit only if the owner asks). Replacing QuickFind or merging the two surfaces.

## Decided at pickup (2026-07-31)

The four calls this spec left to the implementer, recorded here so the walkthrough below is read against what actually shipped.

- **History stays session-only.** The spec's own default, taken rather than escalated. A question is asked about today's library and a restart is a reasonable place for it to end; a durable store is one `SavedSearchStore`-shaped file away if the owner asks. UX37's cap of 20 is what the list renders.
- **The pane docks on "there is anything to show", not on "an answer landed".** Layout is docked whenever a run is in flight or the history is non-empty, so the first question docks the input immediately (the move reads as a response to asking) and returning to the rail with history finds the same docked pane rather than an invitation sitting over a list.
- **The refused second ask is made legible before the click, not after it.** UX37 refuses a second ask while one runs and leaves the field untouched, which on its own is indistinguishable from a dead button. The running card carries the rule and names the way out ("One question at a time. Cancel to ask another."), and the field and the Ask button are visibly inert while the run is up. No transient toast: a state that explains itself is quieter than a message that appears and leaves.
- **The input clears when a run ends, not when it starts.** Through the run the field is the only place the running question is shown (and UX37 keeps the text on purpose so a rail switch cannot blank it); once the answer or the stop is a card, the same text left in the input is a leftover to delete before asking again, which is the opposite of what docking is for. Done in the renderer, so `AskModel`'s contract and UX37's tests are untouched.
- **Both chip kinds stack rather than wrap.** A suggestion is a whole question and a citation is a meeting title, so a flow row would break them mid-sentence at any width the list column actually gets (400 floor, 460 ideal). No wrapping layout was introduced, so the `private` `FlowLayout` in `PreferencesView+Recording.swift` stayed where it is rather than being promoted for one speculative caller. *(UX51 promoted it on 2026-08-04. This reasoning is not superseded, its premise is: the cast strip above the transcript is a real second caller, so `FlowLayout` now lives in `Preferences/PreferencesControls.swift` with two consumers. UX38's own chips still stack rather than wrap, for the reason above.)*

The AI11 leg needed daemon-side plumbing that did not exist: `mp ask` was printing the heartbeat, but `PipelineLauncher.ask` never passed `runMP`'s `onProgress`, and `PipelineProgress` dropped everything past `stage` + `elapsed_s`. That is presentation plumbing rather than engine behaviour (AI11's own ship note names UX38 as the renderer for those counters), so it landed here: the counters ride `PipelineProgress`, `PipelineLauncher.askPhase` decodes the two `mp ask` stages, and `AskInFlight` gained the field UX37 left room for.

## Acceptance

Presentation-level tests over the view's state derivation: empty model renders invitation, non-empty history renders the list with the input docked, asking state renders progress when the engine reports index work. Citation chips invoke the meeting-open callback with the right stem.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green. Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball: fresh Ask scope shows the centered invitation; asking docks the input up with a quiet motion (and no motion under Reduce Motion); the answer arrives as the first card with clickable citations; asking again stacks a second card; leaving and returning shows the same history (UX37's guarantee, visible here).

**[DONE] UX40 (P2): Voice chip rename and un-name, honest strip count.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 11: "when I name someone from the voice panel, I am not able to rename or unname it"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

The FEAT11 cast strip (`VoiceResolutionBar.swift`) renders one chip per voice and branches on exactly one thing: `voice.offersNaming`, true only for `.unresolved` with a voiceprint (`VoiceResolution.swift:52`). Every other state (`.you`, `.roster`, `.namedHere`, `.unattributed`, unresolved-without-voiceprint) is a static chip with a `.help` tooltip (:125-134). No chip has a context menu.

The machinery for rename and un-name exists one layer down and the strip just never reaches it:

- The naming sheet already supports rename: `SpeakerNamingMode { enroll, rename, assignNew }` (`TranscriptTab.swift:906`), and the mode is picked off `NamingTarget.currentName` (:290). The strip's callback hard-codes the enroll shape, never passing a current name (:260-262), so it can only ever open enroll.
- The transcript row's right-click menu offers "Rename..." and "Undo naming" (:849-865, wired to `renameSpeaker` and `libraryModel.undoSpeakerNaming` which drops the overlay entry and un-enrolls), but only when the name lives in the `SpeakerLabelStore` overlay (`clusterName` at :779-781). A `.roster`-origin voice (name baked into `<stem>.json` by the pipeline's finalize, no overlay entry) fails that gate AND fails the `canEnroll` gate, so it gets no Rename, no Undo, and no Name, in the strip or the row menu. Its only rename is the global Preferences People flow (`RosterRename`, which carries the new name across every meeting's overlay).

The count confusion, working as designed but misleading: the header tallies `rosterMatched + namedHere` of `others` (which excludes `.you` and `.unattributed`, `VoiceResolution.swift:73`, :83-84, :146-151), while the strip renders every classified member (:153-160; `VoiceResolutionBar.swift:30`). The owner's screenshot: 9 chips, "7 of 7 voices named", because the owner chip and an "Unknown speaker" chip render but do not count. The exclusion logic is right (the `speaker_unknown` junk drawer must never be offered for naming, and counting the owner would inflate every meeting); the copy just reads as a count over what is visible.

## Scope

- Per-state chip affordances, all routed to existing paths, no new naming machinery:
  - `.namedHere`: context menu with "Rename..." (open the sheet in `.rename` with `currentName` set) and "Un-name", `role: .destructive` (route to the same `undoSpeakerNaming`).
  - `.roster`: context menu with "Rename everywhere..." routing into the `RosterRename` flow, with copy naming the blast radius (it renames this person across all meetings, which is what a roster rename means); plus the existing `.help` explaining the roster match.
  - `.unresolved` with voiceprint: keep the current Name affordance, also as a menu item for consistency.
  - `.you` / `.unattributed`: help text only, unchanged.
- Wire `currentName` through the strip's callback so the sheet opens in the right mode (the one-line gap at `TranscriptTab.swift:260-262`).
- Header copy counts what it shows or says what it counts: prefer rewording over recounting, e.g. "All 7 other voices named." / "5 of 7 other voices named." with the existing empty-roster and no-others variants (`VoiceResolution.swift:78-93`) kept. The word "other" is the fix: it makes the owner-and-unknown exclusion legible in four characters.

## Explicitly not in scope

Changing `VoiceResolution` classification or the counting exclusions (correct as designed). Per-segment reassignment flows (exist, untouched). The roster UI itself. The staleness consequence of a rename on the summary (UX41, filed the same day). FEAT11's owner-owed rebuild eyeball.

## Acceptance

Tests extend the `VoiceResolution`/strip suites: menu offering per origin state (namedHere gets Rename + Un-name, roster gets the everywhere-rename, unresolved keeps Name, you/unattributed get none); the strip's rename path passes `currentName` so the sheet mode resolves to `.rename` (pin at the `NamingTarget` seam); Un-name from the chip invokes the same `undoSpeakerNaming` service call the row menu uses (one implementation).

Header copy tests: the 9-chip/7-named repro renders "All 7 other voices named."; a partial case renders the of-form; empty-roster and no-others variants unchanged.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green (baseline at filing: 1770). Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball on the 2026-07-27 meeting: right-click the misnamed chip, Rename, fix it; right-click again, Un-name, and the chip returns to the unnamed state; the header line no longer contradicts the chip count.

## Progress (2026-07-31): shipped, the eyeball is owner-owed

Everything but the rendered eyeball is in. `swift build` and `swift test` green at 1962 (1949 before, 13 new), truth fences and both dash guards clean; no Python touched.

The per-chip menu is a second pure rule beside the glyph and wording maps, `VoiceResolutionBar.actions(for:)`, rendered by a `ForEach` over its output so the view cannot offer something the rule does not. `VoiceResolution`'s classification and counting are untouched, as specced.

Two gates went in that the spec did not name, both for the same reason (a chip must not offer an action the flow behind it would turn into a no-op, the `WorkflowRowActions` rule):

- `.namedHere` splits. Rename plus Un-name are offered only when the key is a **cluster** label, which is the transcript row menu's own gate (`overlay.labels[speakerID]`) read off the key rather than off a second overlay lookup. The other `.namedHere` shape is FEAT3-SEGMENT's "New person", whose name lives in the overlay's per-segment map and never in `labels`: "Un-name" there would drop an entry that is not present and the chip would not move. That chip offers nothing and its tooltip points at the row menu's "Reset to original label" instead.
- A roster rename that fails now says so. `RosterRename.run`'s failure was surfaced by its two existing callers through a field of their own; a chip has no error slot, so it gets `LibraryDialogs.reportRosterRenameProblem`, the sibling of UX32's workflow refusal for the identical reason. A modal that asks for a new name and then changes nothing is exactly the silence worth a dialog.

Header copy took a third variant the spec's two examples did not cover: at 1 of 1 it reads "The other voice is named.", because "All 1 other voice named" is not a sentence and a 1:1 is the most common meeting there is. The `detail` clause ("2 voices are still unnamed.") was left alone: it only ever renders beside the of-form, whose "of 7 other" has already scoped the number.

Also in the same change: `NamingTarget.mode` lifts the sheet-mode decision out of the sheet's argument list so the rename seam is pinnable, and the tooltips on the states that grew a menu now say a right-click is there (an invisible context menu on a chip is close to not shipping the affordance).

Known limits, both pre-existing and shared with the other two rename surfaces: the overlay carry only reaches a meeting that has a `.summary.json` or a `.speaker_labels.json` and lists the person, so a finalized meeting whose summarize failed keeps the old name on its chips until it is summarized; and a roster voice that was renamed in-app first has a display name that is an overlay alias over the baked label, so the prompt renames what the chip shows.

**[DONE] UX41 (P2): Names changed since this summary: quiet cue + one-click re-summarize.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 11: after renames "summary might need re-generation... or instead maybe we can infer summary with new names without specific extra re-generation call. I am not 100% sure what is the best option"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

The split is real and confirmed on both sides. Generation applies the speaker overlay and bakes the resolved names into the summary text: `summarize()` composes the overlaid transcript (`summarize.py:453-461`, via `transcript_corrections.overlaid_structured` and `speaker_overlay.apply_overlay`) and renders `**Name**:` lines the model reads, so bullets, attendees, and action owners carry whatever names existed at that moment. Display never re-resolves: `MeetingSummary` is a flat decodable with no overlay step, and no summary surface references `SpeakerLabelStore` (grep zero). The repo already states it in as many words: "summaries and transcripts keep whatever they were written with" (`RosterRename.swift:14-16`). Meanwhile the transcript, cast strip, and People rail all resolve at display time and update immediately after a rename.

So after the owner names voices (the exact 2026-07-27 session: seven voices named post-meeting), the transcript says Anisha while the summary still says THEM-3, and nothing says why.

Decision, taken as delegated between the owner's two options:

- **Not silent substitution.** Rewriting names inside generated prose is unreliable (inflected languages, the owner's library is half Ukrainian where names decline by case; possessives; partial matches) and it would falsify provenance: the summary claims to be what the model wrote. Rejected.
- **Not auto-regeneration.** It costs an engine call (cloud money or local minutes) per rename batch, and PIPE11 just made regeneration deliberate and queued. The owner owns the click. Rejected.
- **Yes: a quiet, truthful cue with the fix one click away.** The register precedent is the "Summary edited locally" caption (`MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:94-106`) and the FEAT11 nudge rule ("a nudge, not a feature: no new storage, nothing auto-filled").

The derivation has one trap, found while tracing: a naive `mtime(speaker_labels.json) > mtime(summary.json)` check is falsified by the in-place summary rewrites that do NOT regenerate (the action done/reopen toggle through `MeetingLibraryService.setActionResolved` and the correction editor's `persistEdit`, both re-serialize `summary.json`). The truthful timestamp is `<stem>.run.json`'s `ts`, written at summarize time (`corrections.py:78-87`) and kept truthful by PIPE11 even for standalone re-summarizes (`summarize.py:876-905`). `MeetingStore` already parses `run.json` for backend/model/publish_state (:514, :535) and already prefetches content-modification dates in its scan (:318), so the derivation costs no new I/O class.

## Scope

- Derive `namesChangedSinceSummary` in `MeetingStore`'s post-scan overlay step (the `hasCorrections` shape at :362-367): true when the speaker-labels overlay's mtime is later than `run.json`'s `ts`; false when either file is absent (no summary yet, or never renamed; conservative, no cue). Roster-wide renames route through the same overlay files (`RosterRename` writes per-meeting overlays), so they are covered by construction.
- Render the cue in the detail header's caption slot beside "Summary edited locally": "Speaker names changed after this summary." with an inline "Re-summarize" affordance that opens the existing `ReSummarizeMenu` (UX29's NDA honesty comes free; the cue must not offer a cloud path the clamp forbids).
- Surface parity per the UX28 rule (a chip that exists in one place only is the named failure mode): decide-and-record between header-only (quiet, recommended: the list row stays calm, renames are deliberate acts whose consequence you check in the detail) or header + a row dot. Recommendation recorded: header-only; revisit if the owner reports missing it.
- The cue clears itself by construction: a re-summarize rewrites `run.json.ts` (PIPE11), flipping the comparison.

## Explicitly not in scope

Any rewriting of summary text (rejected above, recorded so the pickup session does not re-litigate). Auto-regeneration or batch "re-summarize all renamed" (the batch pane already covers multi-select re-summarize). Transcript-correction staleness (text edits already re-summarize through their own flow; only names have this silent split). `mp ask` index staleness (the fingerprint already covers overlay files; verified at `embed_index.py:349`).

## Acceptance

Pure derivation tests: rename-after-summarize yields true; action done-toggle rewrite of `summary.json` after a rename still yields true (the trap case, pinned); re-summarize (newer `run.json.ts`) clears it; absent `run.json` or absent overlay yields false.

A header test pins the caption + affordance render when the flag is set, and that the affordance opens the re-summarize path gated by `ReSummarizeMenu` (an NDA meeting's cue leads to the local-only offering).

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green (baseline at filing: 1770). Repo dash guard green. No pipeline change expected; if `run.json` parsing gains the `ts` field in Swift, no fixture is involved (run.json is not a CI4-pinned surface; confirm at pickup).

Owner eyeball: open the 2026-07-27 meeting (names were assigned after summarize); the caption reads "Speaker names changed after this summary", one click re-summarizes through the queue, and when it lands the caption is gone and the summary says Anisha.

## Progress (2026-07-31): shipped, the eyeball is owner-owed

Everything but the rendered eyeball is in. `swift build` and `swift test` green at **2029** (2018 before, 11 new), truth fences clean, both dash guards clean (no em-dash in any added line, none under `daemon/Sources` / `daemon/Resources`). No Python touched; `ruff` and `pytest` re-run anyway and unchanged at 1157.

**The `run.json` fixture question, confirmed at pickup as the spec asked:** it is not a CI4-pinned surface. `scripts/gen_contract_fixtures.py` generates exactly four (`publish-result`, `prefetch-progress`, `speaker-overlay`, `glossary`), and the hand-maintained five in `CONVENTIONS.md#cross-tree-golden-fixtures` are `meta-contract`, `chunking`, `json-extract`, `summary-md`, `transcript-corrections`. Reading `ts` on the Swift side pinned nothing and regenerated nothing.

The derivation is one pure `MeetingStore.namesChangedSinceSummary(overlayModified:runTimestamp:)`, deliberately taking a `Date?` and a `String?` rather than reading disk, so the four acceptance cases are unit tests and not filesystem choreography.

**One placement deviation, which is the spec's own reasoning carried one layer in.** The spec said the post-scan overlay step (the `hasCorrections` shape) and justified it with "costs no new I/O class", pointing at `MeetingStore` already parsing `run.json` at `:514`/`:535` and already prefetching mtimes at `:318`. Both of those lines are inside `buildMeeting`, not inside the post-scan step, and the difference is not cosmetic: `hasCorrections` is cheap there only because corrections live *outside* the recordings dir and the whole set is cached behind one directory mtime. `speaker_labels.json` and `run.json` are both *inside* the dir, so they are already in the per-stem signature. In `buildMeeting` a rename invalidates exactly the row it changed and every other scan costs nothing; in the post-scan slot it would have meant re-reading and re-parsing `run.json` for every row on every 500 ms scan, which is the exact TECH-A12 perf finding the cache exists to fix. So the flag is derived in `buildMeeting`, which is where the spec's stated constraint actually leads.

The trap is pinned twice, once pure and once through a real `performScan`, because a pure test alone cannot express it: the pure function never sees `summary.json`, so only a scan-level test proves that rewriting `summary.json` after a rename (the action done-toggle, a correction save) leaves the cue standing. The doc comment on the derivation names both wrong timestamps and why: `summary.json`'s mtime (two in-place rewriters that regenerate nothing) and `run.json`'s own mtime (`corrections.set_publish_state` rewrites the file after a publish, which the spec did not mention and which would have been the natural second guess).

**Two decisions the spec delegated, both taken and recorded:**

- **Surface parity: header-only**, as the spec recommended. The list row stays calm. A rename is a deliberate act whose consequence you check in the detail pane you are already in, and UX28's named failure mode is a chip that exists in one place while a *second* surface reports the same state differently; one surface reporting it is not that. Revisit if the owner reports missing it.
- **`fgSubtle`, not the neighbouring caption's `fgFaint`.** `fgFaint` sits near 2.8:1 and fails the 4.5 body floor, which is why the provenance row two lines up already moved off it with a comment saying so. A line that carries an action is the wrong place to keep that debt. "Summary edited locally" is left exactly as it is; it is not this task's line to change.

Two smaller things the spec did not name:

- The engine list moved into a shared `reSummarizeItems`, so the `...` menu's submenu and the cue's inline menu render one list. Writing the cue's menu as a second copy would have let UX29's clamp be applied in one and forgotten in the other, which is the drift `workflowChoices` already exists to prevent one level down. A fence counts the cloud engine's mentions in the header file so a third copy fails the build.
- The menu indicator stays **visible** on the inline affordance, unlike the header's `...` menu which hides it. That menu's label is an ellipsis glyph that already reads as a control; a bare word in a caption row does not, and hiding the chevron would have made the fix look like more caption.

A known and intended over-fire: a **re-transcribe** (ASR3) re-anchors the speaker overlay onto the new transcript, which bumps its mtime and raises the cue. The wording is a shade imprecise there (the names did not change, their anchors did), but the summary genuinely is stale after a re-transcribe, and the re-transcribe dialog already ends by telling the owner to re-summarize. Both write paths are change-gated (`carry.speakerOverlay != overlay`, and `PeopleRail.renamed` returning nil when nothing moves), so a no-op rename never raises it.

**Owner-owed:** the eyeball above. Needs one `./scripts/rebuild.sh`.
