**[DONE] UX39 (P2): Cmd+Tab truthfulness: activation ordering, close handoff, count drift.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 9: "when I open library, it is always displayed at the end of command+tab menu... commandtab cannot switch to it immediately if I was commandtabbed from it"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

The whole policy machine is 27 lines (`WindowActivationManager.swift`): `didShowWindow` increments a count and, on the first window, calls `NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.regular)` immediately followed by `NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true)` (:12-18); `didCloseWindow` decrements and drops to `.accessory` at zero (:21-26).

Three defects:

1. **The MRU-tail placement.** `setActivationPolicy(.regular)` is processed asynchronously by the system; an `activate` issued in the same run-loop turn applies against the pre-transition state, so the newly-regular app is appended to the app switcher's MRU list instead of being promoted to front. That is exactly "at the end of Cmd+Tab, and one Cmd+Tab cannot switch back". The call-site ordering compounds it: `LibraryWindow.show()` runs `makeKeyAndOrderFront`, then `activate`, then `didShowWindow` (which flips the policy and activates again) (`LibraryWindow.swift:48-51`, re-open path :15-22), so the window is fronted and activated while the app is still `.accessory`. Same shape in `PreferencesWindow.swift:63-66` and `DiagnosticsWindow.swift`.
2. **No close handoff.** `didCloseWindow` drops to `.accessory` with no re-activation of anything (:24), so closing the Library leaves focus nowhere in particular and the switcher's state stale.
3. **The count drifts on minimize.** `show()` guards on `!w.isVisible`, but `NSWindow.isVisible` is false for a miniaturized window, so minimize-then-reopen runs `didShowWindow` again; `windowWillClose` fires once, so `visibleCount` never returns to zero and the app is stuck `.regular` (Dock icon, Cmd+Tab slot) with no windows. Same hazard at `PreferencesWindow.swift:26-32` and `DiagnosticsWindow.swift:13-16`.

Adjacent: `NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps:)` is deprecated on the macOS 14 floor; twelve call sites across seven windows. The three handshake-skipping windows (Onboarding, Correction, QuickFind) are deliberate (panels/one-shots) and stay.

## Scope

- Reorder the open path: flip the policy to `.regular` FIRST, then defer `makeKeyAndOrderFront` + activation to the next run-loop turn (`DispatchQueue.main.async`) so the Dock transition has landed before the app claims frontmost. Encapsulate in `WindowActivationManager` (a `showWindow(_ window:)` that owns the whole dance) so the three handshake windows cannot re-diverge.
- Close handoff: when the count reaches zero, drop to `.accessory` and yield activation so focus lands on the next app rather than nowhere (the modern `NSApp.yieldActivation(to:)` family where available, else activate the next `NSWorkspace` frontmost candidate; record the chosen mechanism, it is the one genuinely fiddly part).
- Idempotent counting: track shown windows by identity (`Set<ObjectIdentifier>` or the window itself as the key) instead of a bare int, so a re-show of a live-but-miniaturized window deminiaturizes without double-counting; `show()` also learns to `deminiaturize` instead of re-running the open dance.
- Migrate the activation calls to the non-deprecated `NSApp.activate()` API in the same pass.

## Explicitly not in scope

The handshake-skipping panels (QuickFind, Onboarding, Correction) staying Dock-less is intentional. Dock-menu or Dock-icon features while `.regular`. Any change to which windows participate.

## Acceptance

`WindowActivationManager` becomes testable by identity: unit tests pin show/show-again-same-window (count 1), show-two-close-one (still `.regular`), close-all (drops), and the minimized re-show case (no double count). Policy flip and activation ordering are pinned by the manager owning the sequence (call-order recorded via an injected seam in tests).

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green (baseline at filing: 1770). Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball, the actual repro: open the Library, Cmd+Tab away, hold Cmd+Tab: MeetingPipe sits SECOND in the list (front of MRU behind the current app) and one Cmd+Tab returns to it. Minimize the Library, reopen it from the menu bar five times, close it once: the Dock icon disappears.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Added with the 2026-07-31 implementation: the code half shipped and is unit-pinned, but activation ordering is a window-server behaviour no test can observe, so the acceptance above is owner-owed. Walk the owner through it step by step; the owner does not read code. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] With no recording in flight, run `./scripts/rebuild.sh` so the running daemon is the built one. Confirm the menu-bar icon comes back before handing over.
2. [owner] The MRU test. Open the Library from the menu bar, Cmd+Tab away to any app, then hold Cmd and tap Tab. Pass: MeetingPipe sits **second**, right after the app you are in, and letting go returns to it in one Cmd+Tab. Fail (the reported behaviour): it sits at the far right end of the row.
3. [owner] The count-drift test. With the Library open, minimize it (Cmd+M), reopen it from the menu bar, and repeat that five times. Then close it once (Cmd+W). Pass: the Dock icon disappears and MeetingPipe leaves the Cmd+Tab list. Fail: a Dock icon is left behind with no window on screen.
4. [owner] The close handoff, right after step 3's close: glance at the menu bar. Pass: the app you were in before owns the menu bar. Fail: the menu bar still reads MeetingPipe with nothing on screen. This is the one leg with a known fallback, so report it either way: it is `NSApp.deactivate()`, and if it under-delivers the next thing to try is naming a concrete successor app for `yieldActivation(to:)`, **not** `NSApp.hide(nil)` (that one works but hides the recording HUD and the detection prompt along with everything else).
5. [owner] Regression check on the three panels that skip the handshake on purpose. With another app frontmost, press Cmd+K. Pass: the Quick Find panel appears with keyboard focus and typing filters the list. This leg exists because the deprecated `activate(ignoringOtherApps:)` became `NSApp.activate()` here too; a panel that appears *without* focus is the cooperative-activation difference and is worth reporting.
6. Steps 2, 3, and 5 passing moves UX39 to done; step 4 is a nice-to-have that names its own follow-up if it fails.

**[UX48, 2026-08-04] Two of those legs could not do what they claimed, and both are fixed now.** Step 3 is built on Cmd+M and step 5 on Cmd+K, and at the time this app installed no `NSApp.mainMenu` at all, so Cmd+M was the system beep (the owner had to minimize with the yellow title-bar button) and Cmd+K matched only while the status-bar dropdown was open, which is what the owner reported here and what UX48 was filed from. Step 4 was worse than wrong, it was unfalsifiable: its fail state is "the menu bar still reads MeetingPipe with nothing on screen", and an app with no main menu can never own the menu bar, so it reported pass whatever the activation code did. UX48 installs a main menu with the flip to `.regular` and removes it with the drop back, so step 3 now runs as written and step 4's observable is real. Step 5's "with another app frontmost" half is still not producible: Cmd+K is a menu key equivalent, and no menu, main or otherwise, receives a keystroke while another app is frontmost.

**[DONE] AUTO2 (P2): Published-note transcript deeplinks (meetingpipe:// open at a timestamp).**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-22 (owner feature ask, approved in the 2026-07-22 review session; P3 promote-on-demand by design: the in-app jump ships in FEAT10, this is the out-of-app half). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**AUTO2 (P3, new): make the published [mm:ss] timestamps clickable from Obsidian / filesystem / LAN notes.** FEAT10 puts plain ` [12:34]` suffixes in published Markdown; this task turns them into `meetingpipe://open?stem=<stem>&t=<seconds>` links that open the Library at that meeting's Transcript tab at that moment. The scheme is shipped and hardware-verified (AUTO1, 2026-07-20, an `automation` `command` event with verb `open_library`): `AutomationCommand.parse` is the pure tested parser (Automation/AutomationCommand.swift:46) whose `library`/`open` verb already takes a scope, the router (`Coordinator+Automation.handleAutomation`) is the single gate, and `CFBundleURLTypes` is already registered by install.sh, so only new verb parsing lands in code. AskView already navigates from a citation to its stem (AskView.swift:12) and FEAT10 adds the pending-seek seam into TranscriptTab; this task is the URL spelling of those two existing moves.

Scope: parser support for `meetingpipe://open?stem=<percent-encoded stem>&t=<float seconds>` (t optional; a garbage t degrades to open-without-seek; bare `open`/`library` behavior unchanged), with cases in the AutomationCommand tests. Router: resolve the stem to a Library row (the AskView navigation precedent), select the Transcript tab, hand over the pending seek; an unknown stem (stale note, renamed recording) opens the Library quietly with no alert. Publishers: `render_summary_md` gains an optional deeplink mode (a stem parameter) rendering each timestamp as a `[12:34](meetingpipe://open?stem=...&t=754)` link, enabled for the Markdown-file sinks (publish_obsidian.py, publish_fs.py, publish_lan.py) and the stored `<stem>.summary.md`; Notion keeps plain-text timestamps (custom URL schemes are not reliably clickable in Notion rich text). The Swift mirror `AppleIntelligenceSummarizer.renderMarkdown` matches and the CI3 golden `summary-md-golden.json` gains a linked case.

Explicitly not: no Notion deeplinks (revisit only on evidence the scheme renders clickable there); no new UI for stale stems beyond the quiet no-match open; no install.sh changes (the scheme is already registered; a new verb is parse-side only). Depends on FEAT10 (the timestamps in notes and the pending-seek seam); promote to P2 once FEAT10 ships if the owner wants the out-of-app half next.

**Progress (2026-07-24): built; only the owner's click is left.** Promoted to P2 by the owner the day FEAT10 shipped, which is exactly the clause above. Both trees green (1691 Swift, 1032 Python; ruff, pyright, truth fences clean).

Parse and route: `AutomationCommand` gained `openMeeting(stem:seek:)` on the existing `open` / `library` branch, so a bare `open` and every `?scope=` still parse as before, `library?stem=` works too (the two are synonyms everywhere else and a silently-ignored stem on one of them is the kind of asymmetry nobody would guess), and a `t` that is missing, unparseable, negative, NaN, or infinite degrades to open-without-seek rather than to no navigation. The router does **not** resolve the stem: a citation click usually wakes a Library that has never scanned, and `MeetingStore` scans asynchronously from the window's `onAppear`, so "no such meeting" and "not scanned yet" look identical at that instant and collapsing them would send every valid link to the quiet no-match open. Instead `Coordinator+Automation` sets `LibraryWindowModel.pendingTranscriptJump` and shows the window; the pure `Automation/TranscriptDeeplink.resolve` answers `openMeeting` / `libraryOnly` / `wait` against the loaded list, `LibraryRootView` re-asks it on every store revision until it is decidable, and `MeetingDetailView` consumes the request (guarded on the stem, so a request meant for another meeting cannot seek in this one) into FEAT10's `pendingSeek` seam.

Render: `render_summary_md` gained an optional `deeplink_stem`, passed by the filesystem sink, the LAN sink, `summarize`'s stored `<stem>.summary.md`, and `publish-from-paste` (a no-op there today, since a pasted summary carries no anchors, but the two writers of that one file now spell it the same way). Notion is untouched and pinned untouched. Three spellings are contract rather than taste, all documented in CONVENTIONS: `t=` keeps millisecond precision with trailing zeros stripped, because `TranscriptSegmentLookup` picks the last segment starting at or before `t` and truncating an anchor snapped to a 754.32 s segment start would land the jump on the row *before* the cited one; the stem is percent-encoded down to the RFC 3986 unreserved set (Swift has to spell that set out in ASCII, since `CharacterSet.alphanumerics` would leave Cyrillic raw while Python encodes it); and the link syntax replaces the outer brackets rather than nesting inside them, because a leading `[[` is an Obsidian wikilink. The CI3 golden gained a `deeplink_stem` case (a stem with a space and Cyrillic, fractional anchors) and the Swift reader fails if that case ever disappears.

One thing the spec assumed was not true, and it is the important one: **the Obsidian sink never went through `render_summary_md`**. It renders its own user-templatable note, so FEAT10's plain ` [mm:ss]` suffixes had never appeared in an Obsidian note at all. Since Obsidian is the sink this task exists for (and the acceptance says a republished note carries the links), it now renders the shared `evidence_suffix` per section, which adds anchors *and* links to that sink in one step. A summary with no anchors still renders byte-identically, pinned by a test.

**Owner-owed:** the leg the acceptance reserves, click a `[mm:ss]` in a real Obsidian note on this Mac and land on the cited transcript row. Not exercisable here (Launch Services URL delivery is not drivable in this harness and the menu-bar app is not screenshotable). It needs one `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, since the new verb is code, not Info.plist, plus a republish of a meeting that actually has anchors, since existing notes carry the old plain suffixes until they are rewritten.

Acceptance: parse tests pin the happy path, percent-encoded stems, missing and malformed t, and no regression on the shipped verbs (the MeetingPipeAppIntentsTests vocabulary fence stays green). A router-level test pins known-stem to Transcript-tab-with-seek-pending and unknown-stem to Library-without-seek. A republished Obsidian note carries the links and the Notion output is unchanged, both fixture-pinned; CI3 golden regenerated; both suites and truth fences green. Owner-owed: click a link in a real Obsidian note on this Mac and land on the cited transcript row.

**[DONE] PIPE11 (P2): Regenerate correctness: same-stem serialization, provenance, policy snapshot.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-23 (event-log forensics on stem `20260723-103118`, 2026-07-23 assessment session). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**PIPE11 (P2, new): a regenerate can race a concurrent writer, lies about its engine afterwards, and can straddle a policy change mid-chain.** Three defects, one path, all observed in production logs on 2026-07-23.

Context, the observed incident. The regenerate path (`MeetingLibraryService.regenerateMeeting`, Library/MeetingLibraryService.swift:124-159) spawns `mp summarize [--backend X]` directly (`PipelineLauncher.summarize`, PipelineLauncher.swift:477-485) and never enters the `SinkDispatcher` `ProcessingJob` queue, so it runs concurrently with an active run-all and with other regenerates for the same stem; nothing keys on stem to block, drop, or coalesce. On 2026-07-23 (all times UTC): 07:46:15 Reprocess enqueued a run-all; 07:46:26 a regenerate spawned concurrently against the same stem; 07:48:43 a second regenerate spawned (NDA still on, clamped local); 07:49:00 the workflow was reassigned to General (nda=false); 07:49:06 a third regenerate spawned (now genuinely Anthropic). The second (local) writer finished ~9 s before the third (Anthropic) one; had the ordering flipped, a stale local summary would have silently overwritten the Sonnet summary the owner had already seen. Notion received the stale local content first (07:49:19, page slug `Daily-Stand-up-Meeting-Summary`) and the Anthropic upsert 14 s later (07:49:35, slug `Daily-Stand-Up-DMS-5-12-Hotfix-Auth-Epic`), same page id. Writes are individually atomic (PIPE8's `storage.atomic_write_text`), so this is last-writer-wins, not corruption; the defect is that "last" is a coin flip.

Defect 2, provenance. `<stem>.run.json` (backend, model) is written only by `orchestrate.run_all` via `corrections.write_run_sidecar` (pipeline/src/mp/corrections.py:51); a standalone `mp summarize` returns `SummaryOutput` with the true `backend`/`model` (summarize.py:469-476) and throws it away. After the 07:49 Anthropic regenerate, `run.json` on disk still read `backend=local, model=mlx-community/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit, ts=07:48:04`, so the Library detail header showed "On-device (MLX)" over a Sonnet summary (`MeetingStore` reads run.json backend at MeetingStore.swift:635). The same stale attribution poisons the corrections corpus LOCAL9 trains on (records resolve backend from the run sidecar).

Defect 3, policy snapshot. Each spawned subprocess re-reads `<stem>.meta.json` at its own `entry.prepare`, so a regenerate-then-republish chain started under one policy can publish under another: the 07:48:43 regenerate summarized under the NDA clamp (local backend, filesystem sinks), but its republish leg spawned at 07:49:18, after the reassign, re-read the now-General meta and pushed that stale local summary to cloud Notion. Direction of the leak was benign here (the owner had just de-NDA'd deliberately); the inverse direction is the one to close cheaply: a chain started pre-NDA must not egress a summary after the meeting was moved INTO an NDA workflow mid-chain.

Scope. (a) Per-stem serialization: route Library regenerate/republish through the `SinkDispatcher` queue as a lightweight job kind (preferred: it buys UX28's `activeProcessing` visibility and run-all's cancel for free and keeps one execution lane per stem), or, if the queue coupling proves heavy, a per-stem async mutex in `MeetingLibraryService` with coalescing (a second identical request while one is pending is dropped with an event). Same-stem ordering is the invariant; cross-stem concurrency stays as-is. (b) Provenance: standalone `mp summarize` rewrites the run sidecar on success with the `SummaryOutput` backend/model (reuse `corrections.write_run_sidecar`; preserve the existing `publish_state` via `corrections.set_publish_state` semantics rather than resetting it), and a `--candidate` run (TECH-A16 preview) explicitly does not touch it; the Swift badge then stays truthful with no daemon change. (c) Policy: with (a) in place the reassign action joins the same per-stem lane (reassign is already a Library action), which closes the TOCTOU structurally; the acceptance scenario below pins the INTO-NDA direction regardless of which mechanism lands.

Explicitly not: no changes to `config.effective_backend` or the PIPE6 one-shot override semantics (the NDA clamp is deliberate and stays); no cross-stem global lock; no UI work (UX28 owns surfaces; this task is correctness even if UX28 never lands); no rewrite of `publish_router` idempotency (it already upserts correctly once ordering is fixed).

Acceptance. Pipeline: a test pins that `mp summarize` on success rewrites run.json with the answering backend/model and leaves `publish_state` intact, and that `--candidate` leaves run.json untouched; ruff + pyright + pytest green. Daemon: a test pins that a regenerate requested while a same-stem job is active does not spawn concurrently (queued or coalesced, with the event emitted), and that requests for different stems still overlap; a scenario test pins that a chain started before a reassign INTO an NDA workflow cannot publish to a cloud sink after the reassign (fake launcher + meta rewrite mid-chain). Events: reuse the existing coordinator category for the queued/coalesced action; CONVENTIONS table row in the same commit if a new action name is added. Full daemon suite green. Owner eyeball: after an Anthropic re-summarize of an NDA-turned-General meeting, the detail header badge reads Anthropic, and run.json matches.

**[DONE] UX28 (P2): Library processing visibility and control.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-23 (owner findings, 2026-07-23 assessment session; event-log forensics on stem `20260723-103118`). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**UX28 (P2, new): every Library-triggered job is visible while it runs and stoppable when it should not be.** The owner hit all three gaps in one session on 2026-07-23: a mistaken Reprocess could not be cancelled for its whole ~110 s run, a Re-summarize clicked mid-reprocess produced no visible effect at all ("It looks like nothing happened"), and nothing distinguished a queued job from a finished one. PRODUCT.md's truthful-states principle is the bar; PIPE10's out-of-scope note already anticipated this class ("the Library row keeps showing Failed for the ~40 s between the Retry click and run_started, which reads as retry did nothing").

Context, the verified gaps (line refs as of 2026-07-23). (1) Cancel plumbing exists end to end (`LibraryWindowModel.cancelProcessing` LibraryWindow.swift:237-239 -> `Coordinator+MenuActions.swift:94-96` -> `SinkDispatcher.cancelActiveJob` SinkDispatcher.swift:212-216 -> `PipelineLauncher.cancelActiveRun` PipelineLauncher.swift:276-284, SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 10 s, job completes as a retryable failure) but the only UI that reaches it renders under a stalled heartbeat: `MeetingRow.processingIndicator` shows the Cancel button only when `p.stalled` (MeetingRow.swift:337-346, 30 s threshold at SinkDispatcher.swift:37). A healthy job shows an elapsed-time pill and nothing else. (2) Queued-but-not-started jobs have no visible state and cannot be removed: `SinkDispatcher.enqueue` appends unconditionally (SinkDispatcher.swift:61-72) and the only dequeue is `removeFirst()` inside `completeActiveJob` (SinkDispatcher.swift:179-181). A second Reprocess click silently enqueues a duplicate. (3) The regenerate/republish path publishes no state anywhere: `activeProcessing` (LibraryWindow.swift:72-77) is fed only by run-all progress callbacks (Coordinator.swift:300-319); the row spinner `inFlight` is view-local `@State` set only by the row context menu's own actions (MeetingRow.swift:31, 468-491); the detail-menu "Re-summarize with ..." (`MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:407-411`) fires a fire-and-forget Task with no spinner, no toast, no completion signal, and only one variant alerts on failure (SummaryTab.swift:487-492). On 2026-07-23 the regenerate's only observable effect was an `idempotent: true` republish 100 s after the click.

Scope, five legs, smallest-change each. (a) Always-visible Cancel for the active job: the row's processing indicator and the detail header surface Cancel whenever `activeProcessing` matches the stem, healthy or stalled, wired to the existing `cancelProcessing()`; keep the Stalled pill semantics unchanged. (b) Pending-queue truth: queued stems render a quiet "Queued" state (the row already receives `activeProcessing`; extend the published surface with the pending stems from `SinkDispatcher.processingJobs`) and a dequeue affordance removes a not-yet-started job (new `SinkDispatcher.removePending(id:)`, emitting a `pipeline_dequeued` event on the existing coordinator category). (c) Published per-stem busy state for regenerate/republish: replace the view-local `inFlight` with a `@Published` per-stem state set by `MeetingLibraryService.regenerateMeeting`/`republishMeeting` so BOTH affordances (detail menu and row context menu, plus SummaryTab's variant) render the same "Summarizing with Anthropic..." / "Publishing..." chip in the row and the detail header; label carries the requested engine. (d) Completion and failure feedback: regenerate/republish completion routes through the same surface the run-all queue already uses (`PipelineJobDispatcher`'s done-notification / error-banner closures) so success is visible from anywhere and failure is not silent; unify the one-variant NSAlert. (e) Cancellable regenerate: `PipelineLauncher` retains spawned summarize/publish processes per stem (today `retainForCancel: true` is passed only by `runAll`, PipelineLauncher.swift:694, 312) so the busy chip from (c) can offer Cancel; termination follows the existing SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL shape and surfaces as a normal failure with retry.

Interplay: PIPE11 (filed the same day) owns same-stem serialization and provenance; if PIPE11 routes regenerate through the SinkDispatcher queue, leg (c) collapses into the `activeProcessing` surface and leg (e) inherits run-all's existing cancel; whichever task lands second reconciles, and the acceptance bars below hold either way.

Explicitly not: no progress percentages (stage + elapsed from the existing heartbeat is the register); no dedupe/coalescing logic (PIPE11); no NDA-specific affordances (UX29); no new config knobs; no cancel for the in-process ANE transcription stage (it is not a subprocess; out of scope until it hurts, note it in the ship if the boundary is visible in testing).

Acceptance. Swift tests pin: the presentation model shows Cancel for a healthy active job and for a stalled one; a pending job renders Queued and `removePending` drops it exactly once with the event emitted; the per-stem busy state is set and cleared by regenerate and republish from both affordances (fake launcher), including the failure path; a cancelled regenerate completes as a retryable failure and clears the busy state. Events: `pipeline_cancelled` (existing) fires from the always-visible button; `pipeline_dequeued` is new on the existing category (CONVENTIONS event-table row in the same commit; `scripts/truth_fences.py events` green). Full daemon suite green; no pipeline-side changes. Owner eyeball: click Reprocess on a healthy meeting and cancel it within 5 s; click Re-summarize from the detail menu and watch the chip appear, complete, and toast.

**[DONE] FEAT11 (P2): In-app context instruments (glossary editor, voice-resolution surface, context nudges).**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-23 (owner ask, 2026-07-23 assessment session; owner's framing verbatim: "I want the application to provide me instruments so I can do things", nothing done at any level other than the app itself). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**FEAT11 (P2, new): the three cheapest summary-quality levers exist only as hand-edited config or are invisible; give each an in-app instrument.** These levers move BOTH backends and disproportionately help the small local model, because they turn facts the model must infer (who is speaking, what "PS for Venusaur" was supposed to be, what this team's vocabulary means) into facts written in the transcript. The owner's operating rule is that no lever should require editing a TOML or running a CLI.

Context, current state per lever (verified 2026-07-23). (1) Glossary (ASR1): fully built pipeline-side (`mp.glossary`, deterministic normalization at finalize, global `[terms]` + per-workflow `[workflow."<name>".terms]`, optional `[fuzzy]`), but it has zero daemon UI (re-checked at pickup 2026-07-28: "glossary" does hit 11 times in daemon/Sources, but every one is prose, doc comments and UI hint strings about the ASR3 reprocess flow in `BatchActionsPane`, `PipelineLauncher`, `LibraryWindow`, `MeetingDetailView+Header`, and `Library/MeetingLibraryService`; there was no glossary editing UI and no `glossary.toml` reader or writer anywhere daemon-side, so the finding stands) and zero presence on the owner's Mac (`~/.config/meeting-pipe/glossary.toml` does not exist), so ASR garbles like "Resolve PS for Venusaur ticket" (stem `20260723-103118`, local summary) reach both backends raw. (2) Voice naming: the instruments exist (TranscriptTab in-app naming enrolls the voiceprint, FEAT3; Preferences People pane manages the roster) and the owner's roster.json is populated (45 KB, last written 2026-07-16), yet that meeting still surfaced `THEM-B`/`THEM-C` and NO surface says whether roster matching ran, matched, or missed, so the owner cannot tell "not enrolled" from "enrolled but unmatched" without reading sidecars. (3) Workflow context: the editor exists (`WorkflowsView.swift:375-393`, Context prompt group with a hint) but both of the owner's NDA "Client work" workflows carry an empty `context_prompt`, so NDA meetings summarize with no team context at all; nothing nudges toward what good context contains.

Scope. (a) Glossary editor: a Vocabulary surface (Preferences, Pipeline pane or a sibling) that lists wrong -> right term pairs, a global table plus an optional per-workflow section, reading and writing `~/.config/meeting-pipe/glossary.toml` with the ConfigStore TOML round-trip idiom (unknown keys and the `[fuzzy]` section survive untouched; `glossary.example.toml` stays the documented reference). Inline hint: terms apply at finalize, so already-processed meetings pick them up on Reprocess (and in bulk only via ASR3). A small "add to vocabulary" affordance from the Transcript tab's existing text-correction flow (PIPE9) may pre-fill the pair from an edit; keep it a pre-fill, not an auto-write. (b) Voice-resolution surface: in the meeting detail, show the cast as resolved names vs unresolved cluster labels (the data is already in the transcript + speaker overlay), with a one-click path into the existing TranscriptTab naming flow for each unresolved voice; surface the roster-match outcome for the meeting (matched n of m voices) from the pipeline's existing events or, if no durable record exists, name that gap at pickup and add the smallest sidecar field or event that carries it. (c) Context nudges: an empty `context_prompt` renders placeholder guidance naming what actually helps (people and roles, product and ticket vocabulary, meeting cadence), and the workflow list shows a quiet hint chip on workflows with empty context; no new storage, no auto-fill.

Explicitly not: cross-meeting frequency mining ("this unnamed voice appeared in 6 meetings", needs embedding correlation across the library; park until the per-meeting surface exists); auto-suggested glossary terms from the corrections corpus (real idea, separate filing once the editor exists); glossary application at display time (finalize-only is the ASR1 contract and keeps transcripts deterministic); editing roster embeddings or thresholds in-app (DIAR2 owns matching quality); any change to what `mp.glossary` or `mp.roster` compute.

**Progress 2026-07-28 (shipped, owner-owed on the eyeball).** All three legs built with their UI; see the ToC row for the full note. What is worth carrying forward beyond it:

- Leg (b) needed **no sidecar or event change at all**, so the clause reserving "the smallest sidecar field or event that carries it" was not exercised and should not be read as owed. `orchestrate._write_embeddings_sidecar` keys `<stem>.embeddings.json` by the FINAL label, so the sidecar's key set already is the roster-match outcome (owner label / roster name / `THEM-x`), and it is never rewritten by in-app naming. `VoiceResolution.derive` reads it against `RosterProfile.people()` and `summarization.user_label`.
- `glossary-golden.json` is a fourth **generated** CI4 fixture. Regenerate it like the others (`cd pipeline && uv run python ../scripts/gen_contract_fixtures.py`) after any change to `mp.glossary.load_glossary`; `test_ci4_contracts.py` fails if you forget and `CI4ContractFixtureTests` fails if Swift no longer agrees.
- One hazard neither side can pin: two glossary keys that differ only in case are folded by both readers, and "last wins" means document order in Python against toml++'s key order in Swift. The editor never writes that shape (`GlossaryStore.liveTerms` dedupes by folded key), so it can only arrive by hand-editing.
- Not built: the optional "add to vocabulary" pre-fill off PIPE9. Reason in the ToC row. If it is ever picked up, the constraint that decides its shape is the spec's own "keep it a pre-fill, not an auto-write", which the current store cannot express (every row it holds is written on the debounce).

Acceptance. Daemon tests pin: glossary TOML round-trip (unknown keys + `[fuzzy]` survive; per-workflow table wins on a clash exactly as `mp.glossary` resolves it, pinned against the Python reader with a shared fixture in the CI4 idiom if practical, otherwise a mirrored unit pair); the voice-resolution presentation model (resolved vs unresolved rows, deep-link target); the empty-context hint logic. Suites + `scripts/truth_fences.py config` green (glossary keys stay documented). Owner eyeball: define "Venusaur" -> the intended term in-app, Reprocess `20260723-103118`, and the garble is gone from transcript and summary; name one `THEM-*` voice from the detail surface and see the cast row flip to the name.

**[DONE] UX42 (P2): Launch-at-login toggle truthfulness (one mechanism owns login).**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner report, item 12: "regardless this toggle checked or not (it is not on my app) app is started at login"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

Root cause confirmed 2026-07-29, and it is two mechanisms that have never met:

- **What actually starts the app at login**: the launchd user agent `install.sh` writes at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.meetingpipe.daemon.plist` (:483-489 from `scripts/launchd.plist.template`), loaded with `launchctl load -w` (:531) and kickstarted (:539). The template carries `RunAtLoad=true` and `KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit=false}` (template :17-23), and the comment at :14-16 shows both are deliberate design (TECH-UX7: a clean quit exits fully, a crash relaunches). `rebuild.sh:75-88` re-bootstraps the same plist on every dev rebuild, so the agent is continuously refreshed.
- **What the toggle controls**: `LaunchAtLoginService` wraps `SMAppService.mainApp` only (`LaunchAtLoginService.swift:7-9` status-derived read, :17-31 register/unregister with errors swallowed to the log), surfaced in Preferences General (`PreferencesView+General.swift:7`, :93-101) with a footer that says "Registers MeetingPipe with macOS via SMAppService" (:47). Honest about SMAppService; blind to launchd.

Turning the toggle off unregisters an SMAppService entry that was never what launched the app, and leaves the agent armed. Nothing in the app can remove the agent (only `uninstall.sh:70-71` boots it out); `LaunchAgentScheduler`'s digest/backup agents are clean (`StartCalendarInterval` only, no RunAtLoad, and they run `mp`, not the app). The repo even records the split: `docs/backlog/q3-final.md:564`.

One sharp edge to carry: the agent label and the app bundle id are the same string, `com.meetingpipe.daemon` (`install.sh:189`, `Endpoints.swift:6`, template :7), which makes `launchctl print` output and System Settings Login Items entries ambiguous, and makes any dual-registration state (agent + SMAppService both on) look like one entry when it is two.

## Scope

Make exactly one mechanism own login-start, and make the toggle drive it. Recommendation, recorded with the reasoning so pickup does not re-derive it:

**The LaunchAgent owns everything; SMAppService usage is removed.** Reasons: the agent's `KeepAlive` crash-relaunch is deliberate TECH-UX7 design and only supervises agent-started instances, so login-starting via SMAppService would bypass the supervision the product wants; install, rebuild, and uninstall already manage the agent end to end; and two registration systems is the bug this task exists to kill.

- Toggle ON: ensure the plist exists and run `launchctl enable gui/$UID/com.meetingpipe.daemon` (bootstrap if not loaded).
- Toggle OFF: `launchctl disable gui/$UID/com.meetingpipe.daemon`. Disable, not bootout: booting out the agent that owns the running process kills the app under the user's pointer; disable prevents the next login-start and leaves the running instance alone. Decide-and-record whether to also rewrite the plist's `RunAtLoad` to match (belt), noting `launchctl`'s disabled-overrides DB survives plist rewrites either way.
- The toggle's read path reports the real state (`launchctl print-disabled gui/$UID` parsed, or the service's own status query), so the control cannot lie again. Errors surface in the footer instead of being swallowed.
- `install.sh` and `rebuild.sh` respect an existing disabled state: replace `load -w` with a bootstrap that does not force-enable (the `-w` write is exactly what would re-arm a toggled-off install on the next rebuild).
- `LaunchAtLoginService` becomes the wrapper over this (rename or repurpose), with the launchctl invocations behind an injected runner so the state machine is unit-testable. Footer copy updated to name what it really does.
- README and SETUP.md's login/quit semantics paragraphs update in the same commit (DOC10 rule); note for a future D8/notarized world that SMAppService with System Settings visibility could be revisited, so the alternative is recorded, not lost.

## Explicitly not in scope

Renaming the agent label or bundle id (a migration with real breakage risk; the collision is documented here as a known sharp edge instead). Changing TECH-UX7's quit/crash-relaunch semantics. Uninstall behavior. The digest/backup scheduler agents.

## Acceptance

Unit tests over the service with an injected launchctl runner: ON from disabled runs enable (and bootstraps when missing), OFF runs disable and never bootout, state reads reflect the runner's canned print-disabled output, a runner failure surfaces as a user-visible error string.

A script-level assertion (or documented manual step in the PR) that `install.sh` over a disabled agent leaves it disabled.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green (baseline at filing: 1770). Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball, two halves: toggle OFF, `launchctl print-disabled gui/$(id -u)` lists `"com.meetingpipe.daemon" => disabled`, the running app stays alive, and after the next real login the app has not started; toggle ON and the next login starts it. A crash (kill -9) still relaunches when the toggle is ON.

## Progress (2026-07-31): shipped, the eyeball is owner-owed

Everything but the owner eyeball is in, and the eyeball is the one part no session can do: it needs a real logout, and the session deliberately never ran a mutating `launchctl` against the real service (that would change whether the owner's app starts at their next login, as a side effect of a test). `swift build` clean, `swift test` green at 1997 (1980 before, 17 new), `bash scripts/test-login-agent-guard.sh` 9/9, truth fences and both dash guards clean, `bash -n` on all four touched shell scripts; no Python touched, its suite re-confirmed at 1157.

The spec's recommended direction held up under implementation and shipped as written. `LaunchAtLoginService` is now a value type over an injected `LaunchctlRunning`, exposing `status()` and `set(enabled:)` returning a `LaunchAtLoginStatus` (a three-case `LaunchAtLoginState` plus an optional user-visible error). `ProcessLaunchctl` is the real runner, and the tests never construct it, which is the point: running the suite can never change whether the developer's own Mac starts MeetingPipe at the next login.

**The one delegated decision, and its answer: `RunAtLoad` is not rewritten.** Three concrete reasons, none of them visible from the spec alone. (1) The belt is the *weaker* of the two mechanisms, not the stronger: `install.sh` regenerates the plist from `scripts/launchd.plist.template` on every run, so a `RunAtLoad=false` write survives exactly until the next install, while the disabled-overrides database survives it. (2) A rewritten plist only takes effect after a bootout + bootstrap, which is precisely the app-killing move the disable-not-bootout rule exists to avoid, so the belt cannot be fastened without the harm. (3) `rebuild.sh` relies on `RunAtLoad` to bring the daemon back after its bootout, so `RunAtLoad=false` would leave a dev rebuild with the daemon down and the script's own `pgrep` verification dying. One writer, one reader.

**Reads.** `status()` shells `launchctl print-disabled gui/<uid>` and parses the label's line. A label with **no** override line is `enabled`, because that is what launchd means by absence, and reading absence as off would make every fresh install's toggle claim the app does not start when it does. A missing plist reads `notInstalled` and calls no launchctl at all. An unreadable `print-disabled` falls back to the plist's own `RunAtLoad` intent **and says so in the footer** ("The switch shows the launch agent's own setting, which may not match"), because presenting an unread state as a confident one is the original bug in miniature.

**Writes.** ON runs `enable`, then `print` to see whether the job is loaded, then `bootstrap` only if it is not; order matters, since bootstrapping a still-disabled service fails. OFF runs `disable` and nothing else. A refused write re-reads launchd and reports what it is actually holding rather than what was asked for, with the launchctl exit status and stderr in the message. `test_neither_direction_ever_uses_a_destructive_verb` pins the whole rule against `bootout` / `unload` / `kill` / `kickstart` / `remove` in both directions.

**The UI is a `@StateObject`, not `@State`.** `LaunchAtLoginModel` holds the status. A `@State` initial-value expression is re-evaluated on every re-render of the enclosing view, and `ConfigStore` publishes on every keystroke in this pane's hotkey fields, so `@State private var x = LaunchAtLoginService().status()` would have meant one `launchctl` subprocess per character typed. `@StateObject` takes an autoclosure SwiftUI calls once per view identity.

**The shell half.** `scripts/lib/login-agent.sh` is a new sourced helper with two functions: `login_agent_disabled_in_output` (a pure text predicate) and `login_agent_disabled` (the launchctl query over it). The split is what made the acceptance's "script-level assertion that install.sh over a disabled agent leaves it disabled" testable without running an installer on the owner's machine: `scripts/test-login-agent-guard.sh` feeds the predicate nine canned cases (the disabled override, an explicit enabled one, an absent label, empty output, a prefix-colliding sibling in both directions, launchctl's spacing, and two truncated lines that must fail *closed*), invokes no launchctl, and mutates nothing. It is now a mandatory gate in the root `CLAUDE.md` verify table, the way `test-prune-worktrees.sh` is.

`install.sh`'s `launchctl load -w` became a plain `bootstrap` inside a disabled guard, and its final "MeetingPipe is running in your menu bar" line is now conditional, because with the agent disabled nothing started it and saying otherwise is the same class of untruth. `rebuild.sh` branches too: with the agent disabled it pkills and `open`s the app directly rather than bootstrapping (which would fail on a disabled service and `die` on a state the owner chose on purpose), and the existing `pgrep` verification covers both paths.

**Cost recorded rather than lost:** dropping SMAppService means MeetingPipe no longer appears under System Settings ▸ General ▸ Login Items, so there is no system-level surface for the switch. That is written into the service's doc comment as worth revisiting in a notarized, Developer-ID world (D8), where SMAppService could own login-start and the agent could shrink to supervision alone. It is not worth two mechanisms today. The label / bundle-id collision was carried unchanged, as the spec directed.

**Noted and deliberately not fixed here:** `uninstall.sh` boots out the agent and removes the plist but never clears the disabled override, so an uninstall followed by a reinstall keeps launch at login off. That is arguably the right behaviour (the override is the owner's stated preference, and it is keyed on the label, not the plist), and "Uninstall behavior" is explicitly out of this task's scope, so it is named here rather than changed.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Added 2026-07-31, per the 2026-07-30 standing rule: every task gated on an owner action carries one. Walk the owner through it step by step; the owner does not read code. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts. This one needs two real logouts, so it is worth doing in one sitting at the end of a day.

The one command the owner needs, used several times below. It prints what launchd will do at the next login, and it changes nothing:

```sh
launchctl print-disabled gui/$(id -u) | grep meetingpipe
```

2. [owner] Open **Preferences ▸ General ▸ Startup** and read the grey text under the two switches. Pass: it talks about a launch agent and about what happens when you quit. If it still says "Registers MeetingPipe with macOS via SMAppService", you are on the old build; redo step 1.
3. [owner] Before touching anything, run the command above. Pass: it prints `"com.meetingpipe.daemon" => enabled`, or prints nothing at all (which also means enabled), matching the switch being on. This is the check that used to fail: the switch and the machine disagreeing is the whole bug.
4. [owner] Turn **Launch at login** OFF. Three things to look at, in order. Pass: (a) MeetingPipe is **still running** in your menu bar, it must not vanish; (b) the grey line under the switch now reads "MeetingPipe only starts when you launch it manually."; (c) the command above now prints `"com.meetingpipe.daemon" => disabled`.
5. [owner] With it still off, run `./scripts/rebuild.sh`. Pass: it says launch at login is off and that it is relaunching the app directly, it finishes without an error, MeetingPipe is running again, and the command above still prints `=> disabled`. (Before this task a rebuild here would have failed outright.)
6. [owner] Still off, run `./scripts/install.sh`. This is the check the acceptance names, and the one that could not be tested from a session without running an installer on your Mac. Pass: near the end it says launch at login is off and the agent is left disabled, the final summary does **not** claim MeetingPipe is running in your menu bar, and the command above still prints `=> disabled`. (You may need to open the app yourself afterwards.)
7. [owner] Log out and log back in. **Pass: MeetingPipe does not start.** This is the original report, in reverse: the toggle now means what it says.
8. [owner] Open MeetingPipe yourself from `~/Applications`. Turn **Launch at login** back ON. Pass: the grey line goes back to "will start automatically when you log in", and the command above prints `=> enabled`.
9. [owner] Log out and log back in again. **Pass: MeetingPipe starts on its own.**
10. [owner] Last one, the crash check, so the fix did not cost the TECH-UX7 safety net. In a terminal: `kill -9 $(pgrep -f "MeetingPipe.app/Contents/MacOS/MeetingPipe")`. Pass: the menu-bar icon comes back within about ten seconds.
11. Steps 3 to 10 passing moves UX42 to done. Worth knowing rather than testing: with launch at login OFF, **Quit MeetingPipe** really quits, because the relaunch-after-quit behaviour is the same launch agent and it is not running the app. That is stated in the Preferences footer, the README, and `docs/SETUP.md`.

**[DONE] LOCAL16 (P1): Local-LLM resource protection: RAM tiers, fail-closed spawn, free-RAM watchdog.**
Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 8: "check the available resources, and limit the capabilities to certain threshold of memory... make it crystall clear to the user... and make a system 100% protected from hangs and out of memory things"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

P1 because the broken promise is that on-device processing degrades by refusing with a reason, never by hanging the machine, and the machine has been taken down twice: the 14B OOM-hung this 32 GB Mac at long context (recorded in the `local_model` default's own comment, `config.py:123-127`, and AI2's measurements), and the 2026-07-29 `mp ask` incident ended in a hard reboot (AI11 carries that trace). The owner may re-band.

## Context

What exists today, verified 2026-07-29:

- **The only RAM check in the product is `mp doctor`**: `_estimate_model_gb` (0.62 GB per billion params, `doctor.py:287-300`), `_physical_ram_gb` via `sysctl hw.memsize` (:303-317), compared in `check_local_stack` (:375-387) as fail / warn(+4 GB headroom) / ok. It is advisory, manual-only, against TOTAL physical RAM (not free), and nothing in `run-all`, `summarize`, `serve-local`, or `ask` calls it.
- **No free-RAM watchdog is shipped anywhere.** The protocol exists as a shell snippet in the LOCAL13 bench doc (`docs/spikes/local13-local-model-refresh-bench.md:215-234`: kill `mlx_lm.server` below 10% free, `vm_stat`-based) and as AI2's harness-local guard; neither ever became product code. Grep for `vm_stat` / `psutil` / `hw.memsize` outside doctor: zero hits.
- **The server spawn has no memory levers and hides its death note.** `build_server_command` emits only model/host/port/adapter (`summarize_local.py:255-276`); no `--max-kv-size`, no cache limit. Spawned with `stdout=DEVNULL, stderr=STDOUT` (:736-737), so an OOM message from the server is discarded, and the failure surfaces as the generic "exited during startup (rc=...). Check that the model name resolves and you have enough RAM" guess (:765-768).
- **The user-facing limits are static prose.** `LocalModelPreset.all` (`PreferencesWindow.swift:93-118`) hardcodes "~2 GB / ~4.3 GB / ~8 GB" and "wants 24 GB+ RAM (can OOM on 16 GB)" as strings; nothing reads the machine. `ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory` is used nowhere in the app (only inside vendored FluidAudio).
- **The precedent for a fail-closed refusal already exists at the right seam**: `_spawn` refuses an uncached model under the egress guard with an actionable message Swift pattern-matches (`summarize_local.py:721-731`), mirrored by `mp serve-local` (:1029-1039). A RAM-tier refusal is the same shape at the same seams.
- **Measured numbers to build the tier table from**: 4-bit resident ~0.55-0.62 GB/B params (LOCAL13 :79, doctor's estimator); 7B ~4.3 GB measured; 14B ~8 GB, "OOM-unsafe above ~13k-char transcripts" on 32 GB (engine-comparison.md:11, :25); MoE 17-20 GB excluded outright (LOCAL13 :90); AI2's context boundaries (14B fine at 4K, watchdog-abort at 8K, OOM at 16K).

## Scope

1. **A shared resource-guard module** (`pipeline/src/mp/resource_guard.py` or similar): physical-RAM read, a free-memory sampler (`vm_stat` pages-free+purgeable derived, cheap enough per-batch), a pure tier policy (physical RAM to max advisable model GB and a context-token ceiling), and a watchdog helper that aborts the owning run with a typed, surfaced error when free memory crosses the floor (default 10%, config-backed, documented in `config.example.toml` per CI5). Pure `decide` separated from sampling so the policy is table-tested.
2. **Fail-closed spawn.** `_spawn` and `mp serve-local` refuse a model whose estimate exceeds the tier for this machine, with the `summarize_local.py:721-731` message shape naming the smaller preset ("This Mac has 16 GB; the 14B preset needs about 24 GB. Pick Small or Recommended in Preferences > Pipeline."). An explicit override env (`MP_RAM_GUARD=0`) for bench runs, documented as owner-dev.
3. **Watchdog on the paths that can swap the machine**: the local summarize request loop and AI11's embed/answer path consume the same helper; an abort emits a `pipeline` event and writes the failure sidecar naming memory as the stage, so the Library row's failed state says why.
4. **Surfaced limits.** The Preferences preset picker reads `ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory` and annotates each preset live ("fits comfortably" / "little headroom" / "needs ~24 GB; this Mac has 16"), graying the over-tier preset with the reason (truthful-disabled, the UX30 rule). `LocalModelPreloader.shouldPreload` (already a pure gate, `LocalModelPreloader.swift:64-66`) gains the same term so a warm server is never preloaded over tier. `mp doctor` keeps the deep check and gains the tier line. SETUP.md's model-choice paragraph updates in the ship commit (DOC10 rule).
5. **Capture the server's stderr** to a rotated log file (or the existing pipeline log) instead of DEVNULL, so the next OOM postmortem has the actual message.

## Explicitly not in scope

Automatic model downgrade or dynamic quantization fallback (refusal with a named alternative is the contract; silent substitution hides the quality change). MLX cache-limit tuning experiments beyond what AI11 needs (`mx.clear_cache` between embed batches is AI11's leg; a server-side cache lever, if mlx-lm grows one, is a future amendment). Killing or throttling other processes. The LOCAL13 bench itself and its 12 GB bar (owner-owed there). Context-length truncation policy for single-pass summarize (the 80k threshold stands; the guard aborts before swap rather than silently truncating content).

## Acceptance

Pipeline tests: the pure tier policy table (16/24/32/48 GB against 3B/7B/14B and an unparseable model id); spawn refusal (estimate over tier raises the typed error naming the preset, no `Popen` attempted; override env bypasses); watchdog abort with an injected sampler (floor crossing raises, event emitted, failure sidecar stage says memory); stderr of a failing fake server lands in the log.

Daemon tests: preset annotation derivation per RAM size (pure, table-tested); `LocalModelPreloader.shouldPreload` false when over tier; the grayed preset carries the reason string.

Truth fences green with the new config key(s) documented in `config.example.toml` and README in the same commit. Both suites, ruff, pyright green (baselines at filing: 1770 Swift, 1050 Python).

Owner eyeball on this 32 GB Mac: the 14B preset annotates per the table (fits, with the headroom caveat), a simulated 16 GB tier (env override for the test, or the unit table) refuses it, and a local summarize under artificial memory pressure aborts with the named error instead of beachballing the Mac.

## Progress (shipped 2026-07-30, owner-owed on the eyeball)

All five scope items landed; the status stays `owner-owed` only for the eyeball clause above, which needs a rebuilt app in front of a human and a real memory-pressure run.

**The guard module.** `pipeline/src/mp/resource_guard.py` carries the three pieces separably, because AI11 consumes two of them without wanting the third: the sizing helpers (`estimate_model_gb` / `physical_ram_gb`, promoted out of `doctor`, which was no longer their only reader), the pure tier policy (`tier_for` / `assess` / `refusal_message`), and `MemoryWatchdog`, whose sampler and clock are both injectable and whose `check(stage=)` is throttled so an embed loop can call it per batch without paying for a `vm_stat` per iteration.

**The tier table is anchored on measurements, not on a ratio** (a flat "RAM / 3" was tried first and put the 14B over on 24 GB, contradicting its own shipped copy). Rows: 8 GB admits 2.5 GB / 2K tokens, 16 GB admits 5.0 / 4K, 24 GB admits 9.0 / 4K, 32 GB admits 9.0 / 8K, 48 GB admits 20.0 / 16K. That reproduces every number the product already asserts: the 7B runs on 16 GB but tight, the 14B is refused there ("can OOM on 16 GB"), 24 GB is its floor, and on the owner's 32 GB it is still `tight` rather than comfortable, which is the honest reading of a model that has OOM-hung that exact machine.

**Decided, not in the spec: the guard refuses only what it can measure.** A repo id with no parameter count (any Custom preset) assesses `unknown` and is never refused on size, because guessing that a custom id is too big would close the one escape hatch a user has; the watchdog is the backstop for that case. Same fail-open rule when physical RAM cannot be read.

**Decided, not in the spec: the cross-language marker.** The daemon writes `<stem>.error.json`, not Python, so "failure sidecar naming memory as the stage" is implemented as a new `PipelineFailureSidecar.Stage.memory` that `SinkDispatcher.stage(for:)` selects by matching the phrase `Not enough memory` that both the refusal and the abort carry. That is the UX21 `not in the local HuggingFace cache` arrangement, and CONVENTIONS now records it beside the exit-3 mapping. The exit-3 publish mapping deliberately still wins over the marker.

**Decided, not in the spec: the suite pins the guard off.** A `conftest.py` autouse fixture sets `MP_RAM_GUARD=0`, so no unrelated local-client test can fail because the developer's Mac was under pressure or a CI runner is smaller than the model a fixture names; the two files that test the guard turn it back on and pass an explicit `ram_gb`.

**Also shipped:** the server's stdout and stderr now go to a rotated `~/Library/Logs/MeetingPipe/mlx-server.log` (both from the lazy spawn and, via `dup2` before `execvpe`, from the warm `mp serve-local`), and the startup-failure message quotes that log's tail instead of guessing between two causes. `mp doctor` gained a tier line reading the same policy the spawn enforces, plus the current free-memory reading. `LocalModelPreloader.shouldPreload` gained a `fitsMemory` term. `diarize_cleanup` and `engine` (the `mp ask` answer leg) both build their client on the configured floor.

**Verified:** pipeline ruff + pyright clean, 1131 pipeline tests green (51 new: 43 in `test_resource_guard.py`, 8 in `test_summarize_local.py`); `swift build` clean and 1908 daemon tests green (17 new: 14 in `LocalModelTierTests.swift`, 1 in `LocalModelPreloaderTests.swift`, 4 in `SinkDispatcherTests.swift`, less the signature updates); CI5 truth fences green with `summarization.local_memory_floor_pct` documented in `config.example.toml` and the README reference. Docs: README (config reference, local-model paragraph, two troubleshooting entries), ARCHITECTURE (the `resource_guard` bullet, `LocalModelTier`, the preloader's new gate, the error-sidecar stage vocabulary in two places), CONVENTIONS (the memory-marker contract), `docs/SETUP.md` (step 7's model-choice paragraph), root `daemon/CLAUDE.md` and `pipeline/CLAUDE.md` (file index, promoted helpers), and `design/ui_kits/macos_app/PreferencesWindow.jsx` (the local-model row, which was also still showing the pre-LOCAL6 14B as "Recommended").

**Not done, deliberately:** no golden fixture pins the Swift/Python mirror. The two tier tables are pinned by the same worked rows in both suites and each file names the other, which is the `MuteLabels`-style arrangement rather than the CI4 one; a fixture would be the stronger fence if this table ever starts changing.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts. The owner does not read code; everything below is done from the app or one pasted command.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Preferences > Pipeline > Configure local model. **This step changes a setting, and you have to change it back.** "Configure local model" is only rendered when the summarization backend is already `local` or `auto` (`PreferencesView+Pipeline.swift:47`), so reaching it on a cloud config means switching the **Summarization backend** picker to Local first, which repoints every future meeting's summary at the on-device model. Note what the picker read before you touch it, and set it back the moment step 4 is done; the disclosure disappearing when you do is the same rule, not a fault. (Written without this warning, the step silently moved the owner's daily engine from Anthropic to Qwen 7B on 2026-07-31, and it was caught only because an unrelated `mp ask` answer came back visibly weaker.) Then open the **Local model** menu. On this 32 GB Mac all three presets should be selectable, and the sublabel under the row should end with a sentence about *this* Mac: "Fits comfortably on this Mac (32 GB)" for Small and Recommended, "Runs on this Mac (32 GB) with little headroom" once Large is selected. Nothing should read "wants 24 GB+ RAM" any more, and no row should say 32.0. **Custom being unselectable is not a LOCAL16 defect**: the picker offers it while its setter drops it, which is UX43's filed (c) leg; only the three presets are this step's acceptance.
3. [owner] The refusal is not reproducible on a 32 GB Mac without lying to the app, so it is checked from the pipeline side instead. Paste this and read the last lines: `cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run mp doctor 2>&1 | sed -n '/local summarization stack/,/local model server/p'`. Expect a `memory tier:` line naming 32 GB, the admitted size, and the token ceiling, then a verdict on the configured model, then a `free memory now:` reading. Nothing should fail.
4. [owner] The refusal text itself, on a pretend 16 GB Mac: `cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run python -c "from mp import resource_guard as r; print(r.refusal_message(r.assess('mlx-community/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-4bit', 16.0)))"`. It should name the Mac's 16 GB, say the model needs about 24 GB, and tell you to pick Recommended (Qwen 7B-4bit) in Preferences > Pipeline. If that sentence would confuse you in a Library row, say so and it gets rewritten.
5. [owner] The watchdog under real pressure, the one leg that needs a live run. Start a local summarize (Library > any meeting > Re-summarize with > Local MLX) and, while it runs, push the Mac's free memory under 10%. Use `memory_pressure -p 8 -y 45`, which allocates until free memory is 8% or less (below the 10% floor), holds it there for 45 seconds, then exits and releases. **Do not use `memory_pressure -S`**, which this step originally suggested: `-S` simulates the system's pressure *level* without applying any real pressure, while the watchdog reads actual free pages from `/usr/bin/vm_stat` (`resource_guard.sample_memory`), so the simulated form leaves the reading untouched, the watchdog correctly never trips, and the step reports a failure that is not one. Caught on 2026-07-31 before the owner ran it. Expected: the run stops within a couple of requests with "Not enough memory: free RAM fell to N% during local summarize", the Library row goes to Failed with the reason visible, and **the Mac stays responsive**. A beachball here is the bug this whole task exists to remove, and is worth reporting immediately.
