2. [owner] Open `20260727-103155`, the meeting from the report (7 voices, 3 unnamed), Transcript tab. Pass: every chip is fully readable, none is sliced mid-word, and counting the chips agrees with the "n of m other voices named" line above them.
3. [owner] Narrow the window to its floor. Pass: the chips re-flow onto more rows and stay readable; nothing is cut off at any width.
4. [owner] Say "UX51 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] UX52: The detail view does not refresh when a re-transcribe finishes

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31, owner-reported during FEAT11's walkthrough: "when re-transcribing, UI is not updated after it is ended. I need to switch between tabs to see new version. this something need fixing as well. and this is not the first issue, I need full assessment all over the app for this." Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

A Re-transcribe completes correctly and writes a new transcript, and the open detail view keeps showing the old one. Switching to another tab and back reveals the new text, because the Library's centre column is an `if/else` on `scope` so a tab switch destroys the projection view and rebuilds it from disk (the same property `daemon/CLAUDE.md` documents as the reason run state must not live in that view).

`MeetingLibraryService.retranscribeMeeting` (`Library/MeetingLibraryService.swift:305`) ends by logging `retranscribe_done` (`:334`), and nothing on that path bumps a store revision or otherwise tells the detail view its data changed. So the refresh depends entirely on the user performing an unrelated navigation.

The owner confirmed the workaround works, which is what makes this a visibility defect rather than a data one: the re-transcribe itself is correct, verified the same day when FEAT11's vocabulary test showed "sitting environment" corrected to "staging environment" after a tab switch.

**The owner's framing is the more important half and should not be dropped when this task is picked up:** "this is not the first issue, I need full assessment all over the app for this." A missing refresh is a class, not an incident. This task fixes the reported instance and is explicitly not the sweep; the sweep is `/audit`, offered to the owner on 2026-07-31 and theirs to trigger.

## Scope

Make the re-transcribe completion path publish a change the detail view observes, using whatever mechanism the Library already uses for the writes that *do* refresh correctly. Find that mechanism first rather than inventing one: several operations (rename, enroll, reassign, regenerate) already update the UI without a tab switch, so the correct shape exists in this codebase and the defect is that the re-transcribe path does not use it. Copying the working idiom is the fix; adding a second notification mechanism beside it is not.

The chain to check while there, since re-transcribe touches more than the text: the transcript rows, the cast strip (a re-transcribe re-derives speaker clusters, so `TranscriptOverlayCarry` re-anchors both overlay sidecars and the strip's contents genuinely change), and the header's language and duration lines.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Not the app-wide sweep.** The owner asked for a full assessment and that is `/audit`'s job, owner-triggered. Fixing this instance must not turn into an unbounded refactor of every refresh path; anything else the pickup notices gets named here or filed, not fixed opportunistically.

**Not the re-transcribe itself.** It works, and FEAT11's pass on 2026-07-31 depended on it working.

**Not the tab-switch rebuild behaviour.** The centre column rebuilding on `scope` change is deliberate and load-bearing elsewhere; this task adds a refresh signal, it does not change how views are torn down.

## Acceptance

With a meeting's detail view open on the Transcript tab, a Re-transcribe started from its `...` menu updates the visible transcript when it completes, with no tab switch and no reopening. The cast strip above it reflects the re-derived clusters at the same moment.

A test pins the notification rather than the rendering: completing a re-transcribe publishes the store change the detail view subscribes to. Pin it at the service level, since the window-server behaviour itself is not observable in a test.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green. No em-dashes in changed lines.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Open any meeting, Transcript tab, and run **Re-transcribe...** from its `...` menu. **Stay on that tab and do not touch anything.** Pass: when it finishes, the transcript on screen becomes the new one on its own. Watching without navigating is the entire test, since a tab switch has always worked and is what hid this.
3. [owner] Look at the cast strip above the transcript in the same moment. Pass: it reflects the re-derived voices too, rather than the previous run's.
4. [owner] Say "UX52 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] FEAT12: Add to Vocabulary from a transcript correction

Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, items 15/16; the invisible-capability inventory ranked this the highest-leverage missing bridge). Revisits the optional leg FEAT11 (shipped 2026-07-28) deliberately did not build; its scope note records why, and those reasons are honored below as constraints. Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

The Vocabulary teaches the transcriber recurring fixes, but the only way terms get in is a user remembering a garble, opening Preferences, and typing both sides from memory. The moment they actually know the pair is when they fix it in the transcript: the segment context menu's "Edit text..." (`TranscriptTab.swift:849-887`) writes a correction record with the original and edited text (`TranscriptCorrectionStore`), and that knowledge is then discarded. FEAT11's own vocabulary editor cannot benefit from the corrections the product already captures.

FEAT11 skipped this leg for named reasons (backlog row, 2026-07-28): honoring "keep it a pre-fill, not an auto-write" needs an uncommitted-row concept in the store plus a word-diff over the edit, real complexity for a `may` leg. The owner's non-technical-use framing (2026-07-29) changes the value side of that trade, not the constraints: it stays a pre-fill, and the diff stays deliberately dumb.

## Scope

- A pure word-diff helper: given (original, edited) segment text, produce at most one candidate pair when the edit is a single-token or short-span replacement (case-insensitive compare, punctuation-tolerant), and bail (no candidate) on anything larger: multi-word rewrites, insertions, deletions, reordering. Bailing is a feature; a wrong vocabulary pair silently corrupts future transcripts.
- The affordance: after a transcript text edit saves and the diff yields a candidate, offer "Add 'X' to Vocabulary as 'Y'..." in the edit flow's confirmation moment (and/or a standing "Add to Vocabulary..." item in the segment context menu that opens pre-filled from that segment's correction). Clicking opens the pre-filled pair with the scope defaulted to the meeting's workflow (fall back to global when the meeting has none); the user confirms; only then does `GlossaryStore` append. Nothing is ever written without the explicit confirm (FEAT11's honesty rule, restated as this task's hard constraint).
- The pre-fill lands through the same `GlossaryStore` append path the editor uses (no second writer), and the editor shows the new row on next open.
- Copy stays in the UX44 register (no "ASR").

## Explicitly not in scope

Auto-writing pairs from corrections, ever (rejected in FEAT11 and re-rejected here; recorded so pickup does not soften it). Mining historical corrections in batch to seed the vocabulary (a real idea, noted as an adjacency for the owner to commission separately; it has different consent and review needs). Fuzzy-match suggestions. Changing correction storage or `mp.glossary` semantics.

## Acceptance

Pure diff tests: single-token replacement yields the pair (with original casing preserved on the canonical side); a cased variant matches case-insensitively; punctuation-adjacent tokens tolerated; two-token span replacement yields the pair only when contiguous; insertions, deletions, and multi-span edits yield no candidate (each pinned).

Flow tests: the affordance appears only when a candidate exists; confirming appends exactly one row to the right scope via the shared store path; cancelling writes nothing (store contents pinned unchanged).

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green, 23 new tests. Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball: fix a garbled product name in any transcript line; the offer names the exact pair; confirm; Preferences, Pipeline, Vocabulary shows it under the meeting's workflow; Re-transcribe that meeting and the garble is gone (the FEAT11 acceptance loop, now reachable in three clicks).

## Shipped 2026-08-03

Everything above the owner eyeball is done. `swift build` clean, `swift test` 2052 passing against a 2029 baseline measured on this branch, so the delta is +23; the figure this spec was filed with was two months stale, which is why the baseline was measured rather than quoted.

**What landed.** `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/VocabularyCandidate.swift` is the pure half: `VocabularyCandidate.derive(original:edited:)` names at most one pair, and `VocabularyOffer.make` wraps it with the scope default. `TranscriptTab.saveCorrection` builds the offer after a line edit persists, the edit sheet's `onDismiss` hands it to a new `VocabularyOfferSheet`, and only that sheet's **Add** calls `GlossaryStore.addTerm(heard:canonical:workflow:)`, a new entry point that is the Preferences editor's own scope-then-mutate steps collapsed into one call.

**How the diff decides.** Tokens are compared exactly; edge tokens of the changed run that differ only in case are then trimmed off it. That two-step is what keeps a re-capitalized neighbour ("the" to "The") from widening a one-word fix into a two-word pair, while still letting a pure capitalization fix stand when it is the whole edit. It refuses: unequal token counts (every insertion and deletion), a run longer than two tokens, a change split across two places, a same-words reorder, and a pair that trims to the same string on both sides (a punctuation-only tweak).

**Both hard constraints held, and are pinned rather than asserted.** `VocabularyCandidateTests` (23 cases) covers every acceptance clause; `test_making_an_offer_writes_nothing` is the cancel case and pins the glossary file byte-for-byte, which states the pre-fill rule as a fact about the code rather than about the UI wiring. `test_confirming_preserves_the_knobs_the_editor_does_not_model` pins that `[fuzzy]` survives an add, which is the payoff for routing through `GlossaryStore` instead of writing a second time.

**Two decisions the spec left open.**

1. The affordance is the post-save sheet **only**, not the "and/or" standing context-menu item. The confirm moment is where both sides of the pair are known, so it is the leg that earns its complexity; the menu variant would need each row to know whether its segment carries a correction, which is plumbing the row does not have today. If the owner wants a second way in after living with this, it is a small follow-up rather than a rework.
2. A pure capitalization fix counts as a pair. Keys are folded at match time and values are not, so "kubernetes" to "Kubernetes" is a substitution that actually does something to every future transcript, and refusing it would have been the surprising behaviour.

**One race, named rather than fixed.** The sheet's confirm builds its own `GlossaryStore` so the document it merges into is read at confirm time. A Preferences window sitting open on the Vocabulary group mid-keystroke has a 500 ms debounce pending that would then write its own document over this one, costing the term (not the file). Closing that properly means shared ownership of the store, which is a larger change than this leg is worth; it is commented at the call site.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Every task gated on an owner action carries one (2026-07-30 rule). Walk the owner through it step by step; the owner does not read code. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] Install the build so the Library has the new sheet: `./scripts/rebuild.sh` from the repo root.
2. [owner] Open the Library, pick any meeting whose transcript contains a mangled product or person name, and open its **Transcript** tab. If nothing obvious is there, any single word will do: the check is about the mechanism, not about the word being genuinely wrong.
3. [owner] Hover the line and click the pencil (or right-click and pick **Edit text…**). Change exactly **one** word, leaving the rest of the line alone, and press **Save**.
4. [owner] A second sheet should appear, titled **Add to Vocabulary**, with the old spelling on the left and the new one on the right. Read both boxes: they must name the exact pair you just changed and nothing else. If a whole phrase shows up instead of the one word, stop and say so, because that is the diff being less dumb than it is supposed to be.
5. [owner] Check the **Applies to** row. It should already read this meeting's workflow name. A meeting with no workflow shows the line "Applies to every meeting." instead, with no picker, which is also correct.
6. [owner] Press **Cancel** the first time, on purpose. Nothing should have been written.
7. [session] Confirm that: `grep -c . ~/.config/meeting-pipe/glossary.toml` before and after should match, or the file should still not exist if there were no terms. This is the honesty rule, checked once by hand.
8. [owner] Repeat steps 3 and 4, and this time press **Add**.
9. [owner] Open **Preferences ▸ Pipeline ▸ Vocabulary** and set **Applies to** to that meeting's workflow. The new pair should be listed there. Switching **Applies to** back to **Every meeting** should not show it, since it was scoped to the workflow.
10. [owner] Back in the Library, run **Re-transcribe…** from that meeting's `...` menu. It costs no engine call and keeps the existing summary. When it finishes, the garbled word should be spelled correctly in the transcript, without your line edit being what fixed it.
11. [session] If steps 4, 9, and 10 all hold, FEAT12 moves to done and its spec archives into `q6-final.md`. If step 4 named the wrong pair, that is a `VocabularyCandidate.derive` bug and the failing line pair belongs in a test before anything is changed.

# [DONE] FEAT13: Clarify a misheard word where you find it, not in Preferences

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31 at the owner's request, immediately after FEAT11's vocabulary walkthrough made the friction concrete: "I want to have an easy mechanism to 'clarify' things on the flight, not with 'Settings -> Pipeline'. I think it would be nice to select words with mouse, see automatically menu 'Clarify' or something, then enter the clarification, and save it with options to re-transcribe or whatever." Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

FEAT11 shipped the vocabulary editor at Preferences ▸ Pipeline ▸ Vocabulary, and it works: on 2026-07-31 the owner added `sitting environment` to `staging environment`, ran Re-transcribe on `20260723-103118`, and the garble was gone. The friction is where the surface lives. A misheard word is discovered while reading a transcript, and fixing it means leaving the transcript, opening Preferences, finding the pane, retyping a phrase from memory, closing Preferences, and returning to run Re-transcribe.

**This was anticipated and deliberately parked.** FEAT11's spec records it as not built: "the optional *add to vocabulary* pre-fill off PIPE9. Reason in the ToC row. If it is ever picked up, the constraint that decides its shape is the spec's own 'keep it a pre-fill, not an auto-write', which the current store cannot express (every write is live)." This task is that pickup, and the constraint is the most valuable thing carried forward.

**The same session produced the argument for that constraint.** The meeting also contained the word "Venusaur", which the ASR invented and which neither the owner nor the session could decode ("Venusaur I cannot understand myself what was speaking about"). Under an auto-write, selecting it and clarifying would have written a permanent global rule rewriting every future transcript on a guess. Under a pre-fill, the owner saw it and walked away, which is what actually happened. A Clarify affordance that writes on confirm is the whole feature; one that writes on selection is a corpus hazard.

The seam already exists on both sides. The transcript is already editable in place: `TranscriptTab` says "Click a line to edit or seek", and `TranscriptCorrectionStore` (PIPE9) persists a per-segment text overlay to `<stem>.transcript_corrections.json`. The vocabulary side is `GlossaryStore` over `glossary.toml` (FEAT11), whose resolution is mirrored by `mp.glossary` and pinned by a CI4 fixture.

## The design question this task exists to answer

**A per-meeting text fix and a global vocabulary rule are different things with different blast radii, and Clarify touches both.** Correcting one line changes one meeting and is trivially reversible. Adding a glossary term changes every transcript finalized from then on, including meetings not yet recorded. Collapsing them behind one button is the failure mode to avoid.

The affordance should therefore offer both, visibly distinguished, in the register of "fix it here" versus "always fix this". Which of the two is the default, and whether "always" implies "here" as well, is the call to make at pickup and to record. A reasonable starting position, to be challenged rather than assumed: fixing here is the safe default because it is per-meeting and reversible, and promoting to a rule is the deliberate extra step.

The re-transcribe offer the owner asked for ("save it with options to re-transcribe or whatever") belongs on the rule path only. A per-meeting text correction is already applied by the overlay and needs no re-run; a new glossary term only reaches existing transcripts through Re-transcribe, and that is exactly the confusion FEAT11's walkthrough had to warn against ("not Reprocess and not Re-summarize: both re-run over the transcript already on disk").

## Scope

A selection-driven Clarify affordance in the transcript that pre-fills a small editor with the selected text as the "as heard" side, takes the intended text, and offers the two destinations above. On the rule path, offer Re-transcribe for the current meeting once the term is saved.

Nothing is written until the user confirms. The FEAT11 note that "the current store cannot express" a pre-fill is the real work here: `GlossaryStore`'s writes are live, so a staged, uncommitted entry either needs the store to grow that concept or needs the editor to hold the pair until confirm and write once. Prefer the latter if it keeps the store simpler, since a store with a draft state is a store two surfaces can disagree about.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Not an auto-write on selection**, and not a "learn from my corrections" inference. FEAT11 already parked corpus mining ("auto-suggested glossary terms from the corrections corpus") and the Venusaur case above is the argument against inferring rules from garbles.

**Not a replacement for the Preferences editor.** That surface stays: it is where the whole table is reviewed, edited and pruned, which a per-selection affordance cannot do.

**Not fuzzy matching or per-workflow scoping changes.** `[fuzzy]` and the per-workflow term tables are FEAT11's and are unchanged; a term added here goes global unless the editor offers the existing scope choice, which it may.

**Not speaker naming.** The cast strip's chips are their own affordance (UX40) and are not folded in.

## Acceptance

Selecting text in a transcript row offers Clarify. Choosing it opens an editor pre-filled with the selection, and **nothing is persisted until confirm**: a test pins that opening and dismissing the editor leaves both `glossary.toml` and `<stem>.transcript_corrections.json` byte-identical.

The two destinations are distinguishable in the UI and in the tests: confirming the per-meeting fix writes only the correction overlay; confirming the rule writes only the glossary term (or both, if that is the recorded decision), and the rule path offers Re-transcribe while the per-meeting path does not.

A term added through Clarify resolves identically to one typed in Preferences, so the CI4 `glossary-golden.json` fixture and `mp.glossary` still agree; regenerate the fixture if the writer changes (`cd pipeline && uv run python ../scripts/gen_contract_fixtures.py`).

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green. `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green. No em-dashes in changed lines.

## Shipped 2026-08-04

Everything above the owner walkthrough is done. `cd daemon && swift build` clean, `swift test` green with 22 new tests (`ClarifyTests`), `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green, no em-dash in any changed line. The CI4 `glossary-golden.json` fixture was **not** regenerated and did not need to be: the glossary writer is untouched, this task's rule path calls FEAT12's existing `GlossaryStore.addTerm`, and `CI4ContractFixtureTests` passes as it stood.

**What landed.** `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Clarify.swift` is the pure half: `Clarify.Destination` (the two blast radii plus their copy), `Clarify.Plan` (one case per destination), `Clarify.plan(…)`, and `Clarify.substitute`. `ClarifySheet.swift` renders it. `TranscriptTab`'s row context menu gained **Clarify a word…** directly under **Edit text…**, and the host gained a `clarifyTarget` sheet plus `applyClarify`, which routes each plan to exactly one writer.

### The entry point is not the one the spec asked for, because that one cannot fire

The spec's shape was "select words with the mouse, get a Clarify option". **Measured first, per the pickup instruction, and it is not available on this stack.** An on-screen `NSWindow` probe hosting `Text(…).textSelection(.enabled)` (extending UX48's offscreen one) reports that SwiftUI's `SelectionTextField`:

- answers `acceptsFirstResponder` **false**, and `makeFirstResponder(field)` leaves the **window** as first responder;
- engages **no field editor** (`window.fieldEditor(false, for:)` is nil);
- returns **nil** from `validRequestor(forSendType: .string, returnType: nil)`, before and after a `selectAll`.

That closes UX48's own hedge from the other side. Its escape route was that a selectable `NSTextField` conventionally engages the window's field editor, which *is* an `NSTextView` with the standard text menu, so a right-click after selecting might find what a right-click before selecting does not. No field editor is ever engaged, so there is nothing to find, and there is no `NSServicesMenuRequestor` to hand the selection over either. SwiftUI owns the selection privately in a `PlatformViewRepresentableAdaptor<SelectionOverlay>` and exposes no accessor on the macOS 14 floor.

**One workaround was considered and rejected rather than shipped.** Since UX48 installed a main menu whose Copy has a nil target, `NSApp.sendAction(#selector(NSText.copy(_:)), to: nil, from: nil)` plausibly *would* put the live selection on the general pasteboard, and the sheet could read it, verify it occurs in this line, and restore the pasteboard afterwards. It was turned down: it puts the owner's clipboard at risk (a restore cannot faithfully rebuild lazily-provided or custom types) to save typing one word, it is untestable, and it depends on private behaviour that an OS update can change silently. If the owner wants it after living with the shipped shape, it is a small follow-up with a stated cost, not a thing to have guessed at now.

So the affordance is the transcript row's own `.contextMenu`, which is proven to open over transcript text (it is where **Edit text…** and **Assign to…** already live). Walkthrough steps 2 and 3 below are rewritten to match; the durable measurement is recorded in `daemon/CLAUDE.md` so no later session re-derives it.

### The three calls the spec left open

1. **The per-meeting fix is the default.** The spec's own starting position, adopted rather than overturned: it is the reversible, one-meeting option, and promoting to a rule should cost a deliberate second click.
2. **"Always" does not imply "here".** The rule path writes the term and **only** the term. Writing the overlay alongside was rejected for a reason worth keeping: an overlay laid over a term makes a rule that never matched look like it worked, so the owner would have no way to tell a live term from a dead one. It also keeps each choice one-to-one with one write, which is the honesty the whole task is about, and keeps FEAT12's shipped sheet copy true rather than contradicted.
3. **Re-transcribe is a tick box inside the sheet, on the rule path only, defaulting off.** The owner asked to "save it with options to re-transcribe", and pre-registering the choice beats a second modal after the fact. Its presence is itself the visible discriminator between the two paths. Off by default because a rebuild spends minutes of the Mac's time, and a sheet that starts a job nobody asked for is the same class of surprise as a rule written without a confirm. There is no second confirmation once it is ticked: the tick was the ask, and re-asking is the friction this task exists to remove.

### Two smaller decisions

`Clarify.substitute` deliberately mirrors `mp.glossary`'s `\b(<key>)\b` case-insensitive, every-occurrence substitution (`glossary.py:70`), **including its limitation** that a term ending in punctuation ("c++") anchors nowhere and matches nothing. `test_wording_ending_in_punctuation_matches_nothing_here_or_in_the_pipeline` pins that on purpose: making the line path cleverer than the rule path would mean "Fix this line only" fixing a line that "Always fix this" could never fix, which is exactly the confusion between the two blast radii the task exists to prevent. The line path also refuses a substitution that would not change the line, so Clarify cannot write a no-op overlay entry that later shows up in a re-transcribe's carry report as work to preserve.

`LibraryDialogs.reportRetranscribe` is the re-transcribe result dialog, promoted out of `MeetingDetailView+Header`'s private scope because this task gave it a second caller. A carry that dropped an override has to read the same wherever the rebuild was started from, and a private copy per caller is how the Trash confirm came to be worded two different ways for the same action.

**One thing deliberately not done:** no new event action. A Clarify-driven write emits the same `transcript_correction` / `vocabulary_term_added` events the other surfaces do, because it is literally the same write through the same store; a Clarify-specific action would have been a second name for one thing.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Per the 2026-07-30 standing rule. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Open a transcript and **right-click** a line with a misheard word in it. Pass: **Clarify a word…** is there, directly under **Edit text…**. (It is a right-click and not a mouse selection, and that is not a shortcut taken: the app cannot see what you selected. The measurement is above.)
3. [owner] Open it and read what it offers. Pass: the line you right-clicked is shown at the top so you can read the wrong words straight off it, and it is obvious which choice changes only this meeting and which changes every future transcript. **Judge that wording as writing**: it is the only thing standing between a one-line fix and a permanent rule.
4. [owner] Dismiss it without confirming, then check Preferences ▸ Pipeline ▸ Vocabulary. Pass: nothing was added. This is the step that matters most, and the reason it exists is Venusaur: a garble you cannot decode must be walk-away-able.
5. [owner] Now do it for real on a word you are sure about, choosing the per-meeting fix. Pass: that line reads correctly and no vocabulary entry appeared.
6. [owner] Do it again, this time choosing **Always fix this**, and tick **Re-transcribe this meeting afterwards** before pressing the button (it starts off, on purpose). Pass: the term is in Preferences ▸ Pipeline ▸ Vocabulary, the rebuild runs on its own without asking a second time, and the meeting comes back corrected. If a text edit of yours could not be re-anchored the report says how many were dropped, which is expected behaviour rather than a fault.
7. [owner] Say "FEAT13 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] UX55: "Quit (do not relaunch)" is still offered when nothing can relaunch

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31, owner-reported at the end of UX42's walkthrough: "I guess I just need to see one 'quit' instead of 'quit dont relaunch, no? cause when this flag is off, relaunch is not working for classic quit." Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

The status-bar menu offers two quit rows, and the second is conditional (`StatusBarController.swift:596-610`):

```swift
menu.addItem(NSMenuItem(title: "Quit MeetingPipe", ...))
// TECH-UX7: when auto-restart is on (the default), offer a one-off quit
// that does not relaunch. Hidden when the user already disabled
// auto-restart, since the plain Quit above already means quit.
if !UISettings.shared.disableAutoRestart, let coordinator = coordinator {
```

The comment states the right rule: the extra row exists only when plain Quit would be undone by a relaunch, and is hidden otherwise. The condition implements it against one input, `UISettings.shared.disableAutoRestart`, which is a preference the user sets.

**UX42 added a second way for relaunch to be off, and this condition did not learn about it.** That task established the login agent as the single owner of both login-start and relaunch-after-quit, and its own closing note says so: "with launch at login OFF, **Quit MeetingPipe** really quits, because the relaunch-after-quit behaviour is the same launch agent and it is not running the app." So when launch at login is off, plain Quit already means quit, exactly the condition the comment says should hide the extra row, and the row is shown anyway because `disableAutoRestart` is still false. The owner reached that conclusion from the menu alone, which is the clearest possible evidence that the row is confusing rather than merely redundant.

Not a UX42 regression in behaviour: quitting works correctly either way, and the second row is harmless if used. It is a truthfulness defect of the same family UX42 itself was about, a control that describes a distinction the machine no longer makes.

## Scope

Make the row's condition ask whether a relaunch can actually happen, rather than only whether the user disabled the preference. That is the conjunction of `disableAutoRestart` being false **and** the launch agent being enabled, and `LaunchAtLoginService` (UX42) is already the one reader of the latter.

Keep the decision where it can be tested. `StatusBarModel` is the pure presentation type for this menu and its own comment at `:262` already describes this rule, so the predicate belongs there with the agent state as an input, not as a second live read inside the controller's menu-building code.

The menu is rebuilt on state changes already (the `PermissionsSnapshot` dedupe exists precisely because it rebuilds often), so the row should appear and disappear as the toggle moves without needing a restart. Confirm that rather than assume it.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Not the quit behaviour**, and not TECH-UX7's crash-relaunch safety net, which UX42 verified still works (a `kill -9` brings the icon back within ten seconds). Only the row's visibility changes.

**Not the wording of either row.** "Quit MeetingPipe" and "Quit (do not relaunch)" both read fine when each is genuinely applicable.

**Not the Preferences copy.** The Startup pane's explanatory text was rewritten by UX42 and is correct.

## Acceptance

`StatusBarModelTests` pin the predicate: auto-restart on and agent enabled shows both rows; auto-restart disabled shows one; **agent disabled shows one even with auto-restart on** (the case this task adds); both off shows one.

The row appears and disappears in a running app as Launch at login is toggled, without a relaunch.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green. No em-dashes in changed lines.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Per the 2026-07-30 standing rule. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts. Short, and it needs no logouts, unlike the task that found it.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] With Launch at login **on**, open the status-bar menu. Pass: both quit rows are there, which is correct because a plain Quit really would be undone by a relaunch.
3. [owner] Turn Launch at login **off** (Preferences ▸ General ▸ Startup), then open the status-bar menu again. Pass: only **one** Quit row. This is the whole task.
4. [owner] Turn it back **on** and check the menu once more. Pass: both rows are back, without needing to restart the app.
5. [owner] Say "UX55 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] UX49: The done notification says "Open in Notion" whichever sink actually ran

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31, owner-reported during the owner-owed pass: "notification wording. It keep saying 'Open in Notion' while the notion was not an option and there's no new meetings in here since 28th." Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

The meeting-done notification names Notion unconditionally. Both strings are literals:

- `Notifier.swift:120-121`: `content.body = canCorrect ? "Open in Notion. How did this summary look?" : "Open in Notion"`
- `Notifier.swift:331`: `UNNotificationAction(identifier: Self.actionOpen, title: "Open in Notion", ...)`

Neither consults what was published. **The action itself is correct**, which is why this is wording and not a broken feature: it opens `entry.pageURL` (`Notifier.swift:426`), which is taken from the publish result, so for a filesystem publish it opens the real `file:///Users/.../Documents/Meetings/published/<stem>.summary.md` and lands where it should. The user is simply told the wrong thing on the way there, on every meeting.

The owner's library shows how routine that is. Sinks per publish, from `<stem>.publish.json` on 2026-07-31:

| Meeting | Sink that ran |
|---|---|
| 20260731-163028, -121524, -103033 | `filesystem` |
| 20260730-163434, -175154, -163033 | `filesystem` |
| 20260729-160040, -155902, -103147 | `filesystem` |
| 20260728-133356 | `notion` |
| 20260727-140126, -103155 | `filesystem` |
| 20260724-163048, 20260723-163108 | `notion` |

Nine consecutive filesystem publishes, each announced as Notion. The sink follows the workflow (`Personal` publishes to the filesystem, `General` to Notion), so this is not rare or edge-case: it is the common path for this user.

**The second half of the owner's report is not a bug and should not be chased.** Nothing has appeared in Notion since 2026-07-28 because 20260728-133356 was the last meeting to classify as `General`; every meeting since has been `Personal`. Workflow counts per day over the preceding fortnight show the mix has always varied (all `Personal` on 16, 17, 20, 21 July; `General` on 23, 24, 28 July; `Client work` on 22 and 27 July), so there is no step change and no publish failure. Every recent `publish.json` reads `state: "full"`. If the owner wants work meetings in Notion, that is a workflow-matcher question, not this task.

## Scope

Derive the sink's name from what actually ran, at both string sites, and pick the verb from the same source.

The data is already there and already used elsewhere: `PublishResult.load` reads `<stem>.publish.json`, whose `sinks` map names each sink that ran with its `ok` and `page_url`. `MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:443-449` already branches on this exact distinction to choose between "Open in Notion" and "Open in Obsidian" help text, so the naming rule exists and should be promoted rather than copied. That promotion is the point: this is the same class of defect as UX31's seven independent backend-name switch tables, and a second literal spelling of a sink's name is how the notification and the header come to disagree.

The multi-sink case needs a decision rather than a guess, and it should be made once in the pure rule: when two sinks succeed there is one `pageURL` and two plausible names. A neutral phrasing ("Open summary") is the obvious answer and avoids naming one sink over another.

The `Notifier.swift:105` doc comment describing the legacy fallback ("Open in Notion only, or plain 'Local Markdown ready' under regulated mode") needs updating with the behaviour, since it documents the bug as intended. Note that the "Local Markdown ready" variant is keyed on regulated mode rather than on the sink, which is why a plain filesystem publish outside regulated mode never reaches it; that keying is part of what this task corrects.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Not the workflow routing.** Why recent meetings classify as `Personal` rather than `General`, and whether that is what the owner wants, is a matcher question. Measured above and deliberately left alone.

**Not the notification's action behaviour.** `pageURL` already resolves correctly and the Open action already works. Do not "fix" the action while renaming it.

**Not new sinks or a sink picker.** The set of publishers is unchanged.

**Not the correction ("Looks good") flow.** `canCorrect` and the correction action are untouched; only the sink-naming half of the body string changes.

## Acceptance

A pure rule (name it beside the existing header logic, not inside `Notifier`) maps a publish result to the phrase the user reads, and its tests pin: filesystem-only publish names the local note and not Notion; Notion-only names Notion; both succeeding produces the neutral phrasing; no sink succeeding produces no Open affordance at all rather than an action that cannot open anything. `NotificationRouter`'s existing coverage stays green.

`MeetingDetailView+Header.swift` reads the same rule rather than keeping its own copy, so a grep for `"Open in Notion"` returns one site instead of three.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green. `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green. No em-dashes in changed lines.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Per the 2026-07-30 standing rule: every task gated on an owner action carries one. Walk the owner through it step by step; the owner does not read code. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Let a normal meeting finish, or re-summarize any `Personal` meeting to trigger the notification. Pass: the notification no longer mentions Notion, and names the local note instead. This is the whole bug, so if it still says Notion nothing else matters.
3. [owner] Click the notification's Open action. Pass: the summary opens, exactly as it did before. This step exists because the action already worked and must not have been broken by renaming it.
4. [owner] If you have a meeting that publishes to Notion (a `General` one), let one finish or re-summarize it. Pass: that notification does say Notion, and its Open action reaches the Notion page.
5. [owner] Say "UX49 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] PIPE13: Ctrl-C on any `mp` command dumps a traceback instead of exiting

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31, observed during AI11's owner walkthrough. Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

AI11's owner walkthrough, step 5, instructs the owner to interrupt an index rebuild: "let the indexing lines climb past a few hundred, then Ctrl-C". Doing so on 2026-07-31 produced this:

```
^CTraceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../bin/mp", line 10, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File ".../src/mp/__main__.py", line 164, in main
    return run(rest)
  File ".../src/mp/ask.py", line 297, in main
    index = embed_index.load_or_build(
  File ".../src/mp/embed_index.py", line 777, in load_or_build
    return refresh_index(
  File ".../src/mp/embed_index.py", line 733, in refresh_index
    blocks.append(embedder.embed([c.text for c in batch_chunks], kind="passage"))
  File ".../src/mp/embed_index.py", line 260, in embed
    mx.eval(emb)  # mlx is lazy; force the compute before leaving mlx-land
KeyboardInterrupt
```

The interrupt worked correctly in every way that matters: the checkpoint survived and the next run resumed from stem 112 rather than 0, which is precisely what AI11 built. Only the exit reads as a failure.

This is not specific to `mp ask`. `grep -rn "KeyboardInterrupt" pipeline/src/` returns nothing, so no subcommand handles it, and every command long enough to be worth interrupting (`ask`, `run-all`, `prefetch-model`, `digest`, `train-adapter`) ends the same way. A documented, supported, deliberately-resumable action should not be indistinguishable from a crash, and the walkthrough that tells the owner to press Ctrl-C is the reason this is worth the small change.

## Scope

Catch `KeyboardInterrupt` once in `__main__.main`, print a single line to stderr naming what was interrupted, and return 130 (the shell convention for SIGINT, `128 + 2`). Every subcommand is dispatched through that one function as `main(argv) -> int`, so one handler covers all of them and no subcommand needs to learn about it.

For `ask` specifically the message is worth one clause about what survived, since the resume is the non-obvious part and the owner has just been told the run was long: something of the shape "interrupted; the index keeps what it finished, so the next run resumes from there".

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**The handler must not clean up.** AI11's resume works because the interrupt leaves the last checkpoint on disk; a `finally` that deleted a partial index, or a "tidy up before exiting" impulse, would break the exact behaviour the owner verified on 2026-07-31 (interrupted at 112 stems, resumed at 112). Exit and leave the disk alone.

**130 must not collide with an exit code the daemon reads.** `publish_router.EXIT_PUBLISH_FAILED` is 3 and six Swift sites branch on the publish contract; 130 is outside that vocabulary, and this task must not renumber anything that exists. Check `PipelineLauncher`'s exit-code handling treats an unknown non-zero as a generic failure rather than misreporting it.

**Not a graceful-shutdown mechanism.** No signal handlers, no cooperative cancellation, no flushing work in progress. The point is the exit line, not new behaviour on the way out.

**Not the daemon's cancel path.** UX28's in-app Cancel is a different mechanism (`pipeline_cancelled`, the job queue) and is unaffected.

## Acceptance

`test_main_cli.py` (or the existing entry-point test module) pins that a subcommand raising `KeyboardInterrupt` returns 130 from `main`, writes its one line to stderr, and prints no traceback. A second test pins that the handler is at the dispatch level by raising from a different subcommand, so the coverage cannot be read as ask-specific.

An interrupted `mp ask --rebuild` still resumes: the existing embed-index resume test stays green, and nothing in the new path touches the index directory.

`cd pipeline && uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests`, `pyright`, and `pytest -q` green. No em-dashes in changed lines.

Owner-visible check, folded into whatever walkthrough next runs an interrupt: Ctrl-C during an index rebuild prints one line, no traceback, and the next run resumes where it stopped.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts. The engineering shipped 2026-08-04 (see the ToC row); this section exists only because the acceptance's last line is an owner-visible check, and the status stays `owner-owed` until it is run. It is the same leg as **AI11's step 5**, which is also still open, so run them together rather than twice: AI11 asks whether the resume works, this asks whether the exit reads like a crash while it does.

What the session already verified, so it does not need re-doing: a real SIGINT to a real `mp` process exits 130 with exactly `mp <cmd>: interrupted` on stderr and no traceback, proved red against the pre-fix shape. What it could **not** verify is that same behaviour when the interrupt lands inside an MLX index build over the real library, which is the only reason this is still open.

1. [owner] `cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run mp ask "budget" --rebuild`. Let the indexing lines climb past a few hundred, then Ctrl-C.
2. [owner] Read what it printed. Expect exactly one line, `mp ask: interrupted; the index keeps what it finished, so the next run resumes from there`, and **no** `Traceback (most recent call last)` block above it. A traceback here means the interrupt unwound past the handler, which is the whole defect.
3. [owner] Run the same command **without** `--rebuild` and read the first `indexing` line: `stems_done` should start near where the Ctrl-C landed, not at 0. This is AI11's step 5 unchanged; it is repeated here because the one risk this change carries is having disturbed it.
4. [session] On a clean pass, archive PIPE13 per the done-done move. On a traceback in step 2, capture the whole block: it names the frame the exception escaped through, and that frame is the fix.

# [DONE] LANG2: One stray Cyrillic character disables the whole summary-language target

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31, off a miss the owner caught while running UX41's walkthrough: "summary in UA even tho meeting in english, I thought we fixed that". They were right on both counts, which is what makes this worth a task rather than a bug comment. Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

Meeting `20260730-163434` ("Kintava 5.12 Release, HIPAA CloudFront & Kintava 6 Update", 2026-07-30 16:34, header language EN) was re-summarized on 2026-07-31 at 13:43:41Z by `anthropic` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` as part of UX41's owner pass. The summary came back in Ukrainian: its first bullet reads "Heorhii завершив CloudFront setup для GMS (для відповідності HIPAA) та Sentry review rep...", and the stored `summary.json` carries **1,178 Cyrillic characters**.

The transcript it was generated from is English. Measured over `20260730-163434.json`: 22,213 characters of segment text, **25 Cyrillic letters against 17,222 Latin**, so Cyrillic is **0.14% of all letters**. Every one of those 25 is in a single throwaway opening line before the meeting starts ("Суть в том, что мне треба солнце"), and the remaining 30 minutes are English.

The cause is one line. `expected_summary_language(summary_language, transcript)` ends its Latin-dominant branch with:

```python
# Latin-dominant. LANG1: only a *pure* Latin transcript (zero Cyrillic) is a
# firm "en" target. Any Cyrillic mixed in means the meeting may legitimately
# carry another script, so leave it unverified rather than force English.
return "en" if cyr == 0 else None
```

`summary_language.py:106-109`. With `cyr == 25` the function returns `None`, which is the "cannot cheaply verify" answer, and `None` switches off everything LANG1 built: `language_reinforcement` is not added to the prompt, `divergent_sections` is not consulted, and the post-hoc repair never runs. The model was free to answer in any language and nothing was watching. Detection never failed; it was never asked.

**LANG1 (done 2026-07-10, archived in [q6-final.md](./q6-final.md)) is not regressed and this is not a reopen.** Its verifier, its per-section detection including `actions[].task`, and its backend-agnostic repair all work as built. The zero-Cyrillic gate is a deliberate conservatism recorded in its own comment, and its purpose is right: a genuinely code-switched meeting must not be force-flattened into one language. The defect is that the gate is absolute where the thing it is protecting against is proportional, so 0.14% noise is treated identically to a half-Ukrainian meeting.

## Scope

Replace the `cyr == 0` test in `expected_summary_language` with a share-based one, and give the Cyrillic-dominant branch the same treatment so the fix is symmetric rather than an English special case.

The threshold is the whole decision and it should be picked deliberately, not guessed: it needs to leave a meeting like this one (0.14%) verified as `en`, and leave a real code-switched meeting unverified. The corpus can inform it rather than intuition, since 244 recordings exist on disk and their transcripts can be scored for script share in one pass; a short script that prints the distribution of Cyrillic share across the library is cheap and would show whether the population is bimodal (mostly-pure meetings and genuinely mixed ones, with a gap to put the threshold in) or continuous. Record the chosen number and its justification in the function's comment, replacing the one quoted above.

`language_signature` carries the same `cyr >= lat` coarse split for its own purposes and should be reviewed in the same pass for consistency, but it answers a different question (what language is this text) and does not need the same threshold unless the review says so.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Not a change to `summary_language`'s config vocabulary.** `auto` and forced ISO codes stay as they are; `_VERIFIABLE_LANGS` is unchanged. Forcing `en` in config would work around this meeting and is not the fix, since the owner's library is genuinely multilingual and `auto` is the right default for it.

**Not a language-detection library.** The coarse script read is deliberate and sufficient; adding a dependency for this is out of proportion to the problem and the repo's dependency floor forbids it without asking.

**Not a re-summarize of the affected meeting as part of the fix.** That is a one-line owner action once the threshold lands, and it is in the walkthrough below rather than in the code.

**Not the `en` label's meaning.** `"en"` continues to mean "Latin script" rather than English specifically, and callers must keep not asking it to separate Latin languages (the existing docstring is explicit and stays).

## Acceptance

`test_summary_language.py` gains the regression case built from this meeting's real numbers: a transcript of ~17,200 Latin letters carrying 25 Cyrillic ones returns `"en"`, not `None`. A genuinely mixed transcript (a share above the chosen threshold) still returns `None`, and the existing zero-Cyrillic and Cyrillic-dominant cases keep their current answers, so the change is a widening of the verified set and not a re-specification.

The Cyrillic-dominant branch has the mirrored case: a Ukrainian transcript carrying a few Latin words still returns `"uk"`.

The chosen threshold appears once, as a named module constant beside `_LANG_MIN_LETTERS`, with the comment stating what it protects and what the corpus showed.

`cd pipeline && uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests`, `pyright`, and `pytest -q` green. No em-dashes in changed lines.

## As built (2026-08-04)

`expected_summary_language`'s `cyr == 0` test is replaced by one symmetric constant beside `_LANG_MIN_LETTERS`:

```python
_LANG_MAX_MINORITY_SHARE = 0.33
```

Both branches now reject before they read the script: a transcript whose minority script is more than a third of its letters returns `None`, and only then does the Cyrillic-dominant branch do its uk-vs-ru read. Read plainly: a transcript is a firm target only when at least two thirds of its letters are one script, whichever script leads.

### How the number was chosen, and the mistake worth recording

The corpus was scored, per the Scope section's suggestion. The first pass measured the raw segment text of 208 transcripts and landed on **20%**, which looked well supported: the Cyrillic-dominant meetings topped out at 10.8% Latin and the one genuinely bilingual meeting sat at 46.8%, so 20% had margins of 1.8x and 2.3x.

**That measured the wrong text.** `summarize` hands the function `transcript`, which is the *rendered markdown* (speaker labels, header, timestamps), not the segment text. Re-scored on the markdown across all 232 transcripts on disk, the picture moves:

| Group | Count | Minority-script share (markdown) |
|---|---|---|
| Single script exactly | 205 | 0% |
| Cyrillic-dominant | 19 | 0.9% to **23.1%** |
| Latin-dominant, not bilingual | 7 | 0.1% to 1.4%, plus one at 8.0% |
| Genuinely bilingual | 1 | **45.2%** |

At 20% one real Ukrainian meeting (`20260730-163033`) would have lost its verified `uk` target, which is exactly the damage the walkthrough's step 3 exists to catch, reached from the other side. The window is therefore **(23.1%, 45.2%)**, and 0.33 sits 1.43x above the ceiling and 1.37x below the bilingual meeting, about as centred as the data allows.

The two sides differ in kind, not only in degree, which is why one number covers both. In a Ukrainian meeting the Latin minority is borrowed technical vocabulary interleaved word by word (Jenkins, Docker, tenant, API), longest contiguous Latin run 14 words. In an English meeting the Cyrillic minority is somebody actually speaking Ukrainian for a stretch, contiguous runs of 35 to 94 words. The one bilingual meeting is 1,637 Cyrillic words in a single 281-word run and half the transcript.

### Verified against the whole library

Old answer against new, over all 232 transcripts: **7 meetings change, every one of them `None -> en`, and none loses a target.** A pure widening, as the Acceptance section asked for. The seven sit at 0.10%, 0.14% (the subject meeting), 0.59%, 0.75%, 0.81%, 1.37%, and 7.97%. On `20260730-163434` specifically the target is now `en`, and all five sections of the summary it shipped flag as divergent, so LANG1's repair fires on the exact meeting that produced the report.

### `language_signature`: reviewed, deliberately unchanged

It keeps the plain majority split. It answers a different question over much shorter text, and its callers are the per-section checks in `divergent_sections`. The owner's real Ukrainian summaries carry **20% to 37% Latin per section**, with one title at 49%, because that is where the product names live. Gating it on the same share would return `None` for most of them, and a section the detector will not read is a section `divergent_sections` will not flag, which is LANG1's whole mechanism switched off. Fail-safe is the wrong instinct here: a missed flag costs a summary in the wrong language, a wrong flag costs one model call that is discarded unless it comes back clean.

### One finding this task does not fix

The 23.1% ceiling that pins the threshold is **not linguistic**. That meeting's speech is 5.7% Latin; the rest is the markdown wrapper, whose `# Transcript - <stem>` header and one `**Name**:` label per turn are Latin whatever the meeting was spoken in. It is a fixed cost per turn, so it lands hardest on the shortest meetings (that one is ~3 minutes, and 174 of its 218 Latin letters are labels) while the longest Cyrillic meeting barely moves (0.4% to 0.9%). Two consequences, both recorded in the constant's comment: erring low is the safer error, since a threshold set too low costs a short meeting its safety net and leaves it where it was before LANG1, while one set too high forces a genuinely bilingual meeting into a single language, which is an actively wrong answer rather than an absent one; and a still shorter Cyrillic meeting could clear 33% on labels alone, whose fix is to stop counting the wrapper rather than to keep raising this constant. Worth its own task if it ever bites.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Per the 2026-07-30 standing rule: every task gated on an owner action carries one. Walk the owner through it step by step; the owner does not read code. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] Land the threshold, then re-summarize `20260730-163434` (Library, the 2026-07-30 16:34 meeting, Re-summarize with Anthropic).
2. [owner] Read the summary. Pass: it is in English. This is the meeting that produced the report, so it is the one that has to change.
3. [owner] Open two or three meetings that were genuinely conducted in Ukrainian or Russian and read their summaries. Pass: they are still in their own language. This step matters more than step 2: the easy way to "fix" this task is to force English everywhere, and that would quietly ruin every non-English meeting you have. If you want the ones with the most English mixed in, since those are where a bad threshold would show first, they are the 2026-06-18 11:31 and 2026-07-14 16:20 meetings, plus the short 2026-07-30 16:30 one.
4. [owner] The corpus scan found exactly two meetings that really do switch languages, and they now get opposite answers. Read both and say whether that is right. **2026-05-21 16:30** (`20260521-163051`) is mostly English with one Ukrainian stretch of about 66 words, and now gets an English target, so its summary will be steered to English. **2026-06-11 11:32** (`20260611-113210`) is about half and half, and is deliberately left alone, so its summary comes out in whatever language the model picks. There is no automatic right answer for either, and your call is the only way to know whether the threshold sits in the right place. If the first one should have stayed Ukrainian, the constant comes down; if the second should be pinned to one language, it goes up.
5. [owner] Say "LANG2 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] UX53: Sweep every operation for whether the open view learns it happened

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31 at the owner's explicit request, so it would not be lost: "this is not the first issue, I need full assessment all over the app for this", said on discovering that a finished re-transcribe leaves the transcript on screen unchanged. Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

UX52 records one instance: `MeetingLibraryService.retranscribeMeeting` completes, logs `retranscribe_done`, and bumps nothing, so the open detail view keeps rendering the previous transcript until the user switches tabs. The owner's point is that the instance is not the problem. A missing refresh is a defect class, and finding the rest by waiting for the owner to trip over them is the slow way.

**The reason this class hides is structural and worth stating up front, because it shapes the sweep.** The Library's centre column is an `if/else` on `scope`, so switching tabs or rails destroys the projection view and rebuilds it from disk. That means *any* operation that fails to publish a change still looks correct the moment the user navigates anywhere, and navigating is the natural thing to do while waiting. A user learns the workaround without noticing they learned it, so these bugs are under-reported rather than rare. The same property is documented in `daemon/CLAUDE.md` as the reason run state must not live in that view (UX37's Ask incident), which is the same structural fact biting from the other side.

There is also a known-good side to copy from: several operations do refresh correctly today (rename, enroll, reassign, regenerate), so the right idiom exists in this codebase and the sweep is looking for paths that skipped it, not for a mechanism to invent.

## Scope

Enumerate every operation that mutates a meeting's on-disk state, and for each determine whether an open detail view (and the row in the list) reflects the change without navigation. This is `/audit`-shaped work: parallel passes over the surfaces, adversarial verification of anything claimed broken, then filing.

The list to start from, to be completed rather than treated as exhaustive: re-transcribe (known stale, UX52), regenerate / re-summarize, republish, speaker rename, speaker un-name, enroll to roster, workflow reassign, transcript line correction (PIPE9), action item resolved / reopened, evidence-bearing summary rewrite, trash / delete, retention sweep and reaper deletions, glossary change, and anything writing a sidecar the detail view reads.

For each, record the observed behaviour rather than the intended one, and separate three outcomes: refreshes correctly, does not refresh, or refreshes only partially (the transcript updates but the cast strip does not, and similar). Partial refresh is the most likely shape here, because a re-transcribe changes the text, the speaker clusters, and the header lines, and a fix that publishes one of those is easy to mistake for a fix.

Fix the trivial ones in place where the working idiom applies directly; file anything with a real design question rather than growing this task without limit.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Not UX52.** That instance has its own task and its own owner walkthrough; this sweep must not absorb it, and if UX52 lands first this sweep verifies it rather than redoing it.

**Not a rearchitecture of the Library's view lifecycle.** The `if/else` on `scope` is deliberate and load-bearing; this task adds refresh signals where they are missing, it does not change how views are torn down.

**Not non-meeting surfaces** (Preferences, Diagnostics, the status-bar menu) unless a pass finds the same class there, in which case name it rather than fixing it here.

**Not performance.** Whether a refresh is efficient is a separate question from whether it happens.

## Acceptance

A table in this spec listing every enumerated operation against its observed refresh behaviour, with the three outcomes distinguished and the partial ones saying which part went stale. No operation is left as "probably fine": an unchecked row is an unfinished sweep, and saying so is the point of writing the table down.

Every stale operation is either fixed in the same pass or filed with its own row, and the filings are listed here so the sweep's coverage can be read after it closes.

Where fixes land: `cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green, and each fix pins its notification at the service level rather than asserting on rendering, matching UX52's acceptance.

No em-dashes in changed lines.

## The sweep (2026-08-04)

### How the refresh actually works, which is what the table is scored against

A surface refreshes only when **both** halves hold, and the two failed independently, which is why "publishes nothing" and "does not refresh" are different rows below.

1. **A rescan happens.** `MeetingStore.revision` bumps on every rescan (`MeetingStore.swift:257`). A rescan comes from one of two places: the vnode watcher on the recordings dir (`MeetingStore.swift:286`), or the single explicit `refreshLibrary()` UX52 added (`MeetingLibraryService.swift:363` / `:389`, wired at `Coordinator.swift:766`). The watcher is on the **directory** fd, so it fires on any change to the directory's *contents*: a create, a delete, or a rename. An atomic write is a temp file plus a rename, so it counts; a plain in-place rewrite of an existing file does not. Both trees write atomically almost everywhere (`storage.atomic_write_text` on the Python side, `options: .atomic` on the Swift side), so in practice every operation below reaches a bump. The two exceptions found are `publish_notion.py:109` and `publish_obsidian.py:147`, which rewrite their sidecars in place; those runs still bump, because the same publish writes `<stem>.publish.json` through a temp file and `replace` (`publish_router.py:274`).
2. **The surface keys its reload on `revision`.** This is the half that failed in UX52 and the half that fails again below. `TranscriptTab` was getting the bump all along and ignoring it, because its reload key was `meeting.stem`. That is the diagnostic signature: a `.task(id: meeting.stem)` (or an `.onAppear`) over a disk read.

Which is why the surfaces matter more than the operations. Every pane in the detail view, scored once:

| Surface | Reads off disk | Reload key | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Header (`MeetingDetailView+Header.swift`) | the two publish sidecars only; everything else is fields on `Meeting`, which the scan rebuilds | `.task(id: PublishURLsReloadKey(stem:revision:))` | fixed here; was `meeting.stem` |
| `SummaryTab` | `<stem>.summary.json` | `.task(id: SummaryReloadKey(stem:revision:))`, mtime guard | keyed |
| `TranscriptTab` | `<stem>.json` + overlay + corrections + markers | `.task(id: TranscriptReloadKey(stem:revision:))`, four-sidecar fingerprint | keyed (UX52) |
| `AudioTab` | waveform peaks + the audio file | `.task(id: meeting.stem)` | **deliberately** stem-only; re-attaching the player on a rescan would drop the play head |
| `CorrectionsTab` (a sheet) | the correction record | `.task(id: meeting.stem)` | stem-only; no operation was found that changes that record behind the open sheet, and its own Revert clears its state itself |
| List rows (`MeetingRow`) | nothing; a pure renderer over `Meeting` (`MeetingRow.swift:456`) | n/a | follows the scan |
| Facts / People / Meeting time rails | summaries / roster / transcripts | `.onChange(of: store.revision)` | keyed |

### The table

Every operation that mutates a meeting's on-disk state, scored on observed behaviour with an open detail view and no navigation. "Partial" always names which part went stale.

| # | Operation | What it writes | Observed | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Re-transcribe (ASR3) | `<stem>.json`, `.md`, both overlay sidecars, `.embeddings.json` | refreshes | UX52. Verified here rather than redone: text, cast strip and voice resolution all come out of one `TranscriptTab.reload`, the header reads `Meeting`, and the Summary tab is untouched by design because the run does not summarize. UX52's "complete" claim holds **for this operation**; the header gap in row 3 is a different operation reaching the same header. |
| 2 | Regenerate / Re-summarize (PIPE6, PIPE11) | `.summary.json`, `.summary.md`, `.run.json`, then the publish leg | refreshes | Was partial before row 3's fix, on the publish leg only. |
| 3 | Republish (incl. the retry-from-summary path) | `.publish.json`, `.notion.json`, `.obsidian.json`, `.run.json` | **was partial, fixed here** | The stale part was the header's Notion / Obsidian Open buttons. `reloadPublishURLs` was keyed on `meeting.stem`, the exact UX52 signature one file over. The publish-state line beside them *did* refresh (it reads `Meeting`), so a first successful publish left the header saying it had published while offering nothing to open, and a republish to a new page left the old page one click away. |
| 4 | Retry a failed meeting | clears `<stem>.error.json`, then run-all or republish | refreshes | The clear is a delete, so the row leaves the failed set before the run finishes. |
| 5 | Merge fragments (FEAT9) | primary rewritten, fragments trashed | refreshes | |
| 6 | Generate a candidate summary (TECH-A16) | `.summary.candidate.json` / `.md` | refreshes | The compare pane loads the candidate from the call's own completion (`SummaryTab.swift:206`). |
| 7 | Keep the candidate | promotes over `.summary.json` | refreshes | Explicit `await reloadSummary()` at the call site (`SummaryTab.swift:323`). |
| 8 | Discard the candidate | deletes the candidate files | refreshes | |
| 9 | Publish from paste | `.summary.json` + a publish | refreshes | Explicit `await reloadSummary()` (`SummaryTab.swift:406`); its Open buttons ride row 3's fix. |
| 10 | Name / rename / un-name a speaker, enroll to the roster | `.speaker_labels.json`, roster | refreshes | Self-reload at the call site; the store bump is then a no-op because the fingerprint already matches. |
| 11 | Per-line reassign, reset to the original label | `.speaker_labels.json` | refreshes | Same shape. |
| 12 | Transcript line correction (PIPE9, FEAT12, FEAT13's line path) | `.transcript_corrections.json` | refreshes | Row patched in memory, and the file is in `TranscriptLoader.fingerprint`. Three entry points now share the one writer, so all three inherit this: the edit sheet, and FEAT13's "Fix this line only" through the same `saveCorrection`. |
| 13 | Add to Vocabulary (FEAT12, FEAT13's rule path) | `glossary.toml`, outside the watched dir | refreshes (nothing in the Library renders it) | An open Preferences ▸ Vocabulary editor does **not** re-read it (`@StateObject GlossaryStore` reads once in `init`, no watcher), and its 500 ms debounce can write its stale document back over the new term. Non-meeting surface, already documented at `TranscriptTab.swift`'s `addVocabularyTerm`; named, not fixed. **Re-scored after FEAT13 landed:** the defect is unchanged but its reachability is not. FEAT12 could only reach `glossary.toml` from the offer that follows a line edit, so hitting it needed the owner to have just edited a line; FEAT13 puts "Always fix this" directly on every transcript row's context menu. Same bug, materially easier to meet, which is why it graduated to a recommended filing below. |
| 14 | Roster rename everywhere (UX40) | `roster.json` outside the dir, plus `.speaker_labels.json` per matching meeting | **partial** | The carry bumps `revision`, so every meeting-shaped surface follows, and all three call sites reload themselves. What goes stale is a *different open window*: a rename that matched no meeting writes only `roster.json`, publishes nothing at all, and the Library's People rail keeps the old name if the rename was done from Preferences. Narrow; a cross-window signal for the roster is its own design question, so it is named rather than fixed. |
| 15 | Workflow reassign (WF8, AI9) | `.meta.json` | refreshes | Chip, scope membership and the NDA line are all fields on `Meeting`. |

| 17 | Action item resolved / reopened, Summary tab (UX26) | `.summary.json` | refreshes | Optimistic, with a re-read when the write did not land. |
| 18 | Resolve a commitment, Facts rail (AI7) | `.summary.json` per meeting | refreshes | |
| 19 | Summary edit saved, Summary tab editor | `.summary.json` + a correction record | refreshes | |
| 20 | Summary edit saved, standalone grading window (`CorrectionWindow`) | same files | **does not refresh** | It loads `.run.json` and `.summary.json` once in `show()` (`CorrectionWindow.swift:19`) and never re-reads. A regenerate landing while it is open leaves it editing the previous prose, and its save then writes that back over the new summary. That is a lost update, not only a stale view, so the fix is a design question rather than a reload key. Filed as a recommendation, not fixed here. |
| 21 | Revert a correction (`CorrectionsTab`) | rewrites `.summary.json`, deletes the record | refreshes | |
| 22 | Trash a meeting, single or batch | every file for the stem | refreshes | The detail pane empties when the row leaves the array. There is no in-app restore; recovery is Finder's. |
| 23 | Export a meeting | writes outside the library | nothing to refresh | |

The **Audio tab does not**: its waveform and player stay on an audio file that is gone or recompressed, because its load is keyed on the stem alone on purpose (UX52's own comment: a rescan must not drop the play head under a listener). Fixing it means separating the waveform reload from the player attach, which is a real change to playback, so it is named rather than fixed. |
