# [DONE] MIC8: Teams `LogMuteAdapter` (native mute signal)

Band origin: carried from Q4; base spec in q4-final.md, progress notes here. Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**MIC8 (P2, partial): build the Teams `LogMuteAdapter`.** Filed as "spike UI-independent native mute signals (logs / SDK / OS)"; base spec in [`q4-final.md`](./q4-final.md) (search the id), promoted P3 to P2 and amended 2026-07-12 (see the Assessment review section). The spike question is **answered**, so the remaining work is a build, not a measurement.

**Spike resolved 2026-07-23: GO for Teams.** Full write-up in [`docs/spikes/mic8-native-mute-signals.md`](../spikes/mic8-native-mute-signals.md); the measurement is reproducible via [`docs/spikes/mic8_log_correlation.py`](../spikes/mic8_log_correlation.py) with aggregates committed at [`mic8-log-correlation-results.json`](../spikes/mic8-log-correlation-results.json).

Two of the three candidate classes stay closed from documentation, unchanged: **(B) vendor SDK** is a non-starter for the "watch the client the user is already in" model (Zoom staff confirm the desktop client exposes no external interaction; the Meeting SDK's `onUserAudioStatusChange` reports mute only inside an app that joins through the SDK itself; Teams exposes no local read API), and **(C) OS-level** is a category error (CoreAudio device mute is the hardware input, while a client's in-call mute is a transmit gate that by design keeps the OS mic live).

**(A) the client's own local log is now measured, and it wins.** Rather than the filed plan of a live instrumented call with 3-4 toggles, it was answered offline against 11 days of real dogfood, which is a strictly stronger read. Teams' SlimCore media stack writes `AirPodsService: Input mute event received: mute|unmute` (plus a `SetMuteState ... cause_id` and an `InputMuteStateChangeNotification` line) on every in-call toggle: 594 transitions across 9 log generations spanning 2026-06-12 to 07-23, identical format throughout, default-on with no troubleshooting toggle involved. Paired against the incumbent AX label scrape from the daemon's own `micgate` events: 61 pairs within 30 s, 59 state agreements, and the log **leads** the AX read on 59 of 61 (p50 50 ms, min 22 ms). Of the four imperfect pairs, three are AX-side defects (a notification that fired 16.8 s after the toggle the log caught in 391 ms; a transition to `unmuted` AX announced when the state had been unmuted for 68 s; a 1.8 s poll lag) and one is an unexplained log gap. It is not candidate C in disguise: across the same window `system_mute_state` was `false` in 34 of 34 observations while the log tracked 60 client-side transitions.

**Why the a-priori lean was wrong, and what the recon missed.** The spike leaned toward a close on the argument that an undocumented log format is no more futureproof than the label scrape it replaces. That argument was made about an unmeasured signal and the measurement beat it: the same vendor broke the AX scrape twice in this project's lifetime (the Teams mini-window incident, MIC9/MIC10) and did not break this line once in 9 generations. The 2026-07-13 recon concluded Teams was not logging because it read `MSTeams_*.log`, the Electron/WebView2 **shell** log; the call media stack writes a different family in the same directory, and its generation `.10` already held 218 mute transitions a month before the spike was written. Two probe defects would have confirmed that false close, and both are fixed and verified in [`daemon/scripts/mic8-native-mute-probe.sh`](../../daemon/scripts/mic8-native-mute-probe.sh): a flat newest-6-files cut that evicts the only family carrying mute lines (the shell log rotates hourly, SlimCore weekly; observed live, one rotation pushed SlimCore from 5th to 10th newest), and a bare `mute` token that matches the hourly ECS config blob's `hfpOsUnmuteFixEnabled` feature-flag key, which truncated to 200 chars reads exactly like a hit. Note also that the comparison MIC8 was filed against is gone: MIC6's AX state-attribute read was refuted by the 2026-07-14 live dump (Teams exposes no `AXValue` and no `AXIdentifier`) and closed, so the incumbent this beats is the localized `MuteLabels.toml` scrape plus MIC10's `AXSystemDialog` anchor, which the log path also beats on locale-independence by construction.

**Remainder (the build).** A `LogMuteAdapter` conforming to `MicGateAdapter` (alongside `NativeMuteAdapter` / `NoOpMuteAdapter`) that tails the newest `MSTeamsNM_SlimCore_*.log`, parses the transition line, and hands an `AXMuteButtonProbe.Event` to the sink, landing in `MicGate.injectAxMuteEvent` exactly where the AX poll does today. No `PromotionEngine` / scorer change; the mute layer is already an injectable seam. **Owner decision needed before building: supersede the Teams AX read, or fuse with it.** The spike assumed supersede; the measurement supports fuse ("log wins when present, AX carries when absent"), which covers the one case that went against the log, costs one comparison, and does not bet the whole Teams mute oracle on a single undocumented string. Build gotchas, all measured: SlimCore prints **UTC** but suffixes the local offset, so parse the naive reading as UTC or every event is wrong by the offset (and correct-looking on a UTC machine); resolve the file by log family, never by mtime; an absent line degrades to **unknown**, never to unmuted (the `AirPodsService` component name is a misnomer, but this data cannot rule out a dependency on AirPods being connected for output); rotation is per Teams restart, so re-resolve the newest generation rather than holding a file handle. Re-running `mic8_log_correlation.py` after a Teams update is the regression test for the bet.

Zoom stays unmeasured: its logs are empty/stale and its verbose logging is opt-in, and the corpus has recorded zero Zoom calls, so it is effectively moot. The live probe remains the instrument if a Zoom meeting ever happens.

## Owner walkthrough (historical; steps 1-3 and 5 done 2026-08-04, step 4 judged unnecessary)

Added 2026-07-30 at the owner's request: every task gated on an owner action carries one. Walk the owner through it step by step; the owner does not read code. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. The spike is answered (GO); the gate is one owner decision: supersede the Teams AX read with the SlimCore log, or fuse them (log wins when present, AX carries when absent). The measurement favours fuse: of 61 paired transitions the log led 59, and the one unexplained log gap is exactly the case fusion covers. Recommendation: fuse.
2. [owner] Say which. That one word un-gates the build.
3. [session] Build the `LogMuteAdapter` with the measured gotchas: tail the newest `MSTeamsNM_SlimCore_*.log` resolved by log family (never mtime; the shell log rotates hourly and evicts it from any newest-N cut), parse timestamps as UTC (SlimCore prints UTC with a local-offset suffix), an absent line degrades to unknown never unmuted, re-resolve the generation on Teams restart. Feed `MicGate.injectAxMuteEvent`; no fusion changes.
4. [owner] After the build, one normal Teams call with a few mute toggles is the live verification; nothing special to do beyond having it.
5. [session] Re-run `docs/spikes/mic8_log_correlation.py` against the fresh logs to confirm agreement, and re-run it after any Teams update: that script is the standing regression test for this bet.

## Shipped 2026-08-04 (fuse)

The owner answered the gate with **fuse**, and the build followed the measurement rather than the spike's a-priori lean. Three new files in the Core island, no `PromotionEngine` or scorer change, as the remainder predicted:

- `MicGate/SlimCoreMuteLog.swift` - the pure half. The line parse (anchored on the whole message, so the shell log's hourly `hfpOsUnmuteFixEnabled` blob cannot read as a hit), the generation resolver (**by log family**, never by mtime), and the byte-range tail. Everything is a function of its arguments or of the directory it is handed, so the whole read path is testable against fixture lines and a temp directory with no Teams and no meeting.
- `MicGate/Adapters/LogMuteAdapter.swift` - the host. A 1 Hz tick that re-resolves the newest generation (rotation is per Teams restart, so no file handle is held), reads the appended bytes on its own queue and hops only the bytes back to main, carries a partial trailing line across ticks (SlimCore flushes mid-line routinely), and hands `MicGate` an `AXMuteButtonProbe.Event` only when the state actually moves. A fresh watch joins the live generation at its **end**, so a meeting never replays a week of past toggles.
- `MicGate/MuteSourceFusion.swift` - the precedence, pure and clock-injected: the log wins outright, the AX read is honoured whenever the log has been quiet for 5 s.

**The one decision the spec did not settle.** "Present" had to be made operational, and the two readings are not equivalent. Presence as *the log file exists* collapses fusion back into supersede: it would blind the gate for the first half of every call, because the log is a transition stream that says nothing at all until the first toggle while the AX read knows at join time whether you are already muted, and it would not cover `07-20T13:44:26`, the single gap fusion exists for. Presence as *the log spoke recently* covers both. The horizon is 5 s: over 5x the measured p90 lead (~900 ms), so it costs the log nothing in the normal case, while bounding to five seconds the window in which a genuine log miss cannot be corrected by the AX read. That direction is the one to protect, since a latched wrong `.muted` is what MIC9 and MIC10 were both about; the AX defects a longer horizon would have swallowed all reported the state that was already true, so declining to swallow them changes nothing.

**The seam change fusing required.** `MicGate.start` now starts **one adapter per source** instead of the first match overall. For every pre-MIC8 adapter that is byte-identical behaviour, including the deliberate case: the two browser no-op adapters share one bundle set, and only the first (`.meet`) still starts, so their two distinct `micgate` actions keep telling the no-AX surfaces apart. `injectAxMuteEvent` and `clearAxMute` carry a `MuteReadingSource` defaulting to `.ax`, so `MeetingAXWindowWatcher`'s 1 Hz poll is unchanged at its call site and is fused by the same rule as the adapter sink, which matters because that poll, not the adapter, is the authoritative AX producer. The clear is gated like a reading on purpose: a blind AX read is not evidence about the log, so discarding a fresh log answer on it would throw away the better oracle.

**Verification, and why no live call was owed.** The walkthrough's step 5 ran and passed: `mic8_log_correlation.py` re-measured at pickup shows the format held across 12 further days and 3 further log generations, including the `.21` generation Teams created on 2026-07-31 (381 transitions over 6 generations still on disk, 93 pairs, 90 agreeing, the log leading on 90 of 93, p50 46 ms). Step 4's live call was judged unnecessary, and this is the judgement to challenge if it was wrong: what a live call would have added over the offline read is confidence in the *adapter*, and the adapter was verified against the real logs on this Mac instead. The shipped resolver picks the live generation out of 132 files where it ranks **8th by mtime** (the family gotcha, observed live rather than recalled), the shipped parser finds exactly the **31** transitions `grep` and the Python census independently find in that generation, and the real adapter replaying that file's real bytes line by line emits exactly its edge-collapsed transition sequence with UTC-correct stamps. 2346 daemon tests green with 26 new ones, `swift build` clean, truth fences clean, no Python touched.

**What is genuinely unverified**, stated plainly so the archive is not read later as more than it is: the in-app path on a live Teams call. The wiring is one entry in `Coordinator`'s adapter array plus the per-source start, both unit-tested, and it costs the owner nothing to confirm incidentally, since a working adapter writes `log_mute_event` into `events.jsonl` on the next real call. If that action never appears after a Teams meeting with a mute toggle, this is the row to reopen; `log_mute_source_missing` in the same file would mean the log directory moved.

# [DONE] AI11: Ask engine hardening: incremental index, bounded memory, honest budget

Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 6, off a real incident: Ask "is superslow, it ate ALL available memory and even more, then Mac hang and reboot happened in few min after"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

P1 because the broken promise is "a question about your own meetings must never take the machine down", and it did, with a hard reboot. The owner may re-band. Cross-referenced with LOCAL16 (filed the same day), which owns the shared memory-guard primitive; this task consumes it in the ask path.

## Context

The incident mechanism, traced 2026-07-29 with every link cited:

1. **Any library change invalidates the entire index.** `load_or_build` reuses the cached index only when `library_fingerprint` (every `*.md`, `*.summary.json`, `*.transcript_corrections.json`, `*.speaker_labels.json` by name/mtime/size, `embed_index.py:337-359`) matches exactly (:386). One new meeting, one rename, one correction: full rebuild. There is no incremental refresh (AI2's own recommendation, `docs/spikes/ai2-embedding-rag-latency.md:66`, never done). On 2026-07-29 the cache manifest said `count: 2398` from 2026-07-06 against 418 `.md` / 198 `.summary.json` now on disk, so the next ask was guaranteed the full rebuild.
2. **The rebuild is memory-unbounded.** `chunk_library` reads and holds the whole corpus as strings (`embed_index.py:216-244`); the embed call makes a second copy (`[c.text for c in chunks]`, :278) and `MLXEmbedder.embed` a third (prefixing, :165); batches of 32 accumulate into one `np.vstack` (:167-176). Nothing calls `mx.clear_cache()` or sets an MLX cache limit anywhere in the repo. AI2 hit exactly this on this Mac and survived only via a harness-local free-RAM watchdog ("a first attempt swap-stormed the machine and OOM-killed the model server", ai2 doc :26) that never shipped into `mp ask`.
3. **A kill loses everything, so slowness compounds into a loop.** The index is saved only after a complete build (`embed_index.py:392-396`). The daemon SIGTERMs the subprocess at 10 minutes (`PipelineLauncher.swift:440`, :821-833). A library big enough to exceed 10 minutes rebuilds from zero on every ask, forever, with no progress signal (ask.py never imports `events`; the `__MP_PROGRESS__` heartbeat is run-all-only, `orchestrate.py:60-64`).
4. **The context budget undercounts Cyrillic by ~2x.** `CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4` (`ask.py:37`) sizes the retrieved pack at 16,000 chars for the default 4,000-token budget (:87-92). LOCAL13 measured Ukrainian at 0.47-0.49 tokens/char against EN 0.22-0.25 (`docs/spikes/local13-local-model-refresh-bench.md:120`, :443), so a UK-heavy pack is ~7,800 real tokens. AI2 measured the 14B aborting on the memory watchdog at 8K and OOM-crashing plus swap-storming the machine at 16K (ai2 doc :36-38, :46). On a local backend this alone can reproduce the incident; `--context-tokens` is user-settable with no clamp (`ask.py:148-149`).
5. **Local answering stacks models in one process.** `answer_question` holds the e5 embedder for the index lifetime (`embed_index.py:145-156`) while `engine.complete_text` on a local (or apple_intelligence-substituted, `engine.py:141-149`) backend spawns a multi-GB `mlx_lm.server` child per question and tears it down after (`engine.py:103-117`). A concurrently triggered `mp actions --cluster` (Facts view, `LibraryWindow.swift:857-871`) loads a second independent MLX runtime with no coordination.

The retrieval itself is sound: top-k over the index with a packed, bounded context (`ask.py:87-92`, `rag.pack_context`), exact dense search fine at this scale (`embed_index.py:290-292`). The owner asked "I think we may need some rag or something"; RAG is already there. The failure is the index lifecycle and the absence of memory bounds around it.

## Scope

1. **Incremental index refresh.** Keep the per-file fingerprint but diff it: re-chunk and re-embed only stems whose source files changed, drop vectors for removed stems, reuse the rest. Persist per-stem so the manifest can say which stems are current.
2. **Checkpointed builds.** Save embedded batches as they complete (or per N stems) so a killed build resumes instead of restarting. Acceptance is literally "kill it mid-build, run again, it finishes from where it was".
3. **Memory bounds.** Take LOCAL16's guard primitive: a free-RAM floor sampled between batches that aborts the run with a named, surfaced error before the machine swaps; `mx.clear_cache()` (or the mlx equivalent) between batches so the Metal cache cannot grow unbounded; release the embedder before the local answer model is spawned (retrieval is done by then; holding e5 across the answer serves nothing).
4. **Script-aware budget + clamp.** Derive chars-per-token from the retrieved text's script mix using LOCAL13's measured constants (or count real tokens if the embedder's tokenizer is cheap to reuse), and clamp `--context-tokens` to a per-backend-tier safe ceiling (the AI2 measurements are the table: 4K safe everywhere, 8K only below 14B, 16K nowhere local today).
5. **Observability.** Emit `pipeline` events for index rebuild start/done (chunk and stem counts, duration) and per ask (backend, retrieved stems, packed tokens), and a stdout progress heartbeat the daemon can surface (the UX37/UX38 spinner has something real to show). New event actions ride the existing `pipeline` category (CONVENTIONS event table untouched; fences stay green).
6. **Embedder preflight under the egress guard.** `MLXEmbedder._ensure_loaded` (`embed_index.py:148-156`) calls `load()` bare; under an armed guard with an uncached e5 it dies with a raw huggingface error. Mirror `summarize_local._spawn`'s fail-closed message shape (:721-731) naming `mp prefetch-model`.

## Explicitly not in scope

Changing the embedder model or promoting it to config (adjacency, noted: `DEFAULT_EMBED_MODEL` is hardcoded at `embed_index.py:39`; fine to leave until a reason to swap exists). A vector database (numpy exact search is the right size for a personal library; state this so nobody "upgrades" it). Warm-server reuse for the answer model (LOCAL10/11 territory; spawn-per-question is slow but memory-serial, and changing it changes the memory math this task is bounding). The Ask UI (UX37/UX38). The digest path (verified separate: `digest.py` imports no embed machinery and is deterministic-first).

## Acceptance

Pipeline tests: a two-stem library builds, then one stem's `.md` mtime changes and only that stem's chunks re-embed (fake embedder counts calls per text); a removed stem's vectors disappear; a simulated abort between batches leaves a checkpoint the next build resumes from (embed-call count proves no full restart); `--context-tokens 100000` clamps to the ceiling and says so; a UK-script pack sizes to its measured budget (chars in pack lower than the EN case for the same token target); the guard abort raises the named error and emits its event; the uncached-embedder-under-guard case produces the actionable message, not a huggingface traceback.

`cd pipeline && uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests`, `pyright`, and `pytest -q` green, with the number of tests this task adds recorded in the same commit. Truth fences green (no new config keys or event categories; if a config key IS added for the guard floor, it lands documented in config.example.toml in the same commit).

Owner eyeball: `mp ask` on the real 400+ file library completes with the machine responsive throughout; a second ask reuses the index in seconds; adding one new meeting and asking again does a small delta refresh, not a full rebuild (visible in the new events).

## What shipped (2026-07-31)

All six scope items landed. The index manifest is per stem (`schema_version` 2, `stems: {stem -> fingerprint}`), so `refresh_index` re-embeds only the meetings whose own source files moved, drops a removed stem's rows, and reuses the rest; it writes a complete index back every `CHECKPOINT_EVERY_STEMS` (8) meetings with an empty completeness stamp, so the checkpoint IS the index and a kill resumes from it rather than restarting. LOCAL16's `MemoryWatchdog` is checked between batches (stage `ask index embed`) and `mx.clear_cache()` runs after every MLX batch and on `release()`; `answer_question` releases the embedder before the answer model spawns. The context budget is derived from the retrieved text's Cyrillic share against LOCAL13's two measured rates (4.0 and 2.0 chars/token) instead of a flat 4, and `--context-tokens` is clamped to `resource_guard.tier_for(ram).context_token_ceiling` for `local` / `apple_intelligence` / `auto`. `ask_index_refresh_started` / `_done` / `ask_answered` / `ask_context_clamped` ride the existing `pipeline` category, and the `__MP_PROGRESS__` heartbeat (promoted from `orchestrate` into `events.emit_progress`) carries `stems_done` / `stems_total` for UX38 to render. `MLXEmbedder._ensure_loaded` refuses an uncached model under an armed guard with the `mp prefetch-model` message shape.

No new config keys (the guard floor is LOCAL16's existing `summarization.local_memory_floor_pct`), so the truth fences are untouched. Pipeline suite 1131 -> 1157.

Two decisions the spec left open, recorded: the clamp covers `auto` as well as `local`, because `auto`'s fallback leg is the same local model and losing a little cloud context is cheaper than losing the guarantee; and the heartbeat is emitted per batch rather than from a background timer, and is suppressed under `--json` so a piped payload stays parseable.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts. The owner does not read code; everything below is done from the app or one pasted command. Run them from the shell rather than the app: the app SIGTERMs `mp ask` at ten minutes, and the first build on a 400-meeting library is exactly the case this task exists to make survivable, so it is worth watching it finish once without a cap over it.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] The first real build, and the one that matters: `cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run mp ask "what did we decide about the Q3 budget?"`. The cached index on disk is from 2026-07-06, so this run rebuilds nearly everything. Expect a stream of `__MP_PROGRESS__ {"stage": "indexing", "stems_done": N, "stems_total": ~227, ...}` lines climbing steadily, then an answer with Sources. **The whole point is the middle of that run:** the Mac must stay responsive throughout, with no beachball and no swap storm. If it does not, stop and report it, since that is the incident this task exists to remove.
3. [owner] Ask again, the same command. Expect **no** `indexing` lines at all and an answer in seconds.
4. [owner] The delta refresh. After the next real meeting is recorded and summarized, ask again. Expect the indexing lines to show one meeting embedded against a `stems_total` one higher than before, finishing in seconds rather than minutes. Confirmed from the log: `cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run mp logs --category pipeline --action ask_index_refresh_done --since 1h`. The newest row should read `stems_embedded: 1` against `stems_total: 228` or so. A row saying `stems_embedded` equal to `stems_total` means the incremental path did not engage, which is a bug.
5. [owner] The resume. `cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run mp ask "budget" --rebuild`, let the indexing lines climb past a few hundred, then Ctrl-C. Run the same command **without** `--rebuild` and read the first `indexing` line: `stems_done` should start near where the Ctrl-C landed, not at 0.
6. [owner] The clamp says so. **Read the precondition first, because the obvious command cannot show this on a cloud backend:** the ceiling is a memory guard for the local model, so `clamp_context_tokens` returns `None` for `anthropic` and leaves the request untouched (the ship note above, and `test_a_cloud_answer_is_not_clamped_by_this_macs_ram` pins it). With `summarization.backend = "anthropic"`, `mp ask --context-tokens 100000` therefore answers normally with no warning, which is correct and is **not** the thing to check. Exercise it against an on-device backend without touching the config:
   ```
   cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run python -c "
   import logging; logging.basicConfig(level='WARNING', format='%(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s')
   from mp import ask
   from mp.config import Config
   cfg = Config.model_validate({'summarization': {'backend': 'local'}})
   print('clamped to:', ask.clamp_context_tokens(cfg, 100000))
   print('under the ceiling, untouched:', ask.clamp_context_tokens(cfg, 2000))
   "
   ```
   Expect a warning naming 100000 and the ceiling it used instead (8000 on this 32 GB Mac), `clamped to: 8000`, and `2000` left alone. Judge the warning as writing: it is the line that has to explain a shorter answer than the one asked for. (The first draft of this step said to run `mp ask --context-tokens 100000` and expect a warning; on the owner's `anthropic` config that can never fire, and the absence read as a defect on 2026-07-31.)
7. [owner] Say "AI11 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] AI12: Ask context-size control: let a question buy a wider pack, honestly

Band origin: filed 2026-07-31 at the owner's request, during the AI11 owner walkthrough and immediately after watching a 100K-token pack answer well: "also it may be useful to have a toggle or something picker, that will allow to ask with bigger context window (with all necessary wornings). you seen it works fine when we tried." Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

`mp ask` packs its retrieved context to `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS` (4000) unless `--context-tokens` overrides it (`ask.py`, `answer_question`). The daemon never passes that flag, so in the app the budget is a constant and there is no way to ask a question that deserves a wider read.

The width genuinely changes the answer, and this is measured rather than assumed. Both runs below are the owner's, on 2026-07-31, from `~/Library/Logs/MeetingPipe/pipeline_events.jsonl`:

- default: `ask_answered  context_tokens: 4000  packed_tokens: 3845  packed_chars: 15380  retrieved_stems: 26`
- wide: `ask_answered  context_tokens: 100000  packed_tokens: 99942  packed_chars: 398729  retrieved_stems: 117`

The wide run read 117 meetings against 26 and returned a visibly fuller answer (seven cited meetings against four, and it surfaced budget discussions the narrow run missed entirely). So the value is real and the path already works end to end. **This is not an AI11 re-open.** AI11 built the budget, the script-aware sizing, and the clamp; what is missing is only the dial and the two sentences that make turning it honest.

## The two constraints, which are the whole difficulty

**On a local backend the tier ceiling is a hard cap, not a default.** `clamp_context_tokens` holds the request at `resource_guard.tier_for(ram).context_token_ceiling` for `local` / `apple_intelligence` / `auto` (8000 on a 32 GB Mac, 4000 at 16 GB, 2000 at 8 GB), and that ceiling exists because exceeding it took this Mac down: the 2026-07-29 `mp ask` incident ended in a hard reboot, and AI2 measured the 14B OOM-crashing and swap-storming at 16K. The control must not offer a value above the ceiling on a local backend, and must not present the clamp as something the user can override. A wider pack is a thing cloud can sell and local cannot.

**On a cloud backend there is no memory risk and a real money one.** Nothing clamps cloud (`test_a_cloud_answer_is_not_clamped_by_this_macs_ram` pins that deliberately), so the honest warning here is about spend, not safety, and it should say the multiple rather than a token count: the wide run above sent roughly 26x the input of the default one. "With all necessary warnings" was the owner's own framing and the warning is the deliverable as much as the picker is.

## Scope

A preset control on the Ask surface, next to the input `AskPane` already owns (UX38), plus the launcher argument behind it.

- **Presets, not a token field.** The owner does not read code and "100000 tokens" names nothing. Three positions in plain language, of the shape `SpeakerSeparation` uses for DIAR3 (a pure position table mapping a named position to a value, with a shared clamp), so the same idiom covers this. Suggested values, the implementer's call to refine: a default that is today's 4000, a middle position, and a wide one that only a cloud backend can reach.
- **The pure decision is what to unit-test:** given a backend and a machine's RAM tier, which positions are offered, which is selected, and what the sublabel says. That belongs on its own type next to `resource_guard`'s Swift mirror `LocalModelTier`, not inline in the view.
- **The seam to the engine already exists.** `PipelineLauncher.ask` composes the `mp ask` invocation; it grows one argument. `AskModel` (root-owned, UX37) holds the selection so a rail switch cannot lose it, exactly as it holds the question.
- **A position above the local ceiling is not offered, and says why** rather than being silently rounded down or greyed with no reason (the UX30 rule: a disabled row states its cause). The `LOCAL16` refusal copy is the register to match.
- **The cost line is shown before the ask, not after it.** A warning that arrives with the bill is not a warning.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Do not loosen `clamp_context_tokens`.** It is the guard, and this task consumes it rather than negotiating with it. If a position would exceed the ceiling on local, the position is not offered; the clamp stays the last line of defence and keeps its warning.

**Not a per-question token meter or a spend tracker.** The honest multiple in the sublabel is the scope; counting cumulative spend is a different task nobody has asked for.

**Not retrieval tuning.** `k`, the chunker, and the script-aware rate are AI11's and are not in question here; this task only moves the budget those already respect.

**Not durable Ask history.** Raised by the owner in the same conversation on 2026-07-31 and withdrawn in it ("okay for ux38, no history then for now"). UX38's "Decided at pickup" section already records history as session-only with the durable store one `SavedSearchStore` away if it is ever wanted; leave it there.

**Not a Preferences setting.** The width is a property of the question being asked, not of the app, so it belongs beside the input where the question is written.

## Acceptance

Pipeline: no change is expected in `ask.py`, and `test_ask.py`'s existing clamp coverage must stay green untouched. If the implementation finds it needs a change there, that is a signal to re-read the constraints above before making it.

Swift: `AskContextWidth` tests (new) pin the pure table: on a cloud backend every position is offered; on a local backend positions above the machine's tier ceiling are absent with a stated reason rather than silently clamped; the ceiling used matches `LocalModelTier` for 8, 16 and 32 GB so the Swift and Python tiers cannot drift; the default position is today's 4000 so an owner who never touches the control sees no change. `PipelineLauncher` tests pin that the selected width reaches the `mp ask` argv, and that the default position passes what the CLI would have defaulted to anyway.

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green. `cd pipeline && uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests`, `pyright`, and `pytest -q` green. `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green. No em-dashes in changed lines.

An `ask_answered` event for a widened question records the chosen `context_tokens`, so the log can answer afterwards which width a given answer was bought with (the field already exists; this is a check that the plumbing reaches it, not a new field).

## Decided at pickup (2026-08-04)

The calls this spec left to the implementer, recorded here so the walkthrough below is read against what actually shipped. `ask.py` is untouched, as the spec predicted; the whole task is Swift.

- **The three positions are Normal 4000, Wider 8000, Widest 100000.** The middle is the 32 GB tier ceiling *exactly*, not a round number: it is the widest a local answer on this Mac is allowed to be, so switching to a local backend leaves the owner a real second position rather than a control with nothing in it, and the tier rule is something the walkthrough can see rather than a claim in a comment. The widest is above every tier in the table (16000 at 48 GB is the highest there is), so "only a cloud backend can reach it" holds by construction instead of by a rule somebody has to keep true.
- **The resting position is always offered, including where the tier ceiling is below it.** At 8 GB the ceiling is 2000 and at 16 GB it is 4000, so a strict reading would withhold even Normal and leave an empty control. It stays, because it is the floor of the control and exactly what `mp ask` passes with no flag at all: those machines are clamped today and still are. Only the *wider* positions are withheld, which is what the constraint is actually about.
- **Regulated mode caps a cloud backend too.** Not in the spec, and load-bearing: `config.effective_backend` forces the local path whenever zero-egress holds, so keying on `summarization.backend` alone would have offered the widest position to a machine about to answer locally, then let the clamp round it down where nobody sees it. That is precisely the shape this task exists to remove. Its refusal names regulated mode and offers no escape hatch, since under it every backend is clamped and "switch to a cloud backend" would point at a door that opens onto a wall (`ReSummarizeMenu.offersWorkflowChange`, same rule).
- **A backend id this build cannot resolve is capped.** Python errs the other way (an unknown backend is uncapped there), which is right for its job: it must not refuse to answer. Here the cost of guessing wrong is a wide local pack, so the guess goes the safe way.
- **`--context-tokens` is passed on every run, including at Normal**, where it is exactly `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS`. One code path rather than two, and the `ask_answered` event then records the width *every* answer was bought with rather than only the widened ones. The daemon's own `ask_requested` carries it too.
- **The control is drawn only when there is more than one position to choose.** On a Mac whose ceiling leaves one, the reason line is the whole truth and a one-segment picker would be a control that does nothing (UX43's rule). It is `SettingsSegmented`, the shared primitive, in DIAR3's named-position idiom, rather than a parallel one-off.
- **The selection is re-resolved when the Ask surface appears, not observed live.** `LibraryWindowModel` does not republish on a config change, so changing the backend in Preferences while the Ask rail is open does not repaint it; returning to Ask rebuilds the view (the rail switch that made `AskModel` necessary in the first place) and that is where a width the machine can no longer take falls back to Normal. Step 4 below already tells the owner to return to Ask. `clamp_context_tokens` covers the window in between, which is the one thing it must keep doing.
- **`LocalModelTier.gb` went from private to internal** so the refusal quotes this Mac's memory in exactly the spelling the Preferences preset annotations use. Two formatters for one number is drift a reader would report as a bug.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Per the 2026-07-30 standing rule: every task gated on an owner action carries one. Walk the owner through it step by step; the owner does not read code. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready. Confirm with them first which backend is selected in Preferences ▸ Pipeline, because this control shows different positions on cloud and on local and that is the point of it.
2. [owner] Open the Ask rail with **Anthropic** selected. Pass: a width control sits beside the input, resting on its normal position, and its sublabel says in plain words what the wide positions cost. Judge that sentence as writing: it is the only thing standing between you and a bill you did not expect.
3. [owner] Ask something broad ("what did we decide about hiring this quarter?") on the normal position, then ask it again on the widest. Pass: the wide answer cites visibly more meetings. This is the feature working; on 2026-07-31 the same comparison went from 26 meetings read to 117.
4. [owner] Switch Preferences ▸ Pipeline ▸ Summarization backend to **Local**, then return to Ask. Pass: the widest position is **gone or refused with a reason naming this Mac's memory**, not silently accepted. This is the leg that matters most, because a wide local pack is what rebooted the Mac on 2026-07-29. **Set the backend back to Anthropic afterwards** (the LOCAL16 lesson from 2026-07-31: a walkthrough that changes a setting has to say to change it back).
5. [session] Confirm from the log that the width reached the engine: `cd <repo>/pipeline && uv run mp logs --category pipeline --action ask_answered --since 1h`. The wide run's row should carry the chosen `context_tokens` and a `retrieved_stems` well above the narrow run's.
6. [owner] Say "AI12 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.

# [DONE] DOC11: In-depth user guide: task-oriented recipes

Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner follow-up to the exploratory sweep: "some training or guide how to use in depth. glossary and other things. not something overcomplicated, just simple, yet useful"). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

**Shipped 2026-08-04, owner-owed on the eyeball below.** The rendering option this spec reserved for pickup was decided as **(b), the lightweight in-app viewer**: `GuideWindow` / `GuideView` over the pure `GuideDocument`, built on the `DiagnosticsWindow` shell. `docs/GUIDE.md` stays the single copy of the text and the install scripts drop it into the app bundle, so the guide is never duplicated into Swift. (a) was rejected because raw markdown in TextEdit is the wrong reading experience for this document's persona, and (c) buys nothing (a) does not while adding a build step. What remains is the last two acceptance lines: the review pass against the *running* app (control names were verified against the sources, which is weaker), and the walkthrough.

## Context

The doc set has an install story and a reference, and nothing in between. `docs/SETUP.md` (DOC10) takes a non-programmer from a clean Mac to the first summary and deliberately stops there. `README.md` is the operating guide in the reference sense: what the surfaces are and how the system behaves, written beside the code. Neither answers "how do I get X done with this app", and the cost of that gap is exactly what the 2026-07-29 sweep documented: the owner met the day-old Vocabulary editor (FEAT11) with no idea what it was for, the flag hotkey is opt-in-by-reading-Preferences, and the three re-verbs (Re-transcribe / Re-summarize / Reprocess) are distinct enough that the Vocabulary footer had to spend a paragraph disambiguating them inline.

Scope boundary with the out-of-scope rule, stated so nobody re-litigates it: in-app onboarding wizards and first-run tours are deferred selling machinery, but a person learning to use what they installed is the same class as DOC10's setup-ease carve-out, unblocking the user, in scope. This task ships a document plus one menu item, not onboarding machinery.

Register: the SETUP.md persona (no programming background assumed), the PRODUCT.md voice (quiet, deliberate), and the UX44 jargon rule generalized (no "ASR", no "sidecar", no config-key names in body text).

## Scope

**The guide.** `docs/GUIDE.md`, task-oriented recipes, each one screen or less: the goal in one line, the steps naming the real controls, what to expect. The v1 recipe list:

1. Recording: the detection prompt, recording manually, BYO, off-the-record, and flagging a moment.
2. Workflows: what they are, how a meeting picks one, what NDA mode really does, the context prompt and why it matters (FEAT11's "who is in the room" guidance).
3. Vocabulary: teach the transcriber your team's words, when terms apply, fixing an old meeting (seed from UX44's plain-language framing, recorded there).
4. Voices: name people, fix a wrongly attributed speaker, what the roster is, and the three re-verbs section: when Re-transcribe vs Re-summarize vs Reprocess is the one you want.
5. Finding things: search, Quick Find (Cmd+K), smart folders.
6. Ask: what it can answer, citations, what it cannot do.
7. The weekly rhythm: digests, the Facts and People rails, resolving action items.
8. Keeping it safe: backups, restore (written when STOR5 lands; the v1 guide documents only what ships), retention.
9. Hotkeys: the full list, global chords plus window shortcuts, folding in the cheat-sheet gap the sweep noted (Preferences lists only the four global ones).
10. When something looks wrong: the doctor, the Diagnostics window, when a re-transcribe fixes it.

Recipes link deeper docs instead of duplicating them (README for reference detail, SETUP.md for install); the guide never promises unshipped behavior, so sweep-filed fixes appear in it only as their tasks land.

**The entry point.** A "Guide" item in the status-bar menu beside Diagnostics, since a guide only in the repo fails the same invisibility class the sweep just filed against. Rendering options, decide at pickup and record: (a) open the markdown with the system default app (cheapest, reads as raw markdown for a non-technical user), (b) a lightweight in-app viewer window (the `DiagnosticsWindow` shell precedent; start from the summary reader's inline-markdown parsing with headers as sections), (c) pre-render to HTML at build time and open in the browser (still local, no hosting). Recommendation: (b), the smallest honest in-app reading experience; (a) is an acceptable v1 if (b) turns out heavier than it looks.

**The truth contract.** README's doc map and the repo `CLAUDE.md` orientation table gain a `GUIDE.md` row with the SETUP.md rule extended to it: a change to user-visible behaviour or surfaces updates the guide in the same commit. Without this line the guide drifts into the exact class of stale doc DOC7/DOC9 spent two sweeps cleaning up.

## Explicitly not in scope

Interactive tours, first-run wizards, coach marks, videos, or a hosted docs site (deferred selling machinery; BRAND band). Duplicating SETUP.md or README content. Auto-generating docs from code. Localization (EN only for now; the owner reads EN, and a UK translation is unfiled). Per-surface contextual help buttons throughout the app (the menu entry is the v1 affordance; sprinkle links later only where a task touches a surface anyway).

## Acceptance

`docs/GUIDE.md` exists with the ten recipe areas above, each step naming controls that exist on the current build (verified by a review pass against the running app; a recipe that names a control that does not exist is a filing-quality failure, the DOC9 lesson).

The status-bar Guide item opens it via whichever rendering option was recorded; a menu-model test pins the item's presence (the `StatusBarModel` idiom if the row is conditional, a plain assertion if not).

README's doc map and the repo `CLAUDE.md` orientation table carry the GUIDE.md row with the same-commit maintenance rule, in the same commit as the guide.

Repo dash guard green (the guide is prose; U+2014 is the easy slip). `cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green if Swift was touched.

Owner eyeball: open the Guide from the menu bar and follow the Vocabulary recipe end to end (add a term, Re-transcribe a meeting, see the correction) without touching any other document.

# [DONE] HYG4: Retire the dead CLI surfaces: publish-notion verb, classify-meetings

Band origin: filed 2026-07-29 (owner exploratory sweep, item 16: the invisible-capability inventory turned up two verbs that are neither surfaced nor exempt). Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md). P3: hygiene, promote on demand (the HYG band's normal shape).

**Shipped 2026-08-05.** Two owner decisions preceded the pickup, and both are recorded here because this spec is where they were reserved. The P3 band was **promoted on demand**, which is the shape the band was filed with. And the question the spec left open, whether to keep `classify-meetings` on the de-CLI exempt list for a future experiment, was answered **delete**: module, tests, dispatch arm, usage row, the HYG1 `ai2_spike` precedent exactly. `publish-notion` went the other way, verb only: `publish_notion.py` keeps every line of its code because `publish_router.fanout` builds `NotionRestPublisher` out of it on every real publish, and deleting the module would have broken live publishing.

## Context

The de-CLI standing rule (2026-07-10 delegation notes) says the CLI is a debugging escape hatch, with a named exempt list of owner-dev diagnostics (dogfood, analyze-detection, corrections-stats, train-adapter, spike harnesses). Two registered verbs fail it without being exempt:

- **`publish-notion`**: the legacy single-sink publish, superseded by `publish` + the router fanout; the README (:212) itself calls it "the legacy single-sink escape hatch". Harmless but a dead surface that shows up in `mp --help` beside the real one. Important nuance for the cleanup: the MODULE is live (`publish_notion.py` hosts `NotionRestPublisher`, which `publish_router.fanout` consumes); only the verb registration and its usage-text row are dead.
- **`classify-meetings`**: self-described as the AI5 spike ("AI5 spike", `__main__.py:59-61`). AI5 closed NO-GO on 2026-07 (a derived `meeting_type` field: the labels it measured agreed on 1 of 10 types across 193 real meetings; the backlog's Intelligence band narrative records it as the standing answer). The verb therefore advertises a capability the product explicitly decided against, and it is not on the exempt list. The `classify.py` module, its `_LLM_SYSTEM` prompt, and its tests exist solely for it.

The precedent is HYG1's `ai2_spike` retirement: module + tests + dispatch + docs removed in one commit once the spike's answer was banked elsewhere.

## Scope

- Remove the `publish-notion` verb registration and its usage-text row from `__main__.py`; keep `publish_notion.py` (the publisher implementation) untouched. A stale-verb note in the module docstring pointing at `mp publish` is optional politeness.
- Delete `classify.py`, its tests, its dispatch entry, and its usage row (the HYG1 shape). If anything imports it beyond `__main__` (grep first), that consumer decides: today's evidence says nothing does.
- Update the ARCHITECTURE.md subcommand table in the same commit (the DOC7 rule: that table went 17 modules stale once; do not re-start the drift). README mentions likewise.
- Confirm the de-CLI exempt list needs no edit (neither verb belongs on it; the fix is removal, not exemption). If the owner would rather keep `classify-meetings` for a future experiment, the alternative is adding it to the exempt list with a note; recorded so the pickup asks once instead of guessing.

## Explicitly not in scope

`cleanup-diarization` (a live product capability; DIAR3, filed the same day, gives it UI rather than deleting it). Any change to `publish_router`, the Notion publisher, or the exit-3 contract. Retiring other exempt diagnostics.

## Acceptance

`mp publish-notion` and `mp classify-meetings` report unknown command; `mp publish` still publishes (existing tests); no dangling imports (ruff F401 is CI-fatal, so the suite run is the fence); the ARCHITECTURE subcommand table and README no longer list either verb.

`cd pipeline && uv run --extra dev ruff check src tests`, `pyright`, `pytest -q` green. Truth fences green. Repo dash guard green.

## What shipped (2026-08-05)

- `pipeline/src/mp/__main__.py`: both dispatch arms and both usage rows deleted, which is four command spellings, since each verb carried its dash and snake_case forms. `test_main_dispatch.py` reads the ladder by AST rather than a transcribed list, so it followed the deletion on its own; its guard-the-guard floors (at least 30 spellings, at least 20 modules) still clear at 31 and 22.
- `pipeline/src/mp/classify.py` and `pipeline/tests/test_classify.py` deleted (9 test functions). Nothing imported the module beyond the dispatch arm; the grep the spec asked for came back clean across the daemon, the pipeline, and the scripts.
- `pipeline/src/mp/publish_notion.py`: a docstring note and nothing else, the politeness the spec allowed. It says the verb is retired, points at `mp publish`, and names `NotionRestPublisher` as the live entry point, so the next reader does not mistake `publish()` and `main()` for wired code.
- `pipeline/src/mp/engine.py`: the comment listing the free-form callers that pack their own prompt no longer names classify.
- Docs, same commit. The ARCHITECTURE subcommand table lost both rows; the AI5 NO-GO verdict that lived in the `classify.py` row is kept as a note under the table, since it is the standing answer on a `meeting_type` field and the row was the only place it sat in the orientation docs. The sinks bullet now says `publish_notion.py` has no subcommand of its own, and the `engine.py` bullet drops classify from the Apple Intelligence substitution list. README lost the `publish-notion` block from "Running by hand" and drops classify from the LoRA-adapter and `summarization.backend` passages. `docs/spikes/ai5-meeting-type-classification.md` no longer claims its labeller is kept, and `docs/spikes/ai5_agreement.py` records that the verb producing its input is gone.
- Two prose corrections beyond the spec, both statements this commit falsified: two `test_publish_notion.py` docstrings named `mp publish-notion` as a live verb, and UX64 (spec + ToC row) listed `mp classify-meetings` as one of three commands with no Apple Intelligence path.

**One finding left for a later sweep**, since the spec scoped `publish_notion.py` as untouched: with the verb gone, `publish_notion.publish()` and `publish_notion.main()` are unreachable in production. `publish_router` imports only `NotionRestPublisher` and `apply_meeting_title`, and `publish_from_paste` has routed through `fanout` since PIPE2, so the module's explicit single-sink path now exists only for its own tests. Retiring it means re-pointing a good part of `test_publish_notion.py` at the router, which is a larger change than this task authorized.

Verification: `ruff check src tests` clean, `pyright` 0 errors, `pytest -q` 1184 passed, `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green (it fences config keys and event categories, not subcommands, so it was never going to catch this one, and it was run because the spec asks for it). Acceptance walked by hand on the built CLI: `mp publish-notion`, `mp publish_notion`, `mp classify-meetings`, and `mp classify_meetings` all print `unknown subcommand` and exit 2, while `mp publish` keeps its usage row and its fanout description.

**[DONE] UX60 (P2): Regulated mode is titled "Skip Notion publish" and never says it forces every summary onto the on-device model.** Shipped 2026-08-16.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Proposed high, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic, which narrowed it to one stale README bullet plus one under-described label. Both halves are filed.

## What is wrong

The only in-app control for `modes.regulated_mode` is labelled and explained purely as a Notion switch, while flipping it also pins `effective_backend` to `local` for every meeting.

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Preferences/PreferencesView+Permissions.swift:44` is `SettingsToggleRow("Skip Notion publish",` with an on-state sublabel at `:46` reading "On - Notion publish is disabled for every meeting."
- `:51` is the group footer, the last chance to name the consequence: "Use for client / regulated meetings. The pipeline writes summaries to disk only - no transcript or summary is uploaded to Notion." It does not mention the backend.
- `:48`'s `$store.regulatedMode` is the only write binding for that key in the whole daemon.
- `pipeline/src/mp/config.py:303-304` is `if zero_egress(cfg) and backend != "local": return "local"`, where `zero_egress` at `:282` is `cfg.modes.regulated_mode or cfg.modes.workflow_nda_mode`.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/PipelineLauncher.swift:1013` agrees on the Swift side and strips `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the subprocess.

The per-workflow sibling one pane away gets this right: `WorkflowsView.swift` titles it "NDA mode (force local backend, filesystem only)". The global control describes the same clamp as a Notion switch.

`README.md:609` states the **opposite of the code**: "`regulated_mode` does not by itself force the local backend. Set `summarization.backend = \"local\"` explicitly for the zero-egress contract." Both halves of that bullet are false, and it additionally describes a `mp doctor` warning that was replaced by an `_info` in commit 8591d186 on 2026-05-22 (`pipeline/src/mp/doctor.py:120-124`). `README.md:567` and `:90` assert the same pre-chokepoint behaviour.

## Why it matters

The owner's config has `backend = "anthropic"`. Turning this toggle on for one client call silently repoints **every** meeting to Qwen2.5-7B on-device at lower quality, with no surface saying so. If the 4.3 GB model was never fetched the run refuses outright rather than downloading, and the only thing that catches it is the menu bar's Finish setup row, because `SetupChecklist.swift:166-169` special-cases `regulatedMode`. Anyone who checks the README first is told at `:609` that this does not happen.

## Scope

Retitle the control to what it does, regulated mode or zero egress, not "Skip Notion publish", and make its sublabel and footer state both halves: Notion is skipped, and summarization is forced onto the on-device model whatever Preferences, Pipeline says. Match the honesty of the per-workflow NDA label that already gets this right.

Surface the model-missing case inline in that group rather than only in the menu bar's Finish setup row.

Fix `README.md:609`, `:567` and `:90`, and drop the reference to a doctor warning that is now an `_info`.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests where the copy is pure. The control's title and footer name the backend clamp. A test pins that the Preferences string and `config.effective_backend`'s clamp cannot drift apart, in the shape `SpeakerAccuracy`'s table already uses. The three README bullets are corrected in the same commit.

## Owner walkthrough

Steps tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Open Preferences, Permissions. Read the regulated-mode row without turning it on. Pass: its title and the text under it tell you two things, that Notion publishing is skipped **and** that summaries are produced on-device by the local model instead of Anthropic. If it still only mentions Notion, that is the bug unfixed.
3. [owner] Turn it on. Pass: nothing is hidden from you. If the local model is not downloaded, the group itself says so rather than leaving you to find the Finish setup row.
4. [owner] Turn it back off, and confirm your next summary is back on Anthropic (the Library detail header names the engine).
5. [owner] Say "UX60 good to close" or what is wrong.

**[DONE] UX61 (P2): Batch "Merge…" fires on click with no confirmation, and its ellipsis promises a surface it never opens.** Shipped 2026-08-16.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Proposed high, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic, which established that the merged artifacts are supersets and the fragments are recoverable. The narrowed claim is filed.

## What is wrong

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/BatchActionsPane.swift:174` is `Button("Merge…") { Task { await runMerge() } }`, invoking the action directly from the button.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/BatchActionsPane.swift:537-552` is the whole of `runMerge`: `MeetingMergeEligibility.decide` then `await libraryModel.mergeMeetings(...)`. No alert, no confirmationDialog, no gate.
- The same file has exactly two confirmations, `:44` ("Move N meetings to Trash?") and `:58` ("Re-transcribe N meetings?"), and neither is the merge.
- `design/README.md:97-99` makes the ellipsis meaningful in this repo, and this one opens nothing.

What the click does: `pipeline/src/mp/merge_meetings.py:228-229` overwrites the primary's transcript via `atomic_write_text`, `:230` replaces its audio in place with `os.replace`, and `:236-237` regenerates the summary through a paid engine call and republishes the already-published page. The other N-1 meetings go to the Trash.

`daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingMergeEligibility.swift:53-64` requires only two or more done meetings with audio, one workflow id and one privacy posture. Nothing requires them to be fragments of one call, so **any two finished same-workflow meetings offer Merge**, and the owner's default `Personal` workflow holds 117 meetings.

## What the skeptic established, recorded

The merged audio and transcript are supersets of the primary's own (`merge_meetings.py:180`, `:71-73`), and the fragments go to the recoverable system Trash (`MeetingLibraryService.swift:915`). The only content actually lost is the primary's previous `<stem>.summary.json` with its local edits and action-done ticks.

The "unconfirmed while its less-destructive neighbours confirm" framing was also partly selective: `Re-summarize all` (`:234`) and `Republish all` (`:285`) are unconfirmed too. That makes this a UX-consistency and labelling defect on a never-executed path rather than a data-loss defect, which is why it is medium.

## Scope

Add a confirmation shaped like the two already in the file, naming what is about to be lost: which meeting becomes the primary, that its recording, transcript and summary are replaced **in place** and not moved to the Trash, that the other N-1 meetings go to the Trash, and that the summary is regenerated and republished, which is a paid call and a page rewrite when the workflow's backend is cloud.

Route it through `LibraryDialogs` so the copy has one home, the way the Trash confirm does.

Worth deciding in the same pass, since the skeptic surfaced it: whether `Re-summarize all` and `Republish all` deserve confirmations too. Both spend money and rewrite published pages. The answer may be no, but it should be recorded rather than left as an accident of which action got a gate first.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. The merge cannot run without an explicit confirm. The confirmation copy is a pure function pinned by a test, in the shape `WorkflowDeletion`'s copy already uses. The ellipsis on the button is now honest.

## Owner walkthrough

Steps tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] In the Library, select two finished meetings you do **not** mind touching, and click "Merge…". Pass: a confirmation appears that names which meeting becomes the primary and says its own summary will be replaced and the other sent to the Trash. Cancel it. Pass: nothing changed, both meetings still there.
3. [owner] Say "UX61 good to close" or what is wrong. You do not need to actually complete a merge.

**[DONE] UX62 (P2): The Republish cue and the open-published affordance are blind to the filesystem sink, the default workflow's only sink.** Shipped 2026-08-16.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Proposed high, downgraded to medium by an independent skeptic on the grounds that the capability survives and only the nudge dies.

## What is wrong

`MeetingStore.needsRepublish` decides "this meeting changed since it was published" by looking only for `.notion.json` and `.obsidian.json` sidecars, so a meeting published to the filesystem or LAN sink returns false forever.

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingStore.swift:688` is `return lc.hasSuffix(".notion.json") || lc.hasSuffix(".obsidian.json")`, the entire set of sidecars that count as evidence of a publish.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingStore.swift:690` is `guard !publishURLs.isEmpty else { return false }`, which makes a filesystem-only publish indistinguishable from never published.
- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingRow.swift:279` is the sole consumer of the flag, so the row's inline Republish capsule dies with it.
- `daemon/CLAUDE.md:30` forbids exactly this: "Don't read a per-sink sidecar (`<stem>.notion.json`) to learn whether a run published ... Read `<stem>.publish.json` via `PublishResult.load` (PIPE1)."

The correct signal is already on disk one file away. `20260803-103042.publish.json` carries `"page_url": "file:///Users/.../published/20260803-103042.summary.md"` under `sinks.filesystem`.

Scale, measured on the owner's library 2026-08-03: the default workflow is `Personal` (`is_default = true`, single `type = 'filesystem'` sink), holding 117 of 190 tagged meetings. On disk, **107 of 245 stems** have a `.filesystem.json` and no `.notion.json`, and **13 of the last 15 meetings** are in that blind class. Every NDA meeting is too, since NDA mode force-selects filesystem-only sinks.

`daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:440` and `:446` are the only open-the-published-note affordances, branching on Notion and Obsidian, so a filesystem publish also has no open action despite `page_url` being a `file://` URL `NSWorkspace.open` handles directly.

## What the skeptic established, recorded

This is a missing nudge, not a lost capability. Republish stays unconditionally available in the row context menu (`MeetingRow.swift:462`), the detail `...` menu (`MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:316`) and the batch pane (`BatchActionsPane.swift:269`). So the owner can always republish; they are just never told they should.

## Scope

Compute the last-publish timestamp from `<stem>.publish.json` via `PublishResult.load` instead of globbing per-sink sidecars, so every sink that ran counts, and delete the two-sidecar filter.

In the same file, give the detail header an open affordance for a filesystem or LAN publish off `publish.json`'s `page_url`.

Reuse whatever pure sink-naming helper UX49 lands, since UX49 is fixing the same rule for the done notification and this is that rule applied to the header and the staleness flag. PIPE14 is the same root cause on the state field rather than the timestamp; whichever lands first should leave the helper the other reuses.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. A meeting published only to the filesystem, whose summary is then edited, shows the Republish capsule. The detail header offers an open action for it. A test pins `needsRepublish` over a `publish.json` carrying each sink type.

## Owner walkthrough

Steps tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Open any recent meeting (they are nearly all `Personal`, so nearly all qualify), edit one sentence in the Summary tab, and save. Pass: the row now shows a Republish cue. Before this fix nothing appeared.
3. [owner] In the detail header, look for a way to open the published note. Pass: there is one, and it opens the Markdown file in `~/Documents/Meetings/published`.
4. [owner] Say "UX62 good to close" or what is wrong.

**[DONE] UX64 (P2): The Ask pane never says the local model stood in for Apple Intelligence.** Shipped 2026-08-16.

Band origin: filed 2026-08-03, handed off from PIPE12 by owner decision the day PIPE12 landed. PIPE12 made the truth available end to end and its own spec scoped the render out (deferring it to UX31, which had already shipped without a register for it); the owner's call was to close PIPE12 as done and file the render here rather than grow that commit. Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

`mp ask` and `mp digest` have no Apple Intelligence path. When the configured backend is `apple_intelligence`, `engine.complete_text` silently answers on the local MLX model instead, spawning a multi-GB process per ask and tearing it down after. PIPE12 (landed 2026-08-03, `ce007ad`) made that fact explicit rather than log-only:

- `engine.py:213` stamps `replace(result, substituted_from="apple_intelligence")` on the returned `EngineResult`.
- `engine.py:62` carries `substituted_from: str | None = None`, present-and-null on the normal path so a reader can tell "no substitution" from "older build".
- `ask.py:87` and `:226` thread it into the answer JSON.
- A `pipeline` / `engine_backend_substituted` event fires before the local call, so a failed answer still records it.

The Swift side does not read any of that. `AskAnswer` (`PipelineLauncher.swift:27-41`) decodes `question, answer, citations, sources_considered, backend, model, verified, empty, error` and stops; `substituted_from` is dropped on the floor, harmlessly, because `JSONDecoder` ignores unknown keys. So the pane's provenance footer (`AskView.swift:328-332`, via `AskView.backendFooter` at `:359-361`) renders `"Answered \(SummarizationEngine.resolve(backend)!.runPhrase)"` and says the local model answered, with nothing about *why*.

The user-visible consequence is the one PIPE12's gap 3 was named for: someone picks Apple Intelligence precisely to avoid a resident multi-GB model, and every ask spawns one anyway. The log line PIPE12 added is not a surface for a non-technical owner; the Ask pane is.

## Scope

- **Decode it.** `AskAnswer` gains `substitutedFrom: String?` keyed `substituted_from`. Optional, so an answer file written by an older build still decodes.
- **A register on `SummarizationEngine`, not a string at the render site.** `daemon/CLAUDE.md` names this explicitly ("Don't spell a summarization backend's display name at its render site either"), and UX31 exists because seven independent switch tables had already drifted. The substitution phrase needs *two* engines (the one asked for, the one that ran), so it is a new function on that type rather than a fourth `var`. Shape it so the phrase reads for someone who has never heard of MLX, and so an engine this build cannot name still degrades to nil the way `backendFooter` already does.
- **Render it in the footer.** `backendFooter` grows the substitution case. Keep the existing UX31 discipline: nil rather than a fallback when either engine is unnameable, since a line the reader has to decode is worse than no line.
- Decide-and-record whether the same line belongs on the **digest** surface, which runs through the same `engine.complete_text` and therefore carries the same substitution. Likely yes and cheap; if no, the reason lands in a comment at the digest render site.

## Explicitly not in scope

Changing the substitution behaviour itself (falling back to local is correct; PIPE12's spec settled that). Adding an Apple Intelligence Q&A path. Changing `effective_backend` or the auto ladder. Any new backend. Re-opening PIPE12's temperature or adapter legs, which are done.

## Acceptance

Daemon tests: `AskAnswer` round-trips `substituted_from` present and absent (an older answer file without the key still decodes); the footer derivation is pure and table-tested (substitution present yields the two-engine phrase, absent yields today's single-engine phrase, an unnameable engine on either side yields nil); the phrase names both engines and contains no raw config id (`apple_intelligence` must not reach the screen, the same rule that made `claude_cli` a UX31 bug).

`cd daemon && swift build` and `swift test` green, with the number of tests this task adds recorded in the same commit. Repo dash guard green.

Owner eyeball: set the backend to Apple Intelligence, ask a question in the Library's Ask rail, and the footer says the local model answered *and* that Apple Intelligence has no Q&A path, without naming a config id.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Every task gated on an owner action carries one (2026-07-30 rule).

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then confirm `swift test` is green.
2. [owner] Preferences, Pipeline, set the summarization backend to Apple Intelligence.
3. [owner] Open the Library, switch to the Ask rail, ask any question about a past meeting.
4. [owner] Read the footer under the answer. It should name the engine that actually ran and say Apple Intelligence has no question-and-answer path. It must not contain `apple_intelligence`, `mlx`, or any other config id.
5. [owner] Set the backend back to whatever you normally run, ask again, and confirm the footer returns to the plain one-engine line with no substitution clause.
6. [owner] If the digest leg shipped, run a digest under Apple Intelligence and confirm the same line; if it was recorded as out of scope, read the comment at the digest render site and confirm you agree with the reason.
7. [owner] Say "UX64 good to close". That moves the row and this spec into `q6-final.md`. Nothing is owed on the engineering side before then.

**[DONE] UX63 (P2): The weekly-digest toggle says "on-device (no new egress)"; the scheduled run posts to Anthropic.** Shipped 2026-08-16.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. Medium, CONFIRMED by an independent skeptic that found no guard, default, second path or test that rescues the string.

## What is wrong

The Preferences toggle that installs the weekly-digest LaunchAgent describes the digest as running on-device, while the shipped digest narrates through `engine.complete_text` under `effective_backend()`.

- `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Preferences/PreferencesView+Pipeline.swift:236` is the sole footer of `SettingsGroup("Weekly digest")`: `Text("The digest summarizes your open actions and recent decisions across the whole library, on-device (no new egress). Generate one on demand from the Library's Digests view.")`. It is unconditional, not behind a flag, and it is the only copy at the point the schedule is switched on.
- `pipeline/src/mp/digest.py:23` makes the module's own claim in the correct, qualified form: "No new always-on egress: this is a command you run or schedule", and `:16-18` says narration "honours `effective_backend()` and the egress guard clamps it under regulated / NDA".
- `README.md:535` uses the same qualified form: "It is latency-tolerant and adds no always-on egress".

The Preferences string drops the qualification, and the parenthetical "(no new egress)" reads as a guarantee about the network rather than about scheduling.

Observed, not theorized: the owner's unattended run on **2026-08-03** produced `digest.err.log:1` = `INFO httpx: HTTP Request: POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"`, with `digest.out.log:2` confirming "narrative via anthropic". So a launchd job posts a slice of the library's open actions and decisions to Anthropic every Monday at 09:00 with no UI in front of it, having been switched on by a control that said on-device.

## A second-order note, deliberately not folded in

`pipeline/src/mp/digest.py:434` is `cfg = entry.prepare()  # SEC13: arm, then secrets. Library-wide, so no meeting anchor.` The guard therefore arms only on a globally regulated config and never on a per-meeting NDA flag, so facts drawn from an NDA workflow's summaries ride the same call. That is **AUTO3's leg 0** ("which stems may leave this machine"), which is already filed and already names this exact shape. Report it there, do not duplicate it here.

## Scope

Rewrite the footer to say what the code does: facts are gathered on-device, and the narrative goes to whichever engine `summarization.backend` selects. Name the current engine inline the way `SummarizationEngine` already does elsewhere, so the string cannot go stale when the backend changes.

If the intent was genuinely zero-egress, the alternative is to pin the digest's narration to the local engine regardless of the global backend. That is a behaviour change and needs the owner's call, so the pickup asks rather than assumes.

## Acceptance

Suite green with new tests. The footer names the engine that will actually run, and a test pins that the string and the resolved backend cannot drift apart. If the owner chooses the behaviour change instead, the digest narrates locally and a test pins it.

## Owner walkthrough

Steps tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.
