3. **Fixed properly, on all four surfaces.** `daemon/scripts/cal3-teams-title-probe.swift` now emits `"expected": "unknown"` for every captured row instead of a hardcoded `"recognize"` it never computed, and `WindowRecognizerFixtureTests` **reports** an `unknown` row (`[fixture] UNCLASSIFIED recognizer=... titles=...`) instead of asserting it, so a real Teams title this recognizer rejects arrives as a DET-band finding rather than as a red suite on an unrelated commit. A token that is neither `recognize`, `reject` nor `unknown` now fails the suite rather than quietly reading as `reject`, since a typo satisfying the negative case is the same defect one level down. Both new branches were proven by mutating the fixture and watching the suite go red and print, not by inspection. `RowExpectation` is a small pure type with its own test, because the committed fixture holds no `unknown` row today and a suite exercising only the seeded rows would pass with the branch deleted. The secondary state-name defect is corrected on every surface that stated it: only `in_call_one_on_one` has a seeded row to replace, while `in_meeting_named_series` and `in_meeting_ad_hoc` are additions, and the probe's paste note, VALOWN1 step 1, the spike doc's follow-up list and the fixture's `_README` now all say so. VALOWN1's acceptance also gained "no row left `unknown`", since an unclassified row is a decision nobody has made rather than a result. The generalisation went to `daemon/docs/gotchas.md` with one rule line in `daemon/CLAUDE.md`.
4. **Half the named scope was gone, and the two remaining were re-resolved.** UX43 and UX46 are done and archived in this file; their citations are pre-fix history in a frozen record, no session executes them, and re-resolving them by symbol would rewrite the record without a reader, so they were deliberately left. UX45 (shipped, in `owner-verification.md`, so still read) and AUTO3 (live) were re-resolved: `WorkflowsView.sinksSection`, `Workflow.effectiveSinks` with its `flags.ndaMode ? [.filesystem] : sinks` snippet, `WorkflowSink` (three cases at filing, four since UX45 shipped, and the spec now says so), the OpenAI branch in `PreferencesView+Pipeline.swift`, and `ask.main` / `digest.main` for the anchorless `entry.prepare()` (cited as `ask.py:159` and `digest.py:434`, actually at 268 and 476). AUTO3's own four links were also one directory level too shallow and dead; they are fixed. The cite-by-symbol rule is recorded in `.claude/commands/file-task.md` beside the absolute-total rule, as this item asked.
5. **The sweep was more than twice the filed size, and the mechanism is wider than the back-link.** Measured on 2026-08-18: **47** dead back-links against **4** correct ones, not the 20 against 1 recorded at filing. The same inherited-from-`tasks/` depth error had also killed **41** other links in the same file (15 to `TranscriptTab.swift` alone, plus `MeetingCast.swift`, `markdown.py`, `PRODUCT.md`, `GUIDE.md` and others), for **88** dead links in one archive. All 88 are swept, by a rule that rewrites a link only when it is dead now **and** resolves after removing exactly one `../` level, so no correct link could be touched. `q5-final.md` has zero dead relative links and `q4-final.md`'s three are deleted source files rather than depth errors, which confirms the defect entered with the per-task-file split. The source fix is one bullet in `.claude/commands/tech-task.md` step 8's done-done branch stating the **general** rule, that every relative link in a moved body loses one `../` level, of which the back-link is one case; writing only the back-link rule would have left the next archival re-adding a dead `../../../daemon/...` instead. The optional fence was deliberately **not** built: the procedure note is what this item called the minimum, the eight sessions archiving tasks in the same batch all read `tech-task.md`, and a new CI check that false-positives on a quoted pattern would have cost more than it caught.

**Left as findings rather than absorbed**, since each is a different mechanism from the one this task swept, and named here so they are not lost. Fourteen dead relative links remain in four live specs, all the same one-level depth error: `AUTO1.md` (2), `CAL3.md` (7), `DIAR5.md` (1), `DOC13.md` (4). Ten links in this file point at `tasks/<ID>.md` files that were deleted when those tasks were archived (UX44, UX49, UX52, UX57, UX58, UX71, AI12, LANG2, LOCAL15), which is a third mechanism: an archival kills every citation of the spec it moves. And `q4-final.md` carries three links to source files that no longer exist. None of these were touched, both to stay in scope and because two of those files were being edited by parallel sessions on the same day.

## 1. DIAR2 and DIAR3 tell the owner to watch for a `THEM-*` chip on the surface that renders `Unknown A`

**Fixed in place on 2026-08-03 rather than left for this task, because DIAR2 is P1 and the owner is running its sweep now.** Recorded here as the trail.

`docs/backlog/tasks/DIAR3.md:74` step 6 says "read the cast strip above the transcript ... an over-split shows an extra unnamed `THEM-*` chip". `docs/backlog/tasks/DIAR2.md:37` uses the same wording, and `:30` step 4's over-split trigger depends on it.

The cast strip does not render `THEM-*`. `VoiceResolutionBar.swift` renders `Text(voice.displayName)`, and `VoiceResolution.swift` states `displayName` "is what the transcript shows", mapped through `TranscriptDisplay.displayName`, which in `TranscriptTab.swift` turns `THEM-A` into `Unknown A`.

This is the FEAT11 defect shape exactly (FEAT11 step 3 told the owner to click a `THEM-*` chip when the UI renders `Unknown A/B/C`), recurring in two more specs. The audit's own skeptic initially refuted this finding by proving `THEM-*` **does** render in the summary, which is true and is why the summary is a valid place to see cluster labels. The owner corrected it on 2026-08-03: `THEM-*` appears only in the summary view, never in the transcript view or the cast strip, and DIAR3 step 6 names the cast strip. Recorded because the near-miss is instructive: a refutation that proves a string exists **somewhere** does not answer whether it exists on the surface the step points at.

## 2. UX48's step 7 and its acceptance pre-register an observation the scoped fix cannot produce

**Closed by UX48 on 2026-08-04, before this task was picked up.** The finding held and was filed independently by that pickup; both halves of the fix this item proposed were taken. Verified 2026-08-18: the acceptance clause reads "Cmd+K still opens Quick Find with keyboard focus (the regression check)", the strike is recorded beside it, step 7 asks for Cmd+K in the open dropdown and explains why the old wording was unproducible, and the `Find` submenu carrying `Quick Find...` shipped so Cmd+K now works from any MeetingPipe window. The one thing still untrue in the archived body, that the two delivery options were "left to the owner", was corrected in the same commit as this archival.

As filed: `docs/backlog/tasks/UX48.md:66` step 7 read "with another app frontmost and **no menu open**, press **Cmd+K**. Pass: Quick Find appears with keyboard focus". `:33` asserted the same as acceptance, so it was not a walkthrough slip.

It cannot pass, for two independent reasons:

- With another app frontmost, macOS delivers the command-key equivalent to that app. UX48's scope installs a main menu only while MeetingPipe is `.regular`, and with the Library closed it is `.accessory` with no main menu at all.
- The scope's enumerated menu contents were the App menu (Preferences), an Edit menu, and a Window menu (Minimize, Close). **No Quick Find item.** So even frontmost-and-`.regular`, nothing in the main menu matched Cmd+K.

The risk was concrete and named in the spec's own "not in scope": a session chasing the stated acceptance adds a Carbon global hotkey via `HotkeyManager`, which UX48 explicitly forbids ("Do not add per-shortcut view-hierarchy handlers. That is the approach `292dfe49` took and it is the thing this task exists to stop repeating"). It was also a near-verbatim re-run of UX39's step 5, whose premise was refuted in writing on 2026-07-31.

## 3. VALOWN1 tells the owner to paste probe output into a suite that hard-asserts the value the probe hardcodes

`daemon/scripts/cal3-teams-title-probe.swift` emitted `"expected": "recognize"` as a string literal for every capture, in `emitFixtureBlock`, without ever calling `MeetingSourceScanner.isActiveMeetingWindow` to check whether that is true.

`daemon/Tests/MeetingPipeTests/WindowRecognizerFixtureTests.swift` read it as `let expected = (entry.expected == "recognize")` and then `XCTAssertEqual(recognized, expected, ...)`, a hard assertion rather than a report.

`docs/backlog/tasks/VALOWN1.md` step 1 instructed, "**whatever the verdict says**", that "the emitted fixture block replaces the seeded Teams entries ... with `seeded: false`".

So if any real captured Teams title is one the recognizer rejects, which is plausible **precisely because CAL3 exists on the finding that real Teams titles do not match this repo's guessed formats**, the paste turns weeks of owner capture into a red suite on an unrelated commit. VALOWN1's own acceptance ("the fixture test reports a non-zero captured count") would be satisfied while the suite is failing.

Secondary: `fixtureState(for:)` emits states `in_meeting_named_series` and `in_meeting_ad_hoc`, neither of which exists in the fixture's 21 entries, so "REPLACING the seeded rows" has nothing to replace for those and the paste grows the fixture rather than converting it.

**Shipped fix.** The probe emits `unknown`, which is the second of the two options this item offered, and it is the right one rather than the cheap one: the probe's own header records that it carries no Teams title pattern **on purpose**, and it is not linked against the app target, so computing `expected` would mean duplicating the recognizer into a script whose entire premise is that it holds no such knowledge. The suite gained a `RowExpectation` type reading exactly three tokens, reports `unknown`, asserts `recognize` and `reject`, and fails anything else. Both new branches were verified against a deliberately mutated fixture. `in_call_one_on_one` is the only emitted state with a seeded row to replace, and that is now stated by the probe's paste note, the fixture's `_README`, the spike doc and VALOWN1. A `reject` on a real captured title is named as a DET-band finding in all four places. The generalisation is in `daemon/docs/gotchas.md` under "A capture tool must not emit a verdict it never computed", with one rule line in `daemon/CLAUDE.md`.

## 4. Four active specs anchor on `file:line` ranges that now land on unrelated code

UX43, UX45, UX46 and AUTO3 each cite the exact line of the code they exist to change, and in every case the cited line now holds something else, in three of the four by 40 to 200 lines, after LOCAL16, UX35 and AI11 shifted those files.

**Two of the four had shipped and been archived by 2026-08-18**, so the live scope was UX45 and AUTO3. See the shipped note above for what each citation resolved to. The durable half is the rule, now in `.claude/commands/file-task.md`: cite a symbol plus a short quoted snippet, never a bare line number, because a line number is true against exactly one commit and rots the same way an absolute suite total does, and a reader cannot tell a stale citation from a wrong one.

## 5. Every archived spec's link back to the active backlog is broken, and each new archival copies it

Added 2026-08-03, found by SEC15's pickup read and re-verified after the nine-task band landed.

`docs/backlog/q6-final.md` carried its links back to the active backlog with a `../` prefix where a `./` one was needed: **20** of them at filing, **47** by 2026-08-18, against 1 and then 4 spelled correctly. The archive is a sibling of the active backlog, both directly under `docs/backlog/`, so the `../` form resolves to `docs/meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md`, which does not exist. Every one of those was dead in a Markdown viewer and in any link checker.

The mis-spelling is inherited, not invented per task. An archived spec is the task's `tasks/<ID>.md` body moved up one directory, and from `tasks/` the `../` form is **correct**; nothing in the move rewrites it. That is why the count grows on its own. `q4-final.md` and `q5-final.md` are clean, so the defect entered with the per-task-file split, and the correctly spelled links in `q6-final.md` show the right form was known.

**What execution added to the diagnosis:** the back-link is one case of a general rule, not a special one. Every relative link in a moved body is one level too deep, and 41 further links in the same file were dead for exactly that reason, giving 88 in total. The sweep therefore rewrote any link that was dead **and** resolved one level shallower, which is precise enough that no correct link could be caught by it, and the procedure note in `tech-task.md` states the general rule rather than the back-link special case.

Why it belongs in this row rather than DOC12's: the reader is a session opening an archived spec to learn how something shipped, which is this task's stated audience, not a human reading product documentation.

## Scope

Items 2, 3, 4 and 5. Item 1 is already fixed and is recorded here for the trail.

## Acceptance

UX48's step 7 and acceptance clause describe something the scope can deliver. The CAL3 probe cannot emit an `expected` it did not compute, and VALOWN1's paste step says what to do with a `reject`. The four stale citations resolve. `.claude/commands/file-task.md` records the cite-by-symbol rule. `docs/backlog/q6-final.md` has zero dead back-links to the active backlog, and the archival step in `.claude/commands/tech-task.md` says to rewrite the path on the way up, so the count cannot regrow. No code behaviour change beyond the probe, so both suites stay green.

**The filed acceptance named "21" correct back-links, from the 20-against-1 counts at filing. The measured numbers on execution day were 47 against 4, so the shipped bar is zero dead and 51 correct**, which is the same bar with the arithmetic redone rather than a different one. This is the drift that the acceptance rule about absolute totals exists to prevent, appearing in a task about drift.

## Why this is its own row rather than fixed in passing

The 2026-07-31 owner-owed pass established that documentation asserting behaviour the code does not have is this repo's dominant defect class, because sessions steer by these documents and the owner is walked through them. Each item below is small; the class is not.

## The list

**1. The TCC invariant describes signing the app stopped doing.** CONFIRMED by an independent skeptic. `ARCHITECTURE.md:469` says `install.sh` and `rebuild.sh` "codesign adhoc with a stable `--identifier`" and therefore "Screen Recording requires one toggle after rebuild". `scripts/install.sh:368-370` runs `ensure_dev_cert` on every install, and `scripts/lib/dev-cert.sh:32-38` makes ad-hoc the third and last choice. `README.md:162` and `:629` assert the opposite of ARCHITECTURE, correctly: the self-signed "MeetingPipe Dev" identity gives an identity-based designated requirement that does not pin the cdhash, so the grant survives. Two live docs give opposite answers to the same question, and whichever the reader opens first decides whether a real signing regression looks like a bug or expected behaviour. Fix: rewrite `:469` to describe the dev-cert default with ad-hoc as the fallback, and point the invariant at `scripts/lib/dev-cert.sh`.

**2. `--context-tokens` is documented as RAM-clamped without its backend condition.** `README.md:500` says it "is clamped to what your Mac's RAM can answer with", and `mp ask`'s own help text says the same. `ask.context_ceiling` returns `None` for any backend outside `ON_DEVICE_BACKENDS`, so on the shipped default (`anthropic`) an arbitrary value passes through unclamped. This is the same shape as the AI11 step 6 walkthrough failure, which is already recorded: the clamp is on-device-only by design and pinned by a test, and the documentation states it unconditionally. Fix: add the condition. Note AI12 is building a UI control over this budget and should not inherit the wrong mental model.

**3. README's workflow definition claims per-workflow Obsidian vault routing.** `README.md:318` lists "which Obsidian vault" among the per-context routing rules a workflow carries. `WorkflowSink.obsidian` has no associated value, `<stem>.meta.json` carries no vault key, and `mp.workflow.apply_overrides` never touches `obsidian.vault_path`. The vault is global-only. Note UX45 is already filed to add publish-target configuration in-app, so this line may become true; until it does, it is false. Fix: correct the sentence, and cross-reference UX45.

**4. ARCHITECTURE's Key invariants point at `Coordinator` for two things that moved.** `ARCHITECTURE.md:464` says "every transition lives in `Coordinator`" (they live in `Coordination/DetectionStateMachine.swift`), and the following bullet names `Coordinator.processingJobs` as the job queue (it is a private property of `Coordination/SinkDispatcher.swift`). Fix: repoint both.

**5. The Permissions pane's privacy callout understates the app's network reach.** `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Preferences/PreferencesView+Permissions.swift:74` enumerates egress as Anthropic for summarization plus Notion for publishing. The app now also ships the Claude CLI, OpenAI, Obsidian, filesystem and LAN paths. Fix: state the reach in terms of the configured backend and sinks rather than naming two vendors, so it cannot go stale again.

**6. The prompt panel's BYO tooltip names Anthropic unconditionally.** `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingPromptWindow.swift:523` reads "Record, but skip the Anthropic API call. You'll summarize the transcript yourself." That is wrong whenever the resolved backend is local, `claude_cli`, `openai` or `apple_intelligence`. Fix: name the resolved engine, or say "the summarization step" without a vendor.

**7. `docs/SETUP.md` and the installer disagree on the model download size.** `docs/SETUP.md:13` says the speech models are about 475 MB; `install.sh` prints ~630 MB for the same download at the same moment. Fix: make one the source of truth. SETUP.md is the clean-Mac walkthrough, so the installer's figure should win and SETUP should quote it.

**8. README sends the owner to hand-edit a threshold that has a slider.** `README.md:251` says to edit `summarization.skip_above_chars` in `config.toml`; Preferences has shipped a slider over the same value with an explanatory footer. Fix: point at the slider, keep the config key as the secondary route.

**9. The Accessibility rationale diverges between two copies.** `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Preferences/PreferencesView+Permissions.swift:204` returns "Reads browser tab titles to detect Meet and Teams Web sessions", a second diverged copy of `PermissionsCenter.Kind.rationale`. It names a path the owner has never used, while every other surface names native end-detection. Fix: delete the duplicate and read the one rationale. Note DET11 is correcting what those surfaces should *say*; this item is about there being two copies, so land DET11's wording and have this one converge on it.

**10. The `fgFaint` contrast floor, one instance.** `daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingDetailView+Header.swift:101` and `:104` render the "Summary edited locally" glyph and caption in `MPColors.fgFaint` at the smallest type step, while the caption twenty lines below explicitly moved off `fgFaint` because it sits near 2.8:1 against a 4.5:1 floor. Fix: use `fgSubtle`, which clears the floor.

**11. ARCHITECTURE credits the retrieval stack to a consumer that does not import it.** Added 2026-08-03, found by SEC15's pickup read while fencing `rag.py` and re-verified after the nine-task band landed. `ARCHITECTURE.md:395` closes its `embed_index.py` / `rag.py` paragraph with "Both back `ask.py` and `digest.py`". Only the first half is true: `ask.py:36` is `from . import embed_index, engine, entry, events, rag, resource_guard`, while `digest.py` imports neither, and its actual inputs are `actions`, `engine`, `entry`, `events`, `config`, `schemas`, `markdown`, and `prompt_safety`. `mp digest` reads `<stem>.summary.json` and narrates it; it does no retrieval at all. The two other real consumers go unnamed by that sentence: `rag.py:23` itself imports `Chunk` from `embed_index`, and `action_clusters.py:96` pulls `default_embedder` (the paragraph does credit `action_clusters.py` as "the third consumer of that embedder" two sentences later, which is what makes the earlier claim look deliberate rather than loose). Consequence is the ordinary one for this class: a session asked to change retrieval reads this line and goes looking for a digest call path that has never existed. Fix: say both back `ask.py`, and name `rag.py` and `action_clusters.py` as `embed_index`'s other readers. Cheap cross-check for whoever picks this up, since the sentence is about imports: `grep -rnE "^(from|import).*(embed_index|rag)" pipeline/src/mp/*.py`.

## Scope

Fix all eleven. They are independent one-liners to one-paragraph edits, and none needs a decision except item 3's cross-reference to UX45 and item 9's ordering against DET11.

## Acceptance

Every item above corrected. `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` still clean. Where a string is derivable from code (items 5, 6, 9), prefer deriving it over restating it, so the class stops recurring. No behaviour change, so both suites stay green with no new tests except where a derived string gains one.

**[DONE] ARCH6 (P3): dead seams, an unwired presentation model, and knobs that outlived their controls.** Shipped 2026-08-18, all five items. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close; what actually shipped, and the two findings it did not name, are in the ToC row above.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. P3. Distinct from ARCH5, which is the duplication and extraction band; this is code that exists and is not reached.

## 1. `StatusBarModel`'s four decision functions have zero production callers

`StatusBarModel.derive` (`daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/StatusBarModel.swift:121`), `title` (`:137`), `icon(for:)` (`:187`) and `rows` (`:207`) are called from nowhere in `daemon/Sources`. The shipped menu bar composes its own title (`StatusBarController.swift:265-276`), picks its own icon (`:138`, `:149`, `:164`, `:181`, `:200`) and builds its own conditional row set and order in `populateMenu` (`:427-611`), while 19 of the 31 `StatusBarModelTests` methods pin a parallel copy of those three decisions.

The divergence has already begun. `StatusBarController.swift:503` adds a `finishSetup` row that `StatusBarModel.Row` (`:26-46`) has no case for, so the tested row list already disagrees with the shipped menu. `StatusBarController.swift:391`'s `hasPendingPermissionIssue()` has no call site and has sat dead since the extraction.

`docs/backlog/q6-final.md:76` records T3 as having lifted these out of the controller. That claim is false and should be corrected in the archive.

The skeptic's narrowing, recorded: the **rest** of the type is genuinely load-bearing. Seven entry points are read by production (`StatusBarController.swift:268, 393, 404, 488, 519, 635, 693` and `Coordinator+MenuActions.swift:226`), five of them repointed by T3 itself, so "never repointed the controller at it" is false as a blanket statement. Only the four decision functions are orphaned.

Fix: repoint `applyTitle` at `StatusBarModel.title`, the icon at `StatusBarModel.icon`, and have `populateMenu` build its conditional items by switching over `StatusBarModel.rows` with a `finishSetup` case added, so `NSMenuItem` construction stays in the controller while presence and ordering live in one place. Delete the dead private method. Correct the T3 archive row. Green-to-green: the two title implementations agree today, so no user-visible string changes.

## 2. `PrepCardProviding` is an injection seam nothing injects

`daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/PrepCard.swift:115` declares the protocol with the stated purpose at `:113` of keeping the prompt panel from learning where its data comes from. There is exactly one conformer, exactly one injection site that always passes it, and no test ever supplies a fake, so it buys neither testability nor substitution.

Fix: either use it (give the panel tests a fake provider, which is the cheap win if the panel has untested branches) or collapse it. Do not leave it as a seam that documents an intent nothing exercises.

## 3. Two `UISettings` knobs kept their plumbing after DSN1 cut their controls

`menuBarIconStyle` (`daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/Preferences/UISettings.swift:25`) and `showRegulatedBadge` have no writer anywhere in the app, so both are permanently pinned at their init defaults. The icon-style branches, its Combine subscription and the badge subscription are all unreachable.

The CI5 truth fence cannot see this: it compares config-key sets and event-category sets, and these are `UISettings` properties rather than `config.toml` keys. That fence gap is worth recording in the fence's own documentation so the next reader does not over-trust it.

Fix: remove the dead plumbing, or restore the controls if either is wanted. Note `showRegulatedBadge` is read by the title logic in item 1, so land these together.

## 4. Two documented parameters that no caller ever exercises

`MeetingSourceScanner.scan(keepStickyOnEmpty:)` documents a `true` mode for when the owner is mid-recording ("a transient empty scan must not unbias the next pass", `MeetingSourceScanner.swift:51`), and the single production caller hardcodes `false`, so the documented mid-recording protection does not exist. Decide whether it should, since DET9 is touching adjacent liveness logic, then either wire it or delete the parameter and its comment.

`PromptEndPolicy`'s uncorroborated-leave-button filter has been unreachable since START1: no reachable `EndingReason` can carry `leadingSignal == ax_leave_button_invalid` with an empty `confirmedBy`, so `clearsPromptState` always returns true. Its own doc and `DetectionStateMachine`'s describe it as a live guard. Delete it or make it reachable, and fix both comments.

## 5. `PromotionEngine`'s corroboration doc names a corroborator its own rule forbids

`daemon/Sources/MeetingPipeCore/Lifecycle/PromotionEngine.swift:32-34` says a lone uncorroborated invalid is held "until a reliable signal (window-gone) corroborates", but `tick()` requires a **cross-class** corroborator and `axLeaveButton` and `shareableContentWindow` are the same class, so for a native meeting no corroborator can ever exist and that debounce path can never fire. Fix the comment, or fix the rule if the comment describes the intent.

## Scope

All five. Each is small and independent. Items 1 and 3 interact through `showRegulatedBadge`; items 4 and 5 are both detection comments and should land with or after DET9 so the wording is settled once.

## Acceptance

Suite green. No user-visible behaviour change anywhere except where item 4's `keepStickyOnEmpty` decision goes toward wiring it, which needs its own test. The `q6-final.md:76` T3 claim is corrected. The CI5 fence's documentation records what it structurally cannot see.

**[DONE] CI6 (P3): tests and tooling that cannot fail, and one that has never run.** Shipped 2026-08-18. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close, with the acceptance's own internal contradiction noted where it sits and a progress section appended when it landed; item 2's floor was decided by the owner on 2026-08-18 and that decision is recorded in both.

Filed 2026-08-03 by the audit band. P3. From the angle that actually executed both suites on 2026-08-03: 1980 Swift and 1157 Python green, ruff and pyright clean, truth fences clean, both gate scripts pass. Coverage context only, not a finding: daemon 35.07% line / 43.56% region, pipeline 87% statement.

## 1. `scripts/coverage.sh` has never printed its Swift headline and exits 1

`scripts/coverage.sh:87` puts backslash-escaped quotes inside an f-string expression, which is a SyntaxError on every Python version. Verified 2026-08-03 by reading the raw bytes and reproducing the snippet standalone on Python 3.14.2 (exit 1), and by a scratch harness with the identical `set -euo pipefail` + function + `case` structure. Born in `f78ca057` on 2026-07-20 and never touched. `./scripts/coverage.sh swift` and `both` have always exited 1.

Narrower than it sounds, and recorded as such: no coverage number is lost. The per-module llvm-cov table at `:72-75` prints normally before the crash, and `:77-78` says the dead line only restates a number already in that table, so T3's acceptance ("prints per-module numbers for both trees") is genuinely satisfied. Fix is one line.

## 2. The window-title regression fence pins zero real captures and its progress test cannot fail

`daemon/Tests/MeetingPipeTests/WindowRecognizerFixtureTests.swift:10` states the fixture "is the ground truth from running apps". All 21 entries carry `"seeded": true` and none carries `false`, so no row was ever captured from a running app. The suite printed `[fixture] window_titles.json: 0/21 captured, 21 still seeded` on the 2026-08-03 run.

`WindowRecognizerFixtureTests.swift:72-75` is explicit that the progress test always passes: its only assertion is `XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(total, 1)`, which the sibling test already guarantees.

So a Teams window-title change that the seeded guesses happen to model, but the real titles do not, degrades end-detection while all 21 rows stay green, and the one test that would tell a reader the fence is unbacked is written never to speak.

Fix: turn `test_fixture_capture_progress_is_logged` into an assertion with a pre-registered floor that fails while the captured count is zero, and soften the class docstring so it stops asserting ground truth the fixture does not have. Capturing real titles is VALOWN1's job and is owner-gated; note that HYG6 item 3 is fixing the paste path that would otherwise turn that capture into a red suite, so land HYG6 first.

## 3. The SEC13 entry-contract tripwire is a substring test

`pipeline/tests/test_entry_contract.py:62` is `if "entry.prepare" not in src:`, a raw substring test over module text. A mention in a docstring or a comment satisfies it, there is no AST check that a call node exists, and it asserts nothing about `prepare` running **before** the sink, engine or token work it is supposed to gate, which is the entire point of the contract.

Fix: parse the module and assert a real call node, and assert its position relative to the first client construction. LOCAL19 is adding a sibling constructor walk and should use the strengthened shape rather than copying this one.

## 4. `MeetingStore` can pick the wrong per-stem JSON as the transcript

`daemon/Sources/MeetingPipe/MeetingStore.swift:535-537` selects `files.first` matching `.json` with eight suffix exclusions, and the exclusions do not cover `.embeddings.json`, `.filesystem.json` or `.speaker_labels.json`. On a real meeting directory `files.first` can therefore return a sidecar carrying no `audio_seconds`, and the audio-less duration recovery silently yields nil.

Measured caveat, recorded: there are currently **0** audio-less stems that also carry an embeddings sidecar (4 audio-less out of 245, all predating the embeddings feature), so this is latent rather than active, and readdir order is not guaranteed. The test that pins the duration fallback cannot catch it because it builds a directory with only the files it expects.

Fix: exclude the three suffixes, and build the fallback test's directory from the real sidecar inventory rather than from a hand-listed subset.

## 5. `orchestrate._configure_logging` touches the production log path above its own guard

`pipeline/src/mp/orchestrate.py:109-112` does its `mkdir` and `touch` of `~/Library/Logs/MeetingPipe/pipeline.log` above the `if root.handlers: return` guard at `:117`, so a pytest run bumps the real file's mtime, and on a fresh checkout or a CI runner it creates the directory plus an empty `pipeline.log` under the process umask rather than the 0600 SEC14 shipped for that file.

Downgraded to low by a skeptic and recorded as such: **zero bytes are written**, no rotation runs and no generation is dropped, because pytest holds root handlers so the guard fires before the FileHandler. The mode divergence self-heals at the next daemon launch. Also note the claim that "every writer must honour `MEETINGPIPE_LOGS_DIR`" is not what the docs say: `pipeline/src/mp/events.py:8` explicitly carves the text logs out ("The text logs ... stay as-is for tail-based debugging; this module is for grep-based postmortem"). So this is a four-line tidy, not a contract violation.

Fix: move the two lines below the guard.

## Scope

All five. Each is independent and small.

## Acceptance

`./scripts/coverage.sh both` exits 0 and prints both headlines. The fixture progress test fails while the captured count is zero. The entry-contract test asserts a call node and its ordering, and fails against a module that only mentions `entry.prepare` in a comment. The transcript selector excludes the three suffixes and its test builds from the real inventory. A pytest run does not touch `~/Library/Logs/MeetingPipe`. Both suites green.

**Two clauses above cannot both hold, and that was item 2's whole remainder.** "The fixture progress test fails while the captured count is zero" and "Both suites green" are the same sentence read two ways: the captured count is zero, raising it is VALOWN1, and VALOWN1 is owner-gated at P4 and needs five real Teams meetings. So a floor written to fail leaves `swift test` red on `main` from the commit until the owner runs it, which is not a bounded window. **Resolved by the owner on 2026-08-18**, in favour of the skip; the section below records both the reasoning and the mechanism that arms the floor without anyone remembering to.

## Shipped 2026-08-18, all five, with item 2's floor decided by the owner

Verification actually run, not inferred: `./scripts/coverage.sh both` exit **0** (it exited 1 before), pipeline `TOTAL 8262 1010 88%` and 1243 passed, daemon `LINE COVERAGE: 21712/58261 = 37.3%` and 2587 tests with 1 skipped and 0 failures, `ruff` clean, `pyright` 0 errors, `truth_fences.py both` all three fences OK.

**1. Fixed and measured.** The line binds `covered, count, percent` before formatting them. The escape cannot be avoided in place: the program is a single-quoted shell word, so a nested `"` has to be backslashed, and a backslash inside an f-string expression is a SyntaxError. Reproduced standalone first (exit 1, "unexpected character after line continuation character", Python 3.14.2), then the fix run against the same canned payload, then the real script end to end.

**3. Fixed, and mutation-proved on a real module.** `_entry_contract_violations(source, label)` is a pure function over module text, so the checker's own tests drive it with modules written to break each half. It reports two things: no `entry.prepare(...)` **call node** (a docstring, a comment or a `# TODO` no longer counts), and any `*Client` / `*Publisher` / `load_secrets` call above the arm inside the arming function. Both were then driven against `publish_cmd.py` itself: demote its arm to a comment and the checker says "no entry.prepare(...) call node" where the old substring test passed; move a publisher above the arm and it names the ordering violation. The ordering half is vacuous against today's tree, since all fifteen arming functions construct nothing above the arm, which is what a tripwire looks like before it fires and is a different thing from the assertion that *cannot* fire that this task filed against. `test_the_gate_predicate_still_names_the_real_client_surface` pins that the naming convention the gate reads still describes the real client surface, so a rename cannot empty it silently.

**4. Fixed wider than filed, deliberately.** The selector is `lastPathComponent == "<stem>.json"`, not three more exclusions. Two reasons. The inventory in `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s on-disk table plus `CONVENTIONS.md`'s publish receipts holds **thirteen** per-stem JSON sidecars the deny-list missed, not the three this spec named (`.recordfail`, `.recovery`, `.mute-timeline`, `.markers`, `.diarize_cleanup`, `.transcript_corrections`, `.obsidian`, `.lan`, `.apple_pending`, `.correction` on top of the filed three). And this spec's own second clause forces it: a test that builds the directory from the real inventory fails against any deny-list, so the choice was a list that has to be re-completed on every new sidecar or a match that cannot fall behind. Both writers agree the transcript is `<stem>.json` (`orchestrate._finalize_streamed_transcript`, and the daemon's FluidAudio draft), and the scan already groups by the same stem. The new test writes all 21 inventory sidecars plus the transcript and was proved red against the old selector: `nil` against `Optional(1830.5)`.

**5. Fixed, both halves tested.** The mkdir and touch moved below the guard. The negative test (a caller already owns the root logger, so nothing under `~/Library/Logs/MeetingPipe` is created) was proved red against the pre-fix tree; the positive one pins the promise the two lines exist for, that a real run still gets `pipeline.log` on disk before anything is logged.

**2. Shipped in two halves, the second of them decided by the owner rather than by the session.** The class docstring no longer calls the fixture "the ground truth from running apps"; it says what the file is (21 seeded guesses), names the failure mode that leaves, and points at VALOWN1. That half was never in question.

The floor is where the spec argued with itself. `test_fixture_capture_progress_is_logged` becomes `test_fixture_is_backed_by_real_captures`, which **skips** while the captured count is below one, with a message naming the probe and the paste that clears it. A skip is XCTest's own word for "not verified", it is counted in the run summary (`1 test skipped`) rather than buried in output the way the old `print` was, and the floor below it arms itself the moment a `seeded: false` row lands, so nothing has to be remembered. The `[fixture] 0/21 captured` print is kept, because CAL3, VALOWN1, the spike doc and the probe's own header all cite it.

**The owner chose this over the literal `XCTAssertGreaterThan(captured, 0)` on 2026-08-18**, on the reasoning that a run summary reading `1 test skipped` is the honest signal where a silent pass is not, that the floor arming itself on the first real capture costs nobody any vigilance, and that nothing should go red on `main` while VALOWN1 sits unrun at P4 with no bounded window. The case for the hard form was put alongside it and declined: a skip is easier to ignore than a failure, and a fence nobody is forced to look at is how the fixture reached `0/21` in the first place. What answers that is the mechanism rather than the assertion. `docs/backlog/tasks/VALOWN1.md` now carries it in both directions, in the paste step ("the paste is also what un-skips a test") and in its acceptance ("`swift test` reports zero skipped tests"), so the day the captures land, the skip clearing is a machine-checkable part of VALOWN1 being done rather than a note somebody has to act on.

**Do not re-open this as an unfinished item.** All five are shipped; item 2's floor is deliberately a skip, and the only thing outstanding anywhere is VALOWN1's own owner-run capture, which was always its own task.

**[DONE] UX72 (P2): the local-width refusal is written about this Mac's history rather than for the person reading it.** Shipped and closed 2026-08-18. The spec text below is the filing as it stood at close, with a Progress section recording what landed, the one judgement call, and the owner's close.

Band origin: filed 2026-08-04 at the owner's request, found while walking AI12 the day it shipped: the wording "feels bounded to the context of current issues we face on the mac (going past that cap has taken this mac down before - exact sign of this boundary, which is not the case for new users..)". Status and priority live in this task's ToC row in [meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md](./meetingpipe-q6-backlog.md).

## Context

`AskContextWidth.reason` refuses a width the local backend cannot hold with a sentence containing "has taken this Mac down before." (Filed as `AskContextWidth.swift:213`; cited by symbol here per HYG6, since the line moves the first time anyone edits the file, and this one did.)

That is true, and it is why the guard exists: a wide local pack rebooted the owner's Mac on 2026-07-29 (LOCAL16). Writing the incident into the control's copy is a different thing from acting on it. The sentence reports an event in this installation's past, in the second person, to a reader who may have no such past; on a machine that has never been taken down it is not merely irrelevant but unverifiable and slightly alarming.

The rest of the width copy is the model to match, and it is good: "About 25x the text sent to Anthropic, so about 25x the cost of a normal question" and "Needs about 24 GB; this Mac has 16 GB" both state a present fact about *this* machine and *this* request, and neither reaches for history. The refusal should read the same way, saying what will not fit and why, not what happened before.

This is small and it is worth a row rather than a drive-by because the product now has two documents and a possible tutorial in flight (DOC13, FEAT15) whose whole subject is register, and a control that talks about the developer's own incident is the same category of leak as a user-facing guide linking to `../README.md`.

## Scope

Rewrite that one refusal so it states the constraint rather than the anecdote, in the register the neighbouring sublabels already use: what the request needs, what this Mac has, and what to do instead. The existing "Switch to a cloud backend in Preferences" clause is fine and should survive.

Sweep the rest of `AskContextWidth.swift`'s strings for the same shape while there, since the file is small and one pass is cheaper than a second row later.

## Explicitly not / out of scope

**Not the guard itself.** The ceiling is correct, LOCAL16 established why, and the refusal must keep refusing. This is wording only.

**Not the tier table.** Which widths are offered at which memory is AI12's decision and is unchanged.

**Not a general copy sweep.** Other surfaces are DOC12's and DOC13's; this row is `AskContextWidth.swift`.

## Acceptance

`cd daemon && swift build` clean and `swift test` green. Whether this needs a new test is a judgement call: if the copy is already pinned by an existing `AskContextWidthTests` case, updating that case is the whole change.

The string "has taken this Mac down before" appears nowhere in `daemon/Sources`. Worth a source fence given how easy it is to reintroduce from the spec history.

No em-dashes in changed lines. Repo dash guard green.

## Progress

**Shipped and closed 2026-08-18.** Every line of the Acceptance above is green, and the one thing a test could not hold, whether the new sentence reads correctly to someone whose Mac has never crashed, was settled by the owner rather than asserted here.

Verification that actually ran: `swift build` clean in 36.9s, `swift test` 2608 tests 0 failures (3 new in `AskContextWidthTests`, 20 to 23), `python3 scripts/truth_fences.py both` green on config keys, event categories and the `CLAUDE.md` budget, and zero U+2014 in either changed source file.

The four strings the control can now show, in full, so the writing can be judged without a rebuild:

- Local backend, 32 GB: "Local MLX answers on this Mac, so the width is capped at what 32 GB can hold. Switch to a cloud backend in Preferences ▸ Pipeline to read wider."
- `auto`, 32 GB: "Auto can fall back to the model on this Mac, so the width is capped at what 32 GB can hold. Switch to a cloud backend in Preferences ▸ Pipeline to read wider."
- Regulated mode, any backend: "Regulated mode keeps every answer on this Mac, so the width is capped at what 32 GB can hold." (unchanged, and already in this register)
- Unresolvable backend id: "The summarization backend in your config is not one this build knows, so the width is capped at what this Mac (32 GB) can hold." (unchanged)

**Nothing replaced the clause that was removed**, which is the judgement call worth arguing with. The model this spec names states a requirement against a capacity ("Needs about 24 GB; this Mac has 16 GB"), and there is no tokens-to-GB mapping in either tree: `LocalModelTier` maps RAM to a token ceiling and never back, so a width cannot honestly quote what it needs in memory the way a model preset can. This Mac's capacity is already in the sentence, so a replacement clause ("going past that cap would run this Mac out of memory") would restate the cap in different words, and a single sentence beating a paragraph is a voice rule here. Two clauses, two jobs: why the cap exists, and the one thing that lifts it.

**The sweep found nothing else.** The file's other five strings all state a present fact about this machine and this request. `"The summarization backend in your config is not one this build knows"` was read closely and left: "this build" leans developer-ish, but it is true, it is present tense, and it is not the history shape this row is about.

**Three tests, since no existing case pinned this sentence.** `test_the_local_reason_states_the_constraint_rather_than_this_macs_history` pins the three facts the refusal must carry (which backend answers, this Mac's memory, the way out). `test_no_reason_this_control_shows_reports_something_that_already_happened` is a tense guard across five backends, three RAM sizes and both regulated states, deliberately narrow (it bans "has taken" / "took this Mac" / "has crashed" / "used to" / "last time", not the bare word "before", so a future "before you ask" stays legal). `test_no_daemon_source_tells_the_reader_this_mac_has_been_taken_down` is the acceptance fence: it walks every `.swift` under `daemon/Sources` rather than one property, so it still holds if the copy moves types, and it reads comments too. All three were proved red by reintroducing the sentence and re-running, then reverted.

Docs: `design/README.md`'s Voice list gained the general rule, since that is where copy rules live and FEAT15 is in flight on register. `README.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` both describe this control and neither drifted (the README says the control "says why instead of quietly shrinking your request", still true; ARCHITECTURE keeps the 2026-07-29 reboot as the architectural *why*, which is a maintainer doc and the right home for it). `docs/GUIDE.md`, `docs/SETUP.md` and `CONVENTIONS.md` have no width-control copy. `daemon/CLAUDE.md` unchanged: no invariant moved, and its budget has 185 bytes of headroom.

**Closed done-done 2026-08-18 on the owner's read, not on the in-app walkthrough below.** The four strings are deterministic, so they were quoted in full and judged as text: no rebuild, under a minute, and the new sentence being shorter than the one it replaces means it cannot introduce a truncation the old one avoided. Asked what was wrong with the new wording, the owner answered about the old one ("main concern for me was this wording: 'has taken this Mac down before' for new user it is not relevant at all"), which is the original complaint restated and is exactly what the removal plus the source fence answer. The judgement call above, replacing the removed clause with nothing, was put to them explicitly and taken as-is. The walkthrough below is left as filed rather than deleted, since it is the record of what was asked for.

## Owner walkthrough (for the session that picks this up)

Per the 2026-07-30 standing rule. Steps are tagged [owner] / [session] by who acts.

1. [session] `./scripts/rebuild.sh`, then tell the owner it is ready.
2. [owner] Switch Preferences to the Local backend, open Ask, and read the refusal on the widest position. Pass: it tells you what the request needs and what this Mac has, and nothing about anything that happened before. **Set the backend back to Anthropic afterwards.**
3. [owner] Judge it as writing: would it read correctly on a Mac that had never had a problem? That is the whole test.
4. [owner] Say "UX72 good to close" (or what is wrong); [session] moves the row and the spec into `q6-final.md` and deletes this file.
